title: Bulgogi
ing: 1 1/2 lb beef ribeye, very thinly sliced
2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, for garnish
steps: In a bowl, whisk soy sauce, sugar, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, grated Asian pear, grated onion, garlic, ginger, and black pepper until sugar dissolves, about 1 minute.
Add sliced ribeye and massage to coat well. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes (up to 4 hours for deeper flavor).
Drain excess marinade well to encourage browning; reserve onions from marinade if desired.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet or grill pan over high heat until smoking, about 3 minutes. Add 1 tbsp oil and swirl to coat.
Working in batches to avoid crowding, spread beef in a single layer and sear, turning once, until browned and just cooked through, 2 to 3 minutes total per batch.
Add sliced onion, carrot, and scallions to the pan with the last batch and stir-fry until crisp-tender, about 1 to 2 minutes.
Return all cooked beef to the pan, toss with vegetables, and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed; serve immediately.
Optional: For charcoal grill, preheat to high heat. Oil grates, then grill beef slices over direct heat, 1 to 2 minutes per side, until lightly charred and cooked through.
tip: Swap Asian pear with 1/2 apple if needed. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat quickly over high heat to avoid steaming.

title: Carne Asada Tacos
steps: Whisk lime juice, orange juice, soy sauce, olive oil, cilantro, garlic, cumin, chili powder, oregano, salt, and pepper in a bowl to make the marinade.
Pat steak dry, place in a shallow dish, and pour marinade over. Turn to coat. Marinate 20–30 minutes at room temperature (or up to 2 hours refrigerated; bring to room temp before cooking).
Heat a grill or heavy skillet over high heat until very hot, 3–5 minutes. Lightly oil grates or add a thin film of frying oil to the skillet just before cooking.

Shake excess marinade from steak. Sear over high heat until well browned and medium-rare, about 4–5 minutes per side (cook to 130–135°F for medium-rare or 140°F for medium). Rest on a board 5–10 minutes.
Warm corn tortillas on the grill or in a dry skillet over medium heat until pliable and lightly charred, 30–45 seconds per side. Keep wrapped in a clean towel.
Slice steak thinly against the grain, then chop into bite-size pieces for easy tacos. Toss with any resting juices on the board.
Assemble tacos: fill warm tortillas with carne asada, top with white onion, cilantro, and salsa. Squeeze lime over to finish.
Serve immediately, with extra lime and salsa on the side.
tip: Skirt steak is traditional and grills beautifully; cook 2–4 minutes per side. Leftover carne asada keeps 3 days refrigerated; rewarm quickly in a hot skillet to avoid overcooking.

title: Chili con Carne
ing: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
3 tbsp chili powder (New Mexican or ancho)
steps: Pat beef dry, season with 1 tsp of the salt and the pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium-high until shimmering, then brown beef in batches, 6–8 minutes total, adding oil as needed.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and a pinch of salt; cook, stirring, until translucent, 5–6 minutes. Stir in garlic; cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chili powder, cumin, oregano, and cayenne; toast, stirring, 45–60 seconds. Stir in tomato paste; cook 1 minute to darken slightly.

Return beef and any juices to pot. Pour in broth and water, scraping up browned bits. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer; cover partially and simmer for 60 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and continue to simmer until beef is very tender and sauce thickens, 20–30 minutes more. Skim fat if desired.
Stir in vinegar and brown sugar. Mix 1 tbsp masa harina with 2 tbsp water; stir into chili and simmer 5 minutes to lightly thicken. Adjust salt to 1 tbsp total to taste.
Ensure beef is tender and hot; serve hot with optional garnishes (chopped onion, jalapeño, cilantro), and warm tortillas on the side.
tip: For deeper flavor, make a day ahead and reheat; it thickens and mellows. Swap 1 cup broth with strong coffee or lager. Traditional Texas chili omits beans; serve beans on the side if desired.

title: Philly Cheesesteak
ing: 1 lb ribeye steak, very thinly sliced, partially frozen for easier slicing
steps: Freeze ribeye for 30 minutes to firm, then slice paper-thin against the grain. Pat dry to minimize steaming.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large griddle or skillet over medium-high until shimmering, 2 minutes. Add onions, 1/4 tsp salt; cook, stirring, until deeply golden, 8–10 minutes. Transfer aside.

Add 1 tbsp oil to the pan. Spread beef in a single layer; season with remaining 1/4 tsp salt and pepper. Sear without moving 1 minute, then toss and cook until just browned, 2–3 minutes (beef should reach 145°F).
Chop beef lightly with a spatula, mix onions back in, and form 4 even mounds. Lay provolone over each mound; let melt, 1–2 minutes.
Meanwhile, spread cut sides of rolls with butter. Toast cut sides on the griddle until lightly crisp, 1–2 minutes.
Use a spatula to scoop each cheesy mound into a toasted roll, pressing gently to fill end-to-end.
Serve hot immediately; wrap in parchment for a minute to meld if desired.
tip: Wiz-heads: swap provolone for 1 cup warm Cheez Whiz. For peppers, add 1 cup thin-sliced green bell pepper with onions. Leftovers keep 2 days; rewarm beef/onions on skillet, then add cheese and fill fresh rolls.

title: Mongolian Beef
ing: 1 lb flank steak, sliced thin against the grain
1 tbsp cornstarch, mixed with 1 tbsp water
2 cups cooked white rice, for serving
1 tsp sesame seeds, for garnish, to taste
steps: Pat steak dry, slice 1/4-inch thick against the grain, and toss with 3 tbsp cornstarch until evenly coated; rest 10 minutes to hydrate the starch.
Whisk soy sauce, water, brown sugar, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, red pepper flakes, and black pepper in a bowl; set aside. Stir together 1 tbsp cornstarch with 1 tbsp water for slurry.
Heat a large skillet or wok over high heat 2 minutes. Add 2 tbsp frying oil and sear half the beef in a single layer 45–60 seconds per side until browned; remove. Repeat with more oil as needed.
Reduce heat to medium. Add 1 tsp oil, then ginger and garlic; stir-fry 20–30 seconds until fragrant, avoiding browning.
Return beef to pan. Pour in the sauce; bring to a rapid simmer over medium-high and cook 1 minute, stirring.
Stir the cornstarch slurry, add gradually, and simmer for 1–2 minutes until the sauce turns glossy and coats the beef.
Add scallions and toss 30–45 seconds over medium-high heat until just wilted but bright.
Serve immediately over hot rice; sprinkle with sesame seeds to garnish.
tip: For extra tenderness, add 1/4 tsp baking soda to the beef with cornstarch and rest 15 minutes, then rinse and pat dry before coating. Swap Shaoxing wine with dry sherry if needed.

title: Classic Pot Roast
steps: Pat roast dry, season all sides with 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp pepper. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy Dutch oven over medium-high until shimmering, then brown roast 4–5 minutes per side.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and cook 4 minutes until softened. Stir in garlic 30 seconds, then tomato paste 1 minute until darkened.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables and cook 1 minute. Pour in red wine, scraping browned bits; simmer 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Return roast to pot. Add beef broth, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf. Liquid should come halfway up the meat; add a splash more broth if needed.
Cover and braise at 325°F for 2 hours, turning roast once halfway through, until fork-tender.
Add carrots and potatoes around the roast, re-cover, and braise at 325°F for 45–60 minutes until vegetables are tender and beef shreds easily.
Transfer roast and vegetables to a platter, tent with foil. Skim fat from juices; simmer juices on stovetop 3–5 minutes. Whisk in butter to gloss; adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Slice or pull beef across the grain. Spoon pan sauce over meat and vegetables and serve hot (beef should be at least 145°F and fork-tender).
tip: Swap red wine with additional broth if desired. Leftovers keep 4 days refrigerated; reheat gently with a splash of broth.

title: Swedish Meatballs
ing: 1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: In a bowl, combine 3/4 cup milk and 3/4 cup breadcrumbs; let stand 5 minutes to hydrate.
Mix in onion, egg, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper, allspice, and nutmeg, then gently fold in beef and pork until just combined; chill 10 minutes.
With damp hands, form 24 walnut-size meatballs (about 1 to 1 1/4 oz each) for even cooking.
Heat 1 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium; brown meatballs in batches until well browned on all sides, 6–8 minutes total; transfer to a plate.
Melt remaining 1 tbsp butter in the skillet; whisk in flour and cook 1 minute, scraping browned bits.
Whisk in beef broth; bring to a simmer and cook 5 minutes, then whisk in cream and mustard; simmer for 3–4 minutes until lightly thickened.
Return meatballs and any juices to sauce; simmer gently for 5–7 minutes until cooked through to 160°F internal temperature.
Taste and season gravy with salt and pepper; garnish with parsley and serve hot with mashed potatoes or lingonberry sauce.
tip: Use all-beef if preferred; add a splash of soy for deeper color. Meatballs and gravy keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat gently with a little broth or cream.

title: Ropa Vieja
ing: 1 large green bell pepper, thinly sliced
2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro, for garnish
steps: Pat the flank steak dry and season with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium-high, sear steak 3–4 minutes per side until well browned; transfer to a plate.

Add 1 tbsp oil if needed. Add onion and green bell pepper; cook over medium heat, stirring, until softened and lightly golden, 8–10 minutes. Stir in garlic, cumin, oregano, and allspice; cook 30 seconds.
Pour in white wine, scraping up browned bits; simmer for 2 minutes. Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, roasted red peppers, olives, capers, and tomato paste; bring to a simmer.
Return steak and any juices to the pot, submerging in sauce. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer gently for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours, turning once, until beef is very tender.
Transfer beef to a board and cool 5 minutes. Shred along the grain into thin strands using two forks.
Return shredded beef to the pot; simmer uncovered over medium-low for 10–15 minutes to thicken and meld flavors. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped cilantro. Ensure beef is reheated to 165°F before serving. Pair with white rice and sweet plantains if desired.
tip: For a richer base, swap 1 cup broth with reserved beef cooking liquid if using pressure cooker. Leftovers keep 4 days chilled; reheat gently with a splash of broth.

title: Lomo Saltado
ing: 1 lb beef sirloin, cut into 1/2-inch thick, 2- to 3-inch strips
1 lb russet potatoes, cut into 1/3-inch batons
1 large red onion, cut into thick wedges
2 medium Roma tomatoes, cut into thick wedges
1 small ají amarillo, seeded and sliced (or 1 tbsp ají amarillo paste)
1 lime, cut into wedges, for serving
steps: Pat beef very dry, then toss with cumin, black pepper, and 1/2 tsp salt; let stand 10 minutes while you prepare other ingredients.
Rinse potatoes, pat dry, then fry in 350°F oil until golden and crisp, about 6–8 minutes; drain on paper towels and season with 1/2 tsp salt.
Whisk soy sauce, oyster sauce, red wine vinegar, and beef broth in a small bowl; set the sauce by the stove.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large wok over high until just smoking. Sear half the beef in a single layer, 1–2 minutes, until browned but still medium; transfer. Repeat with remaining beef, adding oil as needed.
Add onion to the hot wok; stir-fry over high heat 2 minutes until edges char. Add garlic and ají amarillo; stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return beef and accumulated juices to the wok. Add tomatoes and the sauce; toss over high heat 1–2 minutes until tomatoes just soften and sauce thickens slightly.
Remove from heat and immediately fold in the hot fries to coat but keep them crisp. Taste and adjust salt or vinegar to balance.
Serve at once, garnished with cilantro and lime wedges. Optionally serve with steamed rice alongside.
tip: For authenticity, use ají amarillo; if unavailable, use paste. Fries can be double-cooked: par-fry at 325°F, cool, then finish at 375°F for extra crispness. Serve with rice for the classic combo.

title: Steak au Poivre
ing: 4 steaks beef tenderloin (filet mignon), 6 oz each
2 tbsp whole black peppercorns, coarsely crushed
steps: Pat steaks dry, season all sides with 1 tsp kosher salt. Press the coarsely crushed peppercorns onto both flat faces to adhere.
Heat a heavy skillet over medium-high until very hot, 3 to 4 minutes. Add a thin film of frying oil and 1 tbsp butter.
Sear steaks 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium-rare, turning once. For safety, cook to at least 145°F for medium; rest 5 minutes on a warm plate.
Pour off excess fat, leaving about 1 tbsp. Add shallots and cook over medium heat until translucent, 1 to 2 minutes.
Off the heat, add cognac. Return to medium heat and simmer 1 to 2 minutes, scraping browned bits; reduce by half. Use caution if it flames.
Stir in heavy cream, Dijon, and Worcestershire. Simmer gently, stirring, until nappe thick, 3 to 4 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Whisk in remaining 1 tbsp butter off heat for gloss. Spoon sauce over rested steaks and sprinkle with parsley.
Serve immediately with frites or a simple green salad.
tip: Authentic pepper bite comes from coarse crushed peppercorns, not preground. Sauce holds warm up to 30 minutes; keep at very low heat and thin with a splash of cream if needed.

title: Birria Tacos
ing: 2 lb beef chuck roast, cut into 3-inch chunks
6 dried guajillo chiles, stems and seeds removed
3 dried ancho chiles, stems and seeds removed
2 dried chiles de árbol, stems and seeds removed
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1/2 tsp black pepper, plus more to taste
1/2 cup white onion, finely diced, for garnish
steps: Toast guajillo, ancho, and árbol chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant; do not burn. Simmer chiles in 2 cups boiling water for 10 minutes, then drain.

Broil tomatoes, onion, and garlic on the top rack at 500°F for 8 to 10 minutes until lightly charred. Blend with softened chiles, vinegar, oregano, cumin, paprika, 1 tsp salt, and 1 cup beef broth until smooth.
Season beef with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Sear in a heavy pot with 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes until browned on all sides.
Pour the chile sauce over beef. Add bay leaves and remaining beef broth to barely cover. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently over low heat for 2 to 2 1/2 hours until beef is very tender.
Remove beef; shred with two forks. Skim excess fat from consomé, adjust salt to taste, and keep warm at a gentle simmer for serving.
Heat a skillet over medium. Lightly oil the surface with 1 to 2 tsp oil. Dip a tortilla into the hot consomé to coat, place on the skillet, and cook 30 to 45 seconds until pliable.
Add 2 to 3 tbsp shredded beef and 1 to 2 tbsp Oaxaca cheese to half of the tortilla. Fold and cook 1 to 2 minutes per side until crisp and cheese melts; repeat with remaining tortillas.
Serve tacos hot with cups of consomé for dipping. Garnish tacos and consomé with diced onion, cilantro, and lime wedges to taste.
tip: Sub chuck with short ribs or beef shank for richer flavor. Birria and consomé keep 4 days refrigerated; reheat gently and re-crisp tortillas to serve.

title: Galbi-jjim (Korean Braised Short Ribs)
ing: 3 lb beef short ribs, English-cut, 2-3 inch pieces
8 oz Korean radish (mu) or daikon, peeled, 1-inch chunks
1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, for garnish
steps: Soak ribs in cold water for 30 minutes to draw out blood, changing water once. Drain well and pat dry.
Blanch ribs: cover with cold water in a pot, bring to a boil, and simmer 5 minutes. Drain, rinse ribs and pot to remove scum.
Make sauce: in a bowl combine soy sauce, brown sugar, mirin, sesame oil, grated pear, grated onion, garlic, ginger, black pepper, and 2 cups water.
Heat frying oil over medium in a heavy pot. Add ribs and sear 3-4 minutes per side until browned.
Add sauce to pot, bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 60 minutes, skimming fat as needed.
Add radish and carrot, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes. Add potato and mushrooms, simmer uncovered 15-20 minutes until vegetables are tender and sauce is glossy.
Check seasoning with salt to taste. For richer glaze, simmer uncovered 5 more minutes, basting ribs. Beef should be fork-tender and at least 145°F internal.
Rest 5 minutes off heat. Garnish with scallions and sesame seeds and serve with steamed rice.
tip: Swap Asian pear with 1/2 apple if needed. Make ahead: chill overnight, lift solidified fat, rewarm gently with a splash of water; flavors deepen.

title: Picadillo
ing: 1/2 cup green bell pepper, finely diced
1/2 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/4 tsp black pepper, or to taste
steps: Warm 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering, about 1 minute.
Add 1 cup onion and 1/2 cup green bell pepper; sauté until softened and translucent, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in 3 cloves minced garlic; cook until fragrant, 30 seconds.
Add 1 lb ground beef; cook, breaking up, until no longer pink and lightly browned, 6 to 8 minutes. Drain excess fat if needed.
Season with 1 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp oregano, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp pepper, and 1 bay leaf; stir 30 seconds to bloom spices.
Pour in 8 oz tomato sauce and 1/2 cup dry white wine; bring to a simmer over medium heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in 1/3 cup sliced olives, 1/4 cup raisins, and 1 tbsp capers; continue to simmer until flavors meld and sauce thickens to a glossy ragu, 5 to 8 minutes.
Remove bay leaf; taste and adjust salt and pepper. Rest off heat 2 minutes before serving over rice or with fried plantains.
tip: For a milder sauce, swap wine with 1/2 cup low-sodium beef broth. Picadillo keeps 4 days refrigerated; reheats well. Add diced potatoes (3/4 lb, 1/2-inch) par-cooked 8 minutes, then simmer in sauce until tender.

title: Sloppy Joes
ing: 1/2 cup green bell pepper, finely chopped
4 buns hamburger buns, split and toasted
steps: Warm 1 tbsp frying oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 lb ground beef and cook, breaking up, until browned and no pink remains, 6 to 8 minutes. Drain excess fat if needed.
Add 1/2 cup chopped onion, 1/2 cup chopped green bell pepper, and 2 cloves minced garlic. Cook, stirring, until softened and fragrant, 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in 3/4 cup tomato sauce, 1/4 cup ketchup, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp yellow mustard, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, and 1/2 cup water until combined.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until thick and glossy, 10 to 12 minutes. Season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper to taste.
Meanwhile, spread 2 tbsp butter on the cut sides of 4 hamburger buns and toast in a skillet over medium heat until golden, 1 to 2 minutes.
Taste the filling and adjust sweetness, tang, or salt as desired. The mixture should be spoonable but not runny; add a splash of water if too thick.
Spoon the hot beef mixture onto toasted buns and serve immediately. Beef is fully cooked when crumbled and browned throughout (160°F).
tip: Swap green bell pepper with red for sweeter flavor. Filling keeps 3 days refrigerated; rewarm with a splash of water over medium heat.

title: Beef and Broccoli
ing: 1 lb flank steak, sliced thin against the grain
steps: In a bowl, whisk 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 2 tsp cornstarch, 1 tsp sugar, 1/4 tsp baking soda, and 3 tbsp water. Toss with steak and marinate 15 minutes.
Blanch broccoli in boiling salted water for 1 minute until bright green; drain and shock under cold water, then pat very dry.
Stir together 1/2 cup beef broth, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and 1 tbsp cornstarch until smooth; set aside as the sauce.
Heat a wok over high heat until smoking, add 1 tbsp oil, and stir-fry half the beef in a single layer 1–2 minutes until just browned; remove. Repeat with 1 tbsp oil and remaining beef.
Return wok to medium-high, add garlic and ginger, stir-fry 20 seconds until fragrant without browning.
Add broccoli and the cooked beef, pour in the sauce, and stir-fry over high heat until the sauce boils and thickens, about 1–2 minutes.
Drizzle in 1 tbsp sesame oil, season with black pepper to taste, and toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately with steamed rice; beef should be cooked to at least 145°F for safety and remain tender.
tip: Slice beef very thin while half-frozen for best results. Shaoxing wine adds depth; sub dry sherry if needed. Blanched broccoli can be chilled up to 2 days; re-dry before stir-frying.

title: Bobotie
ing: 1 tbsp chutney (Mrs. H.S. Ball’s or similar)
2 tbsp fruit chutney or apricot jam
steps: Heat oven to 350°F. Tear 2 slices bread into a bowl, pour in 1/2 cup milk, and soak for 5 minutes. Squeeze gently, reserving the soaking milk for the custard; crumble bread.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Cook onion with a pinch of salt, stirring, until soft and golden, 8 to 10 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in curry powder, turmeric, coriander, cinnamon, and cloves; toast spices 30 seconds. Add ground beef and cook, breaking up, until no pink remains and moisture reduces, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in crumbled soaked bread, chutney, raisins, lemon juice, Worcestershire, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp pepper. Simmer 2 minutes to meld. Spread mixture evenly in a greased 8-inch square baking dish.
Whisk reserved milk with 2 eggs and a pinch of salt until smooth. Pour custard over the meat, tilting dish to distribute. Nestle 1 bay leaf on top.
Bake at 350°F until custard is set and an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 160°F, 30 to 35 minutes. Rest 10 minutes before serving.
tip: Serve with yellow rice and chutney. Swap half the beef for ground lamb for a richer, traditional flavor; leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated.

title: Smash Burgers
ing: 1 small yellow onion, very thinly sliced
steps: Preheat a heavy stainless or cast-iron skillet over medium-high until lightly smoking, about 5 minutes.
Split and lightly butter the cut sides of buns. Toast in the dry skillet until golden, 1 to 2 minutes. Set aside.
Stir mayonnaise, ketchup, and mustard in a small bowl to make sauce; set aside.
Divide beef into 4 loose balls (about 5 oz each). Do not compact; season tops lightly with salt and pepper.
Add a thin film of oil to the hot skillet. Place 2 beef balls seasoned side down. Immediately top with a small mound of onions.
Using a stiff metal spatula and another tool for leverage, smash each ball very thin (about 1/4 inch), pressing firmly for 10 seconds to maximize crust.

Cook without moving until deeply browned and edges crisp, 2 to 3 minutes. Scrape under each patty to release crust, flip, top each with a cheese slice, and cook 45 to 60 seconds more until cheese melts and beef is at least 160°F.
Spread sauce on toasted buns, add lettuce and pickles. Stack patties onto buns and serve immediately. Repeat with remaining beef.
tip: For extra onion flavor, smash a few rings directly into the meat. Keep patties thin; resist re-smashing after the first press or you’ll lose juices.

title: Fish Tacos
ing: 1 lb mild white fish fillets, cut into 1-inch strips
2 tbsp Mexican crema or sour cream
steps: Whisk flour, baking powder, 1 tsp salt, cumin, and chili powder in a bowl. Whisk in cold beer until smooth; batter should be thick but pourable. Chill batter for 10 minutes.
Toss cabbage and red onion with mayonnaise, crema, lime juice, hot sauce, a pinch of salt, and black pepper to taste. Let slaw stand for 10 minutes to wilt slightly.
Heat 1 inch frying oil in a deep skillet to 350°F over medium-high heat. Pat fish dry and season lightly with a pinch of salt.
Dip fish strips in batter, letting excess drip. Fry in batches at 350°F until deep golden and fish flakes, about 3 to 4 minutes; internal temperature should reach 145°F. Drain on a rack.
Warm corn tortillas directly over a burner or in a dry skillet over medium heat until pliable, 30 to 45 seconds per side. Keep wrapped in a clean towel.
Assemble tacos: place a few fish pieces in each tortilla, top with cabbage slaw and cilantro. Squeeze lime over the top.
Serve immediately with extra lime wedges and hot sauce on the side.
tip: Swap beer with sparkling water for non-alcoholic batter. Keep fried fish crisp on a 250°F rack up to 20 minutes. Leftover slaw keeps chilled 1 day; refresh with a squeeze of lime.

title: Shrimp Scampi
ing: 1 1/2 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails on
1 tbsp fresh lemon zest, finely grated
12 oz linguine, cooked al dente, reserved 1/2 cup pasta water
1 tbsp olive oil, for frying, as needed
1/4 cup grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, for garnish, optional
1 lemon, cut into wedges, for serving
steps: Pat shrimp dry, then season with 1/2 tsp kosher salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente, 8–10 minutes; reserve 1/2 cup pasta water and drain.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering, about 1 minute. Add shrimp in a single layer and sear until just pink at edges, 1–2 minutes per side; transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add 4 tbsp butter to the skillet. When foaming, add minced garlic and red pepper flakes; sauté until fragrant but not browned, about 45 seconds.
Pour in dry white wine; simmer briskly until reduced by about half, 2–3 minutes. Stir in lemon zest and lemon juice; simmer 30 seconds to meld.
Return shrimp and any juices to the skillet; toss gently until shrimp are opaque and cooked through, 1–2 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in parsley.
Add cooked linguine to the skillet. Toss, loosening with splashes of reserved pasta water until the sauce lightly coats the pasta, 1–3 minutes. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil if needed for sheen. Serve immediately with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano (optional) and lemon wedges.
tip: Use vermouth if wine isn’t handy. For extra brininess, add 2 tbsp capers with the wine. Leftovers keep 1 day; rewarm gently with a splash of water or wine to loosen the sauce.

title: Cioppino
ing: 12 oz firm white fish, cut into 2-inch chunks
12 oz large shrimp, peeled and deveined
8 oz squid, cleaned and sliced into rings
1 small fennel bulb, cored and thinly sliced
1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped, plus more for garnish
steps: Warm 2 tbsp olive oil with 1 tbsp frying oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add onion and fennel; cook, stirring, until softened and translucent, about 8 minutes.
Stir in garlic and red pepper flakes; cook 30 seconds. Add white wine; simmer until reduced by half, about 3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits.
Add crushed tomatoes, seafood stock, bay leaf, oregano, 1/2 tsp salt, and a grind of pepper. Bring to a simmer over medium-low and cook uncovered for 20 minutes to meld flavors.
Rinse mussels and clams; discard any with cracked shells. Increase heat to medium. Add clams to the pot, cover, and cook until they just begin to open, about 6 minutes.
Add mussels; cover and cook until shells open, 3 to 4 minutes. Discard any that do not open.
Gently nestle fish and squid into the broth; simmer uncovered until fish flakes easily, 4 to 5 minutes (fish should reach 145°F).
Add shrimp; simmer until pink and opaque, 2 to 3 minutes (shrimp should reach 120–130°F). Taste and adjust salt and pepper.
Remove bay leaf. Stir in 1/4 cup parsley. Ladle into warm bowls, garnish with more parsley, and serve with lemon wedges and crusty bread.
tip: Use Dungeness crab in place of squid for a classic touch; add cooked picked meat in the last 2 minutes. Broth can be made 1 day ahead; cool, refrigerate, and reheat gently before adding seafood.

title: Bouillabaisse
ing: 2 lbs mixed firm white fish with bones (monkfish, sea bass), cut in 3-inch pieces
1 lb small shell-on shrimp or prawns
1 lb small mussels, scrubbed and debearded
1 large fennel bulb, cored and sliced thin
1 lb ripe tomatoes, grated or crushed
steps: Warm 2 tbsp olive oil in a large wide pot over medium heat. Add onion and fennel; cook until softened and lightly golden, 8 to 10 minutes. Stir in garlic for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, saffron, paprika, and orange zest. Cook, stirring, until thick and jammy, 5 to 6 minutes. Pour in white wine; simmer 2 minutes to reduce.
Add 6 cups fish stock, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp pepper. Bring to a strong boil over high heat, then maintain a lively boil for 10 minutes to build body and flavor.
Arrange the firm white fish pieces in the boiling broth in a single layer; boil briskly until fish is just opaque and flakes, 6 to 8 minutes (145°F). Do not stir; shake pot gently.
Add shrimp; boil until pink and opaque, 2 to 3 minutes (145°F). Add mussels and clams; cover and cook at a lively boil until shells open, 3 to 5 minutes. Discard any that stay closed.
While seafood cooks, toast baguette slices in a 425°F oven until crisp and golden, 6 to 8 minutes. Rub lightly with a cut garlic clove if desired.
Taste broth and adjust salt and pepper. Ladle broth into warm bowls, then divide fish and shellfish on top. Serve immediately with toasted baguette on the side.
tip: For a classic rouille, blend 1 roasted red pepper, 1 garlic clove, pinch saffron, 1/2 cup mayo, and 1 tbsp olive oil; spread on toasts. Fish stock can be made from fish heads/bones and fennel trimmings.

title: Shrimp and Grits
ing: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 small green bell pepper, finely chopped
2 tbsp scallions, thinly sliced, for garnish
steps: Bring 4 cups water and 1 cup milk to a simmer over medium heat; whisk in 1 cup grits. Reduce heat to low, cover slightly ajar, and cook, whisking often, until creamy, 20–25 minutes.
Stir 2 tbsp butter, 6 oz shredded cheddar, and a pinch of salt into the grits. Keep warm on low; add a splash of hot water if too thick.
Pat 1 lb shrimp dry; season lightly with salt and pepper. Heat a large skillet over medium; cook 4 oz diced bacon until crisp, 6–8 minutes. Transfer bacon to a plate; leave 2 tbsp drippings.
If needed, add 1 tbsp frying oil. Sauté 1 chopped onion and 1 chopped green bell pepper in drippings over medium until tender, 6–8 minutes. Add 2 minced garlic cloves; cook 30 seconds.
Pour in 1 cup chicken stock; scrape browned bits. Simmer until slightly reduced, 3–4 minutes. Stir in 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1 tsp hot sauce; season with salt and pepper to taste.
Increase heat to medium-high; add shrimp in a single layer. Cook, turning once, until opaque and 145°F in the thickest part, 3–4 minutes total. Return bacon; toss to coat and heat 30 seconds.
Spoon creamy grits into 4 warm bowls. Top evenly with shrimp, bacon, and pan sauce. Garnish with 2 tbsp sliced scallions.
Serve immediately while hot; adjust seasoning with additional hot sauce, salt, or pepper as desired.
tip: Use stone-ground grits for best texture; avoid instant. Swap cheddar for smoked gouda. Leftovers keep 2 days chilled; rewarm grits with a splash of milk, and reheat shrimp gently to avoid overcooking.

title: Ahi Poke Bowl
ing: 1 lb sashimi-grade ahi tuna, 1/2-inch dice, well-chilled
2 tbsp sweet Maui onion, very thinly sliced
1 tsp limu or ogo seaweed, rinsed and chopped
1 tsp crushed red pepper flakes (Hawaiian chili pepper if available)
1 tsp roasted kukui nut (inamona), finely ground
steps: Chill a mixing bowl for 5 minutes to keep the fish cold. Pat the 1 lb tuna dry, then cut into even 1/2-inch cubes; keep refrigerated until seasoning.
In the chilled bowl, whisk 1/4 cup shoyu, 2 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tsp rice vinegar, and 1 tsp sugar until dissolved, about 30 seconds.
Add tuna, 2 tbsp Maui onion, 2 tbsp green onions, 1 tsp sesame seeds, 1 tsp limu, 1 tsp inamona, and 1 tsp red pepper flakes. Gently fold until just coated, 20 to 30 seconds.
Season with sea salt and black pepper to taste. Cover and chill for 10 to 15 minutes to let flavors marry; do not exceed 30 minutes to keep texture.
While poke chills, cook short-grain rice if needed and keep warm at 150°F; slice 1 cup cucumber into thin half-moons.
Divide 4 cups warm rice among 4 bowls. Spoon poke over rice, letting some marinade drip but not pool, about 1 cup poke mixture per bowl.
Garnish each bowl with extra green onion or sesame seeds if desired; serve immediately while rice is warm and fish is cold.
tip: Authentic touch: limu and inamona add true island flavor—sub wakame and toasted macadamia if unavailable. Keep tuna very cold and serve within 2 hours; leftovers don’t store well.

title: Ceviche
ing: 1 lb firm white fish fillet, skinned and cut in 1/2-inch cubes
1/2 cup red onion, very thinly sliced
1 small ají limo or serrano chile, thinly sliced
1/2 cup cooked corn kernels or choclo, cooled
1 lime, cut into wedges for serving
steps: Rinse onion in cold water for 30 seconds, drain well, and pat dry to tame sharpness; set aside.
Chill a nonreactive bowl and the fish for 10 minutes to keep very cold. Pat fish dry and place in the chilled bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk lime juice, salt, pepper, and sugar until dissolved to make the leche de tigre.
Add fish and chile to the lime mixture, stir gently to coat, and marinate in the refrigerator for 10 to 12 minutes until fish turns opaque on edges.
Fold in the red onion and cilantro, toss gently, and rest 2 minutes to meld flavors.
Taste and adjust salt to balance bright acidity; the liquid should be vibrant and lightly seasoned.
Lightly oil 4 chilled plates with a few drops of frying oil, then divide ceviche and spoon over some leche de tigre.
Serve immediately with sweet potato slices, corn, and lime wedges; consume at once while cold.
tip: Use ultra-fresh, sushi-grade firm fish like corvina, fluke, or halibut. Prep garnishes ahead; ceviche should be mixed just before serving. Keep everything very cold for best texture.

title: Maryland Crab Cakes
ing: 1 lb lump crab meat, picked over for shells
steps: Gently drain any excess liquid from the crab. In a large bowl, whisk mayonnaise, egg, Dijon, Worcestershire, Old Bay, lemon juice, a pinch of salt, and pepper until smooth.
Fold in the crab and parsley, then sprinkle in the crushed saltines. Using a spatula, fold just until the mixture holds together; do not break up the lumps.
Divide into 8 cakes (about 1/2 cup each) and compress lightly. Cover and chill for 15 minutes to help them set.
Heat 1 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering, about 2 minutes.
Add half the cakes and cook until deeply golden, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Internal temperature should reach 145°F. Transfer to a paper towel–lined plate.
Repeat with remaining butter and oil and cook the remaining cakes, 3 to 4 minutes per side, to 145°F internal temperature.
Serve hot with lemon wedges; adjust salt and pepper to taste.
tip: Use as few binders as possible to keep crab forward; add more crushed saltines by the tablespoon only if too loose. Chill formed cakes up to 24 hours; re-crisp in a skillet before serving.

title: Lobster Roll
ing: 4 1/2 lb live lobsters, steamed and meat picked
4 split-top brioche or New England hot dog buns
steps: Steam 4 1/2 lb live lobsters over vigorously boiling water, covered, for 8–10 minutes until shells are bright red; cool, then pick tail, claw, and knuckle meat. Chop into 1/2-inch pieces.
Whisk 1/3 cup mayonnaise, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and 1 tsp Dijon in a bowl. Fold in 1 tbsp celery and 1 tbsp chives. Season with 1/4 tsp salt and 1/8 tsp pepper.
Gently toss lobster meat with dressing just to lightly coat. Chill 10 minutes to meld flavors while you toast the buns.
Heat a large skillet over medium. Brush bun outsides with 2 tbsp melted butter; add 1 tbsp butter and a film of oil. Toast buns 2–3 minutes per side until golden.
Fill each warm bun generously with dressed lobster, dividing evenly among 4 rolls. Do not pack too tightly; let large chunks show.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges; sprinkle with 2 tbsp chopped chives to garnish. Keep rolls warm, not hot, to preserve texture.
tip: For Connecticut-style, skip mayo and warm lobster in 3 tbsp melted butter; fill buns. Meat can be picked up to 1 day ahead; keep refrigerated and dress just before serving.

title: Moqueca
ing: 1.5 lb firm white fish fillets, cut into 2-inch pieces
1 cup red bell pepper, thinly sliced
steps: Pat fish dry, toss with lime juice, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp pepper; marinate for 15 minutes while you prep the vegetables.
Warm 1 tbsp frying oil in a wide pot over medium heat; add onion and bell pepper and cook until softened, about 6 minutes.
Stir in tomato and garlic; cook 2 minutes. Sprinkle in paprika and annatto; stir 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk and fish stock; bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, about 3 minutes.
Nestle fish pieces in a single layer; cover and simmer gently until opaque and flakes easily, 8 to 10 minutes. Fish should reach 145°F at the thickest part.
Drizzle in dendê oil; simmer uncovered 1 minute to bloom its aroma. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Remove from heat; fold in most of the cilantro and scallions, reserving a little for garnish.
Rest 2 minutes, then ladle into warm bowls and garnish with remaining herbs. Serve with rice and farofa.
tip: If dendê oil is unavailable, infuse 1 tbsp neutral oil with 1/2 tsp annatto as a stopgap. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; reheat gently to avoid overcooking the fish.

title: Miso-Glazed Black Cod
ing: 1 tsp neutral frying oil, as needed
steps: Whisk 1/3 cup white miso, 3 tbsp mirin, 2 tbsp sake, 1 tbsp sugar, and 1 tsp soy sauce in a bowl until smooth to make the marinade.
Pat cod dry. Spread a thin layer of marinade on all sides, place in a nonreactive dish, cover, and refrigerate 12–48 hours for best flavor; turn once halfway through.
When ready to cook, wipe excess marinade from fish to prevent burning. Lightly oil a foil-lined sheet or broiler pan with 1 tsp neutral oil.
Position rack 6 inches from broiler element. Preheat broiler to high for 5 minutes, then broil fish skin-side down for 4–5 minutes until top is caramelized.
Flip carefully; broil 3–5 minutes more until fish flakes easily and internal temp reaches 145°F at the thickest part.
Rest 2 minutes. Transfer to plates, spoon any pan drippings over, and garnish with scallions and sesame seeds.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges; squeeze just before eating to balance sweetness.
tip: Saikyo miso gives the signature gentle sweetness; substitute any white (shiro) miso if needed. Marinated fillets keep refrigerated up to 2 days; blot and cook straight from the fridge.

title: Moules Frites
ing: 2 leeks, white and light green parts thinly sliced
1 lb russet potatoes, cut into 1/4-inch batons
1 lb russet potatoes, cut into 3/8-inch batons
1 lemon, cut into wedges, for serving
steps: Rinse mussels under cold water, discarding any with cracked shells or that remain open after a firm tap. Keep chilled and covered with a damp towel.

Rinse potato batons, soak in cold water for 20 minutes, then drain and pat very dry. Heat frying oil to 325°F in a deep pot; fry potatoes in batches 4–5 minutes until pale and tender. Drain on a rack.
Increase oil to 375°F. Just before serving, fry potatoes again 2–3 minutes until crisp and golden. Season hot fries with 1/2 tsp salt and set on a rack.
For the mussels, melt butter with olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add leeks, 1/2 tsp salt, and cook 6–8 minutes until soft but not browned; add garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Add wine, bay leaf, and thyme; bring to a boil over high heat for 2 minutes to reduce slightly. Add mussels, cover, and steam over high heat, shaking the pot, for 4–6 minutes until shells open.
Discard any mussels that remain closed. Reduce heat to low, stir in cream and half the parsley, and season with pepper and additional salt to taste. Simmer 1 minute to warm through without boiling.
Serve mussels in warm bowls with plenty of broth. Top with remaining parsley and lemon wedges. Serve frites immediately on the side for dipping into the mussel broth.
tip: Substitute shallots for leeks for a sharper profile. Keep fries crisp by draining on a rack, not paper. To reheat fries, refry 1–2 minutes at 375°F.

title: Garlic Butter Shrimp
ing: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails on
1 lemon, cut into wedges, for serving
steps: Pat shrimp dry with paper towels and season with 1/4 tsp kosher salt and 1/8 tsp black pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil and 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high until butter foams, about 1 minute.

Add shrimp in a single layer; cook without moving until pink on bottoms, about 1 to 1 1/2 minutes. Flip and cook 1 minute more; transfer to a plate (internal temp should reach 120°F for shrimp doneness).
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 1 tbsp butter and minced garlic; cook, stirring, until fragrant but not browned, 30 to 45 seconds.
Stir in 1/4 cup dry white wine and 1 tbsp lemon juice; simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, scraping browned bits, until slightly reduced.
Return shrimp and any juices to the skillet; add red pepper flakes and lemon zest. Toss over medium heat until coated and heated through, 30 to 60 seconds.
Remove from heat; sprinkle parsley and adjust seasoning to taste. Serve immediately with lemon wedges.
Optional: Spoon over rice, pasta, or crusty bread to catch the sauce.
tip: Swap wine with 1/4 cup low-sodium chicken broth if preferred. Leftovers keep 1 day refrigerated; rewarm gently on low to avoid overcooking shrimp.

title: Tod Mun Pla (Thai Fish Cakes)
ing: 1 lb firm white fish fillets, skinless, diced
1/2 cup finely sliced yardlong beans, thinly chopped
1/2 cup thinly sliced kaffir lime leaves
steps: Place fish, red curry paste, fish sauce, sugar, and egg in a food processor; pulse until a smooth, tacky paste forms, 30–60 seconds. Chill the paste for 10 minutes to firm.
Fold in chopped yardlong beans and sliced kaffir lime leaves until evenly distributed; the mixture should be sticky but moldable.
Wet hands and shape 12–16 small patties, about 2–2.5 inches wide and 1/2 inch thick. Keep chilled while heating oil.
Stir vinegar, sugar, and salt until dissolved, then toss with cucumber and shallot; set aside. Top with crushed peanuts just before serving.
Heat 1/4 inch frying oil in a skillet over medium heat to 350°F. Fry patties in batches without crowding, 2–3 minutes per side, until deep golden and cooked through to 145°F.
Drain fish cakes on a rack or paper towels. Fry remaining batches, adjusting heat to maintain 350°F.
Serve fish cakes hot with the cucumber relish and cilantro garnish.
tip: Yardlong beans can be swapped with green beans. For extra bounce, beat the paste 1–2 minutes by hand after processing. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; re-crisp in a 375°F oven for 8 minutes.

title: Shrimp Tempura
ing: 1 lb large shrimp (16–20 count), peeled and deveined, tails on
1 cup cake flour, plus 1 tbsp for dusting
steps: Pat shrimp dry. Make 4–5 shallow slits on the belly side to prevent curling, then gently straighten. Lightly dust shrimp with 1 tbsp cake flour and shake off excess.
Make tentsuyu: in a small saucepan combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar; bring to a simmer for 2 minutes, then keep warm.
Heat frying oil in a deep pot to 340–350°F. Line a rack over a sheet pan for draining.
In a chilled bowl, whisk egg with ice-cold sparkling water. Add cake flour, rice flour, baking powder, and salt; stir 8–10 times just to combine. Batter should be lumpy and cold; do not overmix.

Working in batches, dip shrimp by the tail into batter, letting excess drip. Flick a little extra batter onto the oil, then gently slide shrimp in. Fry at 340–350°F for 1 1/2–2 minutes until pale golden.
While frying, occasionally drizzle scant batter over shrimp to create lacey edges. Do not overcrowd; maintain oil temperature between batches.
Remove shrimp to the rack to drain 1 minute. Serve immediately with warm tentsuyu and a spoonful of grated daikon on the side for mixing into the sauce.
Repeat with remaining shrimp, skimming batter bits between batches to keep oil clear; serve hot and crisp.
tip: Keep batter and bowl cold; place over ice if your kitchen is warm. For a veggie platter, fry batons of kabocha, sweet potato, or shiso leaves using the same batter and timing adjusted to thickness.

title: Goan Fish Curry
ing: 1.5 lb firm white fish fillets (kingfish or cod), cut into 2-inch pieces
2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
6 dried Kashmiri red chilies, stems removed
steps: Toast Kashmiri chilies, cumin, coriander, and peppercorns in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant; cool slightly.
Grind toasted spices with turmeric, garlic, ginger, and 2 tbsp water into a smooth paste; set aside.
Soak tamarind paste in 1/2 cup warm water for 5 minutes, then press and strain to get tamarind liquid; discard fibers.
Heat coconut oil with 1 tbsp neutral oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add onions and sauté for 6–8 minutes until lightly golden.
Stir in the spice paste and cook, stirring, for 2–3 minutes until the oil separates and paste smells cooked.
Pour in coconut milk, tamarind liquid, 1/2 cup water, salt, jaggery, and black pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer for 5 minutes.
Slip in fish pieces in a single layer. Simmer gently on low for 6–8 minutes until fish flakes and reaches 145°F at the thickest part.
Rest off heat for 5 minutes to let flavors meld. Adjust salt, jaggery, or tamarind to balance tang and heat; garnish with cilantro before serving.
tip: Kingfish, pomfret, or snapper work well; avoid very delicate fish. Curry improves after a few hours; refrigerate up to 2 days. Reheat gently without boiling to keep fish tender.

title: Carnitas
ing: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch chunks
1 lb pork belly, skin on, cut into 2-inch chunks
1/4 cup white onion, finely chopped, for garnish
steps: Combine pork shoulder and pork belly in a wide, heavy pot in a single layer. Add orange juice, milk, lard, water, salt, pepper, garlic, cinnamon stick, bay leaves, oregano, and onion slices.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce to low so liquid barely bubbles. Cover ajar and simmer for 75 minutes, turning meat every 20 minutes, until tender.
Uncover and increase heat to medium. Cook 25–35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid evaporates and pork cooks in rendered fat.
Fry pork in its fat over medium-high heat 8–12 minutes, turning often, until edges are deeply browned and crisp. Remove cinnamon, bay leaves, and onion.
Check doneness: internal temp should reach 145°F for pork; rest 5 minutes. Break meat into large chunks with tongs; moisten with a spoon of rendered fat.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30–60 seconds per side until pliable.
Serve carnitas in tortillas with chopped onion, cilantro, and lime wedges.
tip: Substitute 2 tbsp brown sugar for milk if avoiding dairy. Carnitas keep 4 days refrigerated; re-crisp in a skillet with a spoon of fat over medium heat 5 minutes.

title: Tacos al Pastor
ing: 8 oz fresh pineapple, sliced into rings
8 oz white onion, sliced, plus 4 oz finely diced
steps: Whisk achiote paste with 1/2 cup pineapple juice, 2 tbsp vinegar, minced garlic, oregano, cumin, black pepper, and 1 tsp salt until smooth to form the marinade.
Toss thinly sliced pork with the marinade; cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour and up to 8 hours, turning once halfway.
Heat a cast-iron skillet over medium-high; add a thin film of frying oil as needed. Sear pineapple rings 2–3 minutes per side until caramelized; chop and reserve.
In the same skillet, cook marinated pork in batches over medium-high, 4–6 minutes total per batch, until lightly charred and cooked through to 145°F; rest 2 minutes, then chop.
Sauté the sliced onion in the skillet 2–3 minutes until just tender and lightly charred; chop and combine with pork and half the chopped pineapple.
Warm corn tortillas directly over a medium flame or in a skillet 30–45 seconds per side until pliable; keep wrapped in a towel.
Assemble tacos: fill tortillas with pork mixture, top with reserved pineapple, finely diced onion, cilantro, and serrano if using. Squeeze lime over each taco.
Serve immediately with extra lime wedges; for street-style, double up tortillas and keep tacos hot covered with a clean towel.
tip: No grill? The cast-iron method still delivers great char. Marinate the pork overnight for deeper flavor; cooked meat keeps 3 days refrigerated. Swap pork shoulder with thin-cut pork loin, adjusting cook time.

title: Tonkatsu
ing: 4 pork loin chops, 1/2-inch thick, pounded to 1/3-inch
steps: Trim fat to an even rim, then lightly score the fat to prevent curling. Pound chops to 1/3-inch. Pat dry and season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper.
Set up dredging: place 1 cup flour in a shallow dish; beat 2 eggs with 2 tbsp milk in another; place 2 cups panko in a third. Dredge pork in flour, shake off excess.
Dip each cutlet in egg, let excess drip, then press into panko, coating fully. Rest breaded cutlets on a rack for 5 minutes to set.
Heat 2 inches frying oil in a deep skillet to 340–350°F over medium heat. Fry 1–2 cutlets at a time, turning once, until golden, 5–6 minutes total.
Check doneness: insert an instant-read thermometer into the center; pork should reach 145°F. Drain on a rack; season lightly with salt while hot.
Return oil to 340–350°F between batches. Skim crumbs as needed to keep oil clear and maintain even browning.
Mound 2 cups shredded cabbage and hot rice onto plates. Slice cutlets crosswise into 3/4-inch strips with a serrated or very sharp knife.
Serve immediately with tonkatsu sauce and lemon wedges on the side; drizzle sauce over pork to taste.
tip: Use fresh panko for the lightest crust. Keep cutlets on a wire rack in a 200°F oven up to 15 minutes to hold. Swap pork with chicken cutlets (cook to 165°F).

title: Char Siu
ing: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 3 long strips
steps: Whisk maltose, 2 tbsp honey, sugar, light soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, oyster sauce, five-spice, sesame oil, salt, white pepper, garlic, and food coloring (optional) until smooth.
Trim excess surface fat from pork. Add pork strips to marinade, turn to coat, cover, and refrigerate for 8 to 24 hours, turning once halfway.
Remove pork 30 minutes before roasting. Heat oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed sheet with foil and set a rack on top; lightly oil the rack.
Arrange pork on rack, reserving marinade. Roast at 425°F for 15 minutes, then baste with marinade.
Reduce oven to 375°F. Continue roasting 20 to 25 minutes, basting every 7 to 8 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 145°F internal.
Simmer remaining marinade in a small saucepan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes to reduce. Off heat, stir in remaining 2 tbsp honey to make glaze.
Brush pork all over with warm glaze and return to oven 3 minutes to set. Rest 10 minutes, then slice across the grain into 1/4-inch pieces.
Optional finish: briefly char edges under the broiler on high for 1 to 2 minutes, watching closely, then re-glaze lightly before serving.
tip: Pork butt/shoulder gives classic succulence; pork belly works but is richer. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; rewarm gently and re-glaze with a touch of honey for shine.

title: Pulled Pork Sandwiches
ing: 2 lb pork shoulder, trimmed of excess surface fat
4 brioche hamburger buns, split and toasted
steps: Mix salt, brown sugar, paprika, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, ground mustard, and cayenne; rub all over pork shoulder and let sit 20 minutes at room temperature.
Heat a heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium-high and add frying oil as needed; sear pork on all sides until browned, about 8 minutes total.
Add chicken broth and apple cider vinegar; bring to a simmer, cover, then cook at a gentle simmer over low heat for 3 to 3 1/2 hours until fork-tender and 195–205°F internal.
Transfer pork to a board; rest 15 minutes. Skim fat from pot juices and reduce liquid over medium heat for 5 minutes to concentrate flavor.
Shred pork with two forks, discarding large fat pieces; return meat to pot with reduced juices and stir in 1/2 cup barbecue sauce. Simmer 5 minutes to meld.
Taste and adjust seasoning with a pinch of salt or vinegar if needed; keep warm over low heat for serving.
Spread remaining barbecue sauce on toasted buns, pile pork onto each bun, and top with coleslaw.
Serve immediately while hot, with extra sauce on the side.
tip: Pork can be cooked in a 300°F oven, covered, 3 1/2 to 4 hours. Make ahead: cool, refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat with a splash of broth. Substitute cider for broth for a sweeter profile.

title: Cochinita Pibil
ing: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 3-inch chunks
1 large banana leaf, rinsed and softened
1 cup pickled red onions, for garnish
steps: Soften banana leaf by passing over medium flame for 10–15 seconds per section until glossy and pliable; set aside. If unavailable, use a double layer of heavy foil.
Blend sour orange juice, vinegar, achiote paste, ancho powder, cumin, oregano, 1 tsp kosher salt, 1/2 tsp pepper, and garlic until smooth, 30 seconds.
Pat pork dry. Heat frying oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high. Sear pork in batches until well browned, 6–8 minutes total; transfer to a plate.
Lay banana leaf in pot, overlapping to line sides. Scatter half the sliced onion, add pork with any juices, pour in marinade, and top with remaining onion.
Fold banana leaf over pork to seal. Cover pot with lid. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium, then reduce to low and cook covered for 2 hours, maintaining a gentle burble.
Transfer pot to a 325°F oven and braise until pork is very tender and shreds easily, 60–75 minutes. Pork should reach 195–205°F for shredding.
Uncover, discard leaf, and shred pork in juices. Simmer uncovered over medium for 5–8 minutes to thicken. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Serve cochinita pibil hot with pickled red onions and lime wedges. Offer warm tortillas if desired.
tip: No sour orange? Use 1/3 cup fresh orange juice + 3 tbsp lime juice. Make ahead: cool and refrigerate in juices up to 3 days; reheat gently with a splash of water.

title: Porchetta
ing: 3 lb pork belly, skin-on, butterflied to 1/2-inch and squared
steps: Pat pork belly and loin dry. Mix kosher salt, black pepper, fennel seeds, red pepper flakes, rosemary, sage, garlic, lemon zest, and olive oil into a paste; set aside.
Score belly skin in a 1/2-inch crosshatch without cutting into meat. Flip, spread paste evenly over belly’s meat side. Place loin down the center; roll belly tightly around loin.
Tie roast every 1 to 1.5 inches with kitchen twine. Mix baking powder with white wine vinegar; rub lightly over the skin to promote crisping. Refrigerate uncovered for 1 hour.
Heat oven to 325°F. Set roast seam-side down on a rack over a rimmed pan. Roast at 325°F for 1 hour 45 minutes, basting once with pan drippings.
Add white wine and chicken stock to the pan. Continue roasting at 325°F until an instant-read thermometer in the loin reads 145°F, about 20 to 30 minutes more.
Increase oven to 475°F and roast until skin blisters and turns glassy-crisp, 10 to 15 minutes, rotating pan once. Rest uncovered 20 minutes on a board.
Skim fat from pan juices; reduce in a saucepan over medium heat to a syrupy jus, 5 to 8 minutes. Slice porchetta into 1/2-inch rounds and spoon jus over.
Serve warm with bitter greens or crusty bread; reserve extra crackling for garnish to keep it crisp.
tip: Sub pork shoulder for loin if preferred; cook until 195°F in the shoulder portion for shreddable texture. Leftovers keep 4 days refrigerated; re-crisp slices at 425°F for 8 to 10 minutes.

title: Katsudon
ing: 1 lb pork loin cutlets, 4 pieces, 1/2-inch thick
1 sheet nori, thinly sliced for garnish, as needed
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then combine 2 cups rice with 2 1/4 cups water in a pot. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes; rest covered 10 minutes.
Pound pork cutlets to even 1/2-inch thickness. Pat dry and season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper.
Set up dredging: place 1/2 cup flour in one dish, 2 beaten eggs in a second, and 1 cup panko in a third. Dredge pork in flour, dip in egg, then coat thoroughly in panko.

Heat 1/2 inch frying oil in a skillet to 350°F. Fry cutlets 3–4 minutes per side until golden and an instant-read thermometer reads 145°F. Drain on a rack and rest 3 minutes; slice into 3/4-inch strips.
In a 10-inch skillet, combine 1 cup dashi, 1/4 cup soy sauce, 3 tbsp mirin, 1 tbsp sugar, and 1 thinly sliced onion. Simmer over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until onions are tender.

Divide the onion-broth mixture into two batches if using a single skillet. Add sliced cutlet to the simmering onions, pour 1/4 of the lightly beaten eggs over, cover, and cook 45–60 seconds until just set but still custardy.
Repeat with remaining cutlets and egg, keeping finished portions warm. Eggs should be softly set; avoid overcooking for authentic texture.
Scoop hot rice into 4 bowls. Slide the pork-egg-onion mixture over each, spooning some broth on top. Garnish with scallions and nori to taste.
tip: Substitute store-bought dashi (granules) per package if needed. Fry katsu ahead and re-crisp at 375°F for 5–7 minutes; assemble with fresh egg-onion simmer just before serving.

title: Gua Bao (Pork Belly Buns)
ing: 1.5 lb pork belly, skin-on slab, cut into 1-inch slices
2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
1/2 cup rice wine (michiu) or Shaoxing wine
1/3 cup rock sugar or granulated sugar
1/2 cup quick-pickled mustard greens (suan cai), rinsed and chopped
steps: Pat pork belly dry and slice into 1-inch pieces. Heat a heavy pot over medium and add 1 tbsp oil. Sear pork until lightly browned, 4–6 minutes, rendering some fat. Spoon off excess fat if needed.
Add ginger, garlic, scallion, and star anise; sauté until fragrant, 1 minute. Stir in light soy, dark soy, rice wine, sugar, and 1 cup water. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce to a bare simmer, cover, and braise over low heat for 75–90 minutes until pork belly is very tender. Flip pieces once or twice. Uncover and simmer 10–15 minutes to reduce to a glossy sauce.
Skim fat. Season with white pepper to taste. Keep warm over low heat; sauce should lightly coat the pork. If too salty, add a splash of water and simmer 2 minutes.
Set a steamer over simmering water. Steam bao buns until hot and fluffy, 5–7 minutes. Keep covered so they don’t dry out.
Assemble: Open each bun, spread a spoonful of braising sauce inside, add 2–3 pieces of pork belly, then top with mustard greens, crushed peanuts, and cilantro.
Serve immediately while hot, passing extra sauce, peanuts, and greens at the table for customizing.
Optional crisping: For a firmer edge, pan-sear a few pork pieces in 1 tsp oil over medium-high for 30–45 seconds per side, then dip back in sauce before assembling.
tip: Suan cai substitute: quick-pickle chopped mustard greens or napa with salt and a splash of rice vinegar. Leftover pork keeps 3 days refrigerated; rewarm gently with a splash of water.

title: Lechon Kawali
steps: Rinse 2 lb pork belly under cold water and pat dry. In a pot, combine 8 cups water, 1 tbsp kosher salt, 1 tsp peppercorns, 4 smashed garlic cloves, 2 bay leaves, and 1 tbsp vinegar.

Add pork belly, skin side up, and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook covered for 45 to 60 minutes until tender but not falling apart and pork reaches at least 145°F internally.
Remove pork and drain well. Pat very dry, especially the skin. Place on a rack set over a tray, skin side up, and chill uncovered for 1 to 2 hours to dry the skin thoroughly.
Score or prick the skin all over with a fork or skewer. Season meat side with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper to taste. Cut slab into 2- to 3-inch wide strips for easier frying.

Heat 2 cups frying oil in a deep, heavy skillet to 325°F over medium heat. Carefully add pork pieces, skin side down, and fry for 8 to 10 minutes until lightly golden; maintain 300–325°F. Remove and drain.
Let pork rest 10 minutes. Increase oil to 375°F. Return pork and fry 3 to 5 minutes more until skin blistered, very crisp, and deep golden brown.
Transfer to a rack and rest 5 minutes. Slice into bite-size pieces. Ensure finished pork is 165°F at thickest part for safety.
Serve hot with dipping sauce if desired (toyomansi or spiced vinegar).
tip: For extra crackle, air-dry the boiled pork in the fridge overnight. Leftovers keep 3 days chilled; re-crisp in a 400°F oven for 8–10 minutes.

title: BBQ Baby Back Ribs
ing: 2 racks baby back ribs, membrane removed
1 tbsp chopped parsley, for garnish, as needed
steps: Heat oven to 300°F. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil and set a wire rack inside; lightly oil the rack.
Pat ribs dry. Stir brown sugar, salt, pepper, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne. Rub all over both sides of ribs.
Place ribs meat side up on rack. Pour apple cider into the pan (not on ribs). Cover tightly with foil and bake at 300°F for 2 hours 15 minutes.
Remove foil. Carefully transfer ribs to a clean foil-lined sheet; discard pan juices. Increase oven to 450°F.
Stir barbecue sauce, apple cider vinegar, mustard, and Worcestershire. Brush a thin coat on ribs.
Return ribs to oven and roast at 450°F for 10 minutes. Brush again and roast 10 minutes more until lacquered and lightly charred.
Rest ribs 10 minutes. Slice between bones and brush with any remaining warm sauce.
Serve hot, garnished with parsley.
tip: Swap apple cider with 1 cup water plus 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar. Ribs can be baked covered a day ahead; cool, cover, and refrigerate. Glaze and roast at 450°F for 15 minutes to reheat and caramelize.

title: Bánh Mì Thịt
steps: Make quick pickle: combine 1/2 cup rice vinegar, 1/3 cup water, 2 tbsp sugar, and 1/2 tsp salt in a bowl; stir to dissolve. Add 1 cup carrots and 1 cup daikon; toss and chill for at least 30 minutes.

Marinate pork: mix 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 2 tsp sesame oil, 2 cloves minced garlic, and 1 tsp black pepper. Add 1 lb thin-sliced pork; toss and marinate 20–30 minutes.
Sear pork: heat 2 tbsp frying oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook pork in batches 5–7 minutes total until browned and juices run clear, 145°F; rest 5 minutes.
Warm rolls: heat oven to 350°F. Bake 4 banh mi rolls directly on rack for 5–7 minutes until crisp outside and soft inside; cool 2 minutes, then split lengthwise without cutting through.
Prepare spreads: mix 1/2 cup mayonnaise with a spoon to loosen. Have 2 tbsp pâté ready at room temperature for easy spreading.
Assemble: spread mayo on both cut sides of each roll; smear about 1/2 tbsp pâté per side. Layer warm pork along the bottom of each roll.
Add pickles and veg: drain carrot-daikon pickle well. Add cucumbers, a generous handful of pickles, cilantro sprigs, and jalapeño slices to each sandwich.
Finish and serve: press gently to compact. Serve immediately while bread is crisp and fillings are cool-warm contrasted.
tip: Sub pork shoulder with pork belly for richer flavor. Pickles keep 1 week refrigerated in brine; drain before using for best texture.

title: Mapo Tofu
ing: 12 oz soft tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 tbsp doubanjiang (Pixian broad bean chili paste)
1 tbsp douchi (fermented black beans), rinsed and chopped
1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
2 tsp chili flakes (facing heaven), or to taste
2 tsp cornstarch, mixed with 2 tbsp water
2 scallions, white and green parts sliced, divided
steps: Bring a medium pot of water to a simmer over medium heat. Slip in tofu cubes and gently simmer for 2 minutes to firm; drain carefully and set aside.
Heat 2 tbsp frying oil in a wok over medium heat until shimmering. Add doubanjiang and stir-fry for 60–90 seconds until the oil turns red and aromatic.
Add ground pork and cook, breaking up, until no longer pink and slightly crisp, about 4–5 minutes; splash in Shaoxing wine and cook 30 seconds.
Stir in douchi, garlic, ginger, and chili flakes; fry 30–45 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to burn.
Pour in chicken stock, soy sauce, and sugar; bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to a brisk simmer for 2 minutes.
Gently add tofu cubes and swirl the wok to coat without breaking. Simmer for 4–5 minutes to let flavors penetrate.
Stir cornstarch slurry, then drizzle it in while gently stirring; simmer 1–2 minutes until the sauce is glossy and clings to tofu.
Turn off heat. Sprinkle in ground Sichuan peppercorns and most of the scallion greens; swirl to combine. Plate and finish with remaining scallions.
tip: Use medium tofu for a firmer bite. Substitute chicken for pork if desired. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; reheat gently with a splash of stock.

title: Twice-Cooked Pork
ing: 4 oz Sichuan ya cai (preserved mustard greens), rinsed and drained
6 oz leeks or Chinese garlic chives, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 tbsp doubanjiang (Pixian broad bean chili paste)
1 tbsp douchi (fermented black beans), rinsed and chopped
steps: Place pork belly, water, and Shaoxing wine in a pot, bring to a boil, then simmer over medium-low for 25–30 minutes until just cooked through (internal temp 145°F). Cool 10 minutes in liquid.
Remove pork, pat dry, and chill 15 minutes to firm. Slice across the grain into thin 1/8-inch slices; reserve 1/4 cup cooking liquid.
Heat a wok over medium-high until smoking, add pork slices dry, and render, stir-frying 3–4 minutes until edges curl and fat releases; push meat to the rim.
Add 2 tbsp oil if needed, then doubanjiang and douchi to the center. Stir-fry the pastes 45–60 seconds until brick red and fragrant without burning.
Add ginger and garlic, stir-fry 20 seconds. Return pork to the center, toss to coat evenly in sauce.
Stir in light soy, dark soy, sugar, and 2–3 tbsp reserved pork broth to loosen. Stir-fry 1 minute until glossy and clinging.
Add ya cai and leeks, stir-fry 1–2 minutes until leeks are just tender but bright; splash in black vinegar and toss 10 seconds.
Season with ground Sichuan peppercorn and white pepper to taste. Serve immediately with steamed rice.
tip: Ya cai is traditional; if unavailable, use finely chopped Tianjin preserved vegetable. Keep pork slices thin for best texture; leftovers reheat well in a hot wok for 1–2 minutes.

title: Choucroute Garnie
ing: 8 oz slab bacon, cut into 2-inch pieces
12 oz smoked pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
12 oz smoked kielbasa, cut into 3-inch lengths
1 tbsp Dijon mustard, plus more for serving
steps: Rinse sauerkraut under cold water 10 to 20 seconds to soften acidity, then squeeze dry. Fluff with fingers to separate strands and set aside.
Warm a large heavy pot over medium heat, add oil as needed, and brown slab bacon and smoked pork shoulder until lightly golden, 6 to 8 minutes. Transfer meats to a plate; leave rendered fat in pot.

Add onion and garlic to pot and cook until translucent, 5 minutes. Stir in sauerkraut, juniper, peppercorns, bay leaves, Riesling, and stock. Nestle browned meats into sauerkraut, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for 60 minutes.
Add whole potatoes on top of sauerkraut. Cover and simmer until potatoes are just tender, 20 to 25 minutes.
Prick bratwurst and kielbasa once each to prevent bursting. Nestle bratwurst and kielbasa into pot, cover, and simmer gently until heated through, 15 minutes.
Add frankfurters on top, cover, and simmer until all sausages are hot and pork shoulder is fork-tender, 10 to 12 minutes more. Keep heat low to avoid boiling, which toughens meats.
Stir Dijon into cooking juices, taste, and season sauerkraut with salt to taste. Remove bay leaves and arrange sauerkraut on a warm platter, topping with all meats and potatoes.
Serve hot with additional Dijon and, if desired, a drizzle of warm cooking juices. Keep platter covered in a low oven at 200°F up to 20 minutes before serving.
tip: Swap Riesling with dry Sylvaner if preferred. Leftovers reheat gently with a splash of stock; keeps 3 days refrigerated. Serve with good mustard and rye or country bread.

title: Pork Chops with Apples
ing: 4 bone-in pork chops, about 1 in thick (8–10 oz each)
2 medium tart apples, cored and sliced 1/2 in thick
steps: Pat pork chops dry; season both sides with 1 tsp kosher salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper.
Heat 2 tbsp frying oil in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering; sear chops 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium; add 1 tbsp butter, onion, and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring, until translucent and lightly browned, 5–6 minutes.
Add apple slices and 1 tbsp thyme; cook, stirring, until edges soften and caramelize, 4–5 minutes.
Stir in 1/2 cup apple cider and 1/2 cup chicken broth; scrape browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Whisk in 1 tsp Dijon and 1 tsp apple cider vinegar. Nestle chops and any juices into the skillet; reduce heat to medium-low.
Cover and cook at a bare simmer until apples are tender and chops reach 145°F in the thickest part, 5–8 minutes.
Uncover; spoon sauce over chops and let rest off heat 3 minutes. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste before serving.
tip: Use firm-tart apples like Granny Smith, Honeycrisp, or Braeburn. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; rewarm gently with a splash of broth to loosen the sauce.

title: Lamb Kofta
ing: 1/3 cup yellow onion, very finely grated and well-drained
2 cloves garlic, minced to a paste
steps: Combine lamb, grated onion (squeezed dry), parsley, mint, cilantro, cumin, coriander, allspice, paprika, cinnamon, salt, pepper, garlic, and olive oil in a bowl. Mix gently until just uniform, 30–45 seconds.
Cover and chill the mixture for 15 minutes to firm slightly; meanwhile, preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high (about 425°F). Lightly oil grates with frying oil.
Divide mixture into 8 portions (about 3 oz each). With wet hands, shape each onto a metal skewer or into oval patties about 3/4 inch thick.
Grill kofta over medium-high heat, turning every 2–3 minutes, until well-browned and an instant-read thermometer in the center reaches 160°F, 8–10 minutes total.
Rest kofta 3 minutes off heat to reabsorb juices. Warm flatbreads briefly on the grill, 15–30 seconds per side.
Serve kofta hot with warmed flatbreads and your preferred accompaniments.
tip: For stovetop, sear in a lightly oiled cast-iron skillet over medium-high, then finish to 160°F. Make ahead: shape up to 1 day in advance; keep chilled and uncovered 1 hour, then cover.

title: Moroccan Lamb Tagine with Apricots
ing: 2 lb lamb shoulder, trimmed and cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks
2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
steps: Warm 2 tbsp olive oil in a heavy pot or tagine over medium heat until shimmering, then brown lamb in 2 batches, 6–8 minutes per batch; transfer to a plate, leaving fond in the pot.

Add onion and a pinch of salt; cook over medium heat, stirring, until golden, 8–10 minutes. Stir in garlic, cumin, coriander, ginger, paprika, cinnamon, turmeric, and cloves; toast 45–60 seconds until fragrant.
Return lamb and any juices. Season with 1 1/4 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Pour in 1 cup chicken broth and 1 cup water; scrape up browned bits and bring to a simmer.
Cover tightly and cook at a gentle simmer over low heat until lamb is very tender, 75–90 minutes, stirring once or twice. Maintain a bare simmer; add a splash of water if needed.
Stir in dried apricots and 1 tbsp honey; simmer uncovered over low heat until sauce slightly thickens and apricots soften, 10–12 minutes.
Skim excess fat. Stir in 1 tbsp lemon juice; adjust salt and pepper. Ensure lamb is at least 145°F for safety, then rest off heat 5 minutes.
Scatter toasted almonds over the tagine and top with chopped cilantro and parsley. Serve hot with couscous or crusty bread.
tip: Swap apricots for prunes or a mix for deeper sweetness. Make ahead: cool and chill up to 2 days; flavors improve. Reheat gently with a splash of water.
