title: Herb-Crusted Rack of Lamb
steps: Heat oven to 450°F. Pat lamb dry, trim excess surface fat, and season all over with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper.

Warm a skillet over medium-high, add frying oil as needed, and sear lamb fat-side down first until well browned, 2–3 minutes per side. Transfer to a rack over a rimmed sheet, fat-side up; cool 5 minutes.
Mix breadcrumbs, parsley, rosemary, thyme, garlic, lemon zest, remaining 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp pepper, and olive oil until evenly moistened.
Brush Dijon thinly over the lamb’s fat cap and upper sides. Press crumb mixture onto the mustard-coated areas to form an even crust.
Roast at 450°F for 12–15 minutes, then reduce oven to 350°F and continue roasting until an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 125–130°F for medium-rare, about 8–12 minutes more.
Rest lamb on a warm platter, loosely tented with foil, for 10 minutes to allow juices to redistribute; temperature will rise to 130–135°F.
Slice between the bones into chops and arrange on a warmed plate. Spoon any juices from the pan over the meat and serve immediately.
tip: Use panko if breadcrumbs are dry; add 1 tsp olive oil if mixture looks sandy. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; rewarm gently at 300°F, 8–10 minutes.

title: Mansaf
ing: 2 lb bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into large chunks
3 cups long-grain rice, rinsed and soaked 20 minutes
2 loaves shrak or markook bread, as needed
steps: Soak 2 cups jameed in hot water for 30 minutes, then blend with soaking liquid until pourable and smooth; set aside.
Add lamb, water, and onion to a pot. Bring to a boil, skim foam, reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 60 minutes until lamb is tender and reaches 145°F.
Strain broth; discard onion. Return lamb to pot. Stir in blended jameed, turmeric, cumin, pepper, and salt. Simmer very gently for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.

Rinse soaked rice until water runs clear. Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a pot over medium; add rice and 1 tsp salt, stir 1 minute. Add 4 cups hot lamb broth, bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat, and cook for 12 minutes. Rest off heat 10 minutes, then fluff.
Warm shrak or markook bread over a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side until pliable. Arrange 1–2 loaves on a large platter, letting edges overhang.
Spoon some hot jameed sauce over bread to moisten. Mound rice in the center, then arrange lamb pieces on top. Ladle more sauce over lamb and rice to generously coat.
Melt remaining 1 tbsp ghee; toss with toasted almonds and pine nuts. Scatter nuts and chopped parsley over the top.
Serve immediately, passing extra hot jameed sauce on the side so diners can add more to taste.
tip: If jameed stones are very hard, soak overnight; adjust thickness with hot broth. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; reheat sauce gently with a splash of broth to loosen.

title: Lamb Keema
ing: 1 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/4 tsp black pepper, or to taste
steps: Warm 2 tbsp oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat until shimmering, then add 2 tsp cumin seeds and bloom until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add 1 cup finely chopped onion and cook, stirring, until deep golden brown, 8 to 10 minutes. Add 2 tsp grated ginger and 3 cloves minced garlic; sauté 1 minute.
Crumble in 1 lb ground lamb; cook over medium-high, breaking up, until no pink remains and moisture reduces, 6 to 8 minutes. Spoon off excess fat if needed.
Sprinkle 1 tsp ground coriander, 1 tsp Kashmiri chili, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp black pepper; stir 30 seconds to coat the meat.
Stir in 1 cup finely diced tomato and cook until they break down and the oil separates at the edges, 5 to 7 minutes.
Pour in 1/2 cup water, bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low and cover; simmer for 8 minutes for flavors to meld.
Stir in 1 cup frozen peas; simmer uncovered until peas are tender and keema is thick but saucy, 3 to 4 minutes. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Finish with 1 tbsp lemon juice and 1/4 cup chopped cilantro. Serve hot with roti, naan, or rice.
tip: Sub green chilies for heat or add 1 tsp paprika for milder color. Keema keeps 3 days refrigerated; reheat gently with a splash of water. Swap peas for diced potatoes; simmer until tender.

title: Kleftiko
ing: 3 lb bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into large pieces
1 lb yellow potatoes, peeled and quartered
6 oz feta cheese, cut into chunks
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Heat oven to 325°F. Cut four large sheets of parchment and foil to fully wrap the lamb into a sealed parcel (foil outside, parchment inside).
In a large bowl, combine lamb, potatoes, onion, garlic, lemon zest and juice, olive oil, white wine, oregano, thyme, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Toss until everything is well coated.
Lay parchment over foil in a roasting pan. Pile the lamb and vegetables in the center, scraping in all juices. Scatter feta and tomatoes over the top.
Fold parchment tightly over the filling, then seal with foil to create a completely enclosed package to trap steam.
Bake at 325°F for 2 hours without opening. Increase oven to 375°F and bake 30 minutes more to deepen browning and tenderize.
Carefully open the parcel—steam is hot. Check lamb is very tender and at least 145°F in the thickest pieces. Spoon juices over the meat and potatoes.
Return uncovered to the oven at 375°F for 10 minutes to slightly reduce the juices and set the feta.
Rest 5 minutes. Transfer to a platter with all juices. Garnish with parsley and serve immediately.
tip: Add bell pepper wedges with the tomatoes if you like. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat covered at 325°F with a splash of water.

title: Lamb Shawarma
steps: Whisk yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, vinegar, salt, cumin, coriander, allspice, paprika, cinnamon, black pepper, cardamom, garlic, and cayenne in a bowl until smooth.
Toss lamb slices and onion with the marinade until well coated; cover and refrigerate for at least 45 minutes and up to 12 hours.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high until lightly smoking, add frying oil, and sear lamb in batches 3–4 minutes per side until browned; cook to 145°F for medium and up to 160°F for well.
Return all lamb to pan, reduce heat to medium, and cook 2–3 minutes to glaze with rendered juices; rest off heat 5 minutes, then slice any larger pieces thinly.
Warm pita at 350°F for 5–7 minutes or over a skillet 1–2 minutes per side until pliable.
Assemble shawarma: pile lamb into pita, add tomatoes and parsley, and drizzle with tahini sauce; season with salt and pepper to taste.
For a plate-style serving, spoon lamb over rice or fries, add tomatoes and parsley, and drizzle tahini; serve immediately.
tip: For oven method, spread marinated lamb on a sheet at 425°F for 15–18 min, then broil 1–3 min to char. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat in a hot skillet to re-crisp.

title: Slow-Roasted Lamb Shoulder
steps: Heat oven to 325°F. Pat lamb dry. Rub with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Using a small knife, make 10–12 slits and tuck in garlic slices, rosemary, and thyme.
Scatter onions and carrots in a roasting pan. Set lamb shoulder on top, fat side up. Pour wine and stock into the pan; do not pour over the meat.
Cover pan tightly with foil and roast at 325°F for 2 hours. Uncover, baste, and continue roasting uncovered for 1 hour, basting every 20 minutes.
Increase oven to 425°F and roast a final 20–30 minutes until the exterior is well browned and the lamb is fork-tender; internal temp should reach at least 145°F.
Transfer lamb to a board, tent with foil, and rest for 20 minutes. Skim excess fat from the pan, reserving 1 tbsp for the gravy.
Set pan over medium heat. Mash vegetables slightly. Stir in Dijon. Sprinkle flour over vegetables and cook 2 minutes, stirring.
Whisk in reserved fat, then gradually add 1 cup hot water, simmer for 5–7 minutes until thick. Strain into a saucepan, pressing on solids; whisk in butter and lemon juice. Season to taste.
Carve or pull the lamb into large pieces and serve with the pan gravy.
tip: Swap white wine with 1 cup extra stock if preferred. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat covered with a splash of stock at 300°F until warmed through.

title: Lamb Chops with Mint Sauce
ing: 8 lamb rib chops, about 1 in thick
1/2 cup fresh mint leaves, finely chopped
steps: Pat lamb chops dry, rub with olive oil, then season evenly with kosher salt and black pepper on both sides.
Make the mint sauce: in a heatproof bowl combine chopped mint, white wine vinegar, and granulated sugar. Pour in boiling water, stir until sugar dissolves, and let steep for 10 minutes.
Heat a heavy skillet or grill pan over medium-high until very hot, about 2 minutes. Sear chops 3 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until an instant-read thermometer reads 130–135°F.
Rest chops on a warm plate, tented loosely with foil, for 5 minutes to reach 135–140°F. Skim any excess fat from the pan if desired.
Stir the mint sauce, taste, and adjust sweetness or sharpness with a pinch more sugar or vinegar if needed.
Serve lamb chops warm with spoonfuls of mint sauce over or alongside.
tip: For medium doneness, cook to 140–145°F, about 4 minutes per side. Sauce keeps 1 week refrigerated; refresh with a few torn mint leaves before serving.

title: Maqluba
ing: 2 cups basmati rice, rinsed until clear, soaked 30 minutes
1 lemon, cut in wedges, for serving
steps: Pat lamb dry, season with 1/2 tsp salt and black pepper. Heat 2 tbsp frying oil in a heavy 4–5 qt pot over medium-high. Brown lamb on all sides, 6–8 minutes. Remove to a plate; pour off excess fat.

Add onion rings to pot with a drizzle of oil; cook until lightly golden, 5–6 minutes. Return lamb, add stock, turmeric, cumin, allspice, cinnamon, and 3/4 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 35–40 minutes until lamb is tender.

While lamb simmers, heat 1/4 inch frying oil in a skillet to 375°F. Fry eggplant rounds until deep golden, 2–3 minutes per side; drain on paper towels. Fry cauliflower florets until golden, 3–4 minutes; drain. Lightly salt vegetables.
Toast pine nuts in a dry skillet over medium heat until golden, 2–3 minutes; set aside. Drain soaked rice well.

Strain lamb broth to measure 3 cups liquid; add water if needed. Return lamb and onions to the clean pot. Layer half the eggplant and cauliflower over lamb, then all the rice, then the remaining vegetables on top. Press gently to level.
Pour the 3 cups hot broth over rice to just cover; do not stir. Bring to a lively simmer over medium heat. Cover, reduce to low, and cook 30 minutes. Turn off heat and let steam, covered, 15 minutes.
Loosen edges with a knife. Invert a wide platter over the pot; using oven mitts, flip pot and platter together. Rest 2 minutes, then lift pot to unmold the maqluba.
Sprinkle with toasted pine nuts and parsley. Serve hot with lemon wedges. Ensure lamb pieces are at least 145°F; broth should have fully absorbed and rice tender.
tip: For lighter prep, brush eggplant/cauliflower with oil and roast at 425°F until golden. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat covered with a splash of broth to revive rice.

title: Shepherd's Pie
ing: 2 lb russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Place potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch, add a pinch of salt, bring to a boil, then simmer for 12–15 minutes until fork-tender.
Drain potatoes well. Mash with butter and warmed milk until smooth; season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add lamb, cook 6–8 minutes, breaking up, until browned and no pink remains; drain excess fat, leaving about 1 tbsp.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook 6–8 minutes until softened. Stir in garlic and tomato paste; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beef stock and Worcestershire; add thyme, 1/2 tsp salt, and pepper. Simmer for 5–7 minutes until slightly thickened. Stir in peas and remove from heat.
Spread lamb mixture in a 2-quart baking dish. Spoon mashed potatoes on top, smoothing to edges to seal. Rough up the surface with a fork for browning.
Bake at 400°F for 20–25 minutes until bubbling at edges and potatoes lightly golden. For deeper color, broil 1–2 minutes, watching closely.
Rest 10 minutes before serving so layers set and juices settle.
tip: Swap lamb for beef to make cottage pie. Filling can be made 2 days ahead; chill, then top with potatoes and bake, adding 5–10 minutes to heat through.

title: Chana Masala
ing: 1/2 cup chickpea cooking liquid or water
steps: Warm 2 tbsp oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and toast until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add onion and a pinch of salt; cook, stirring, until deep golden brown, 10 to 12 minutes. Add ginger and garlic; sauté until raw smell fades, 1 minute.
Stir in tomatoes; cook down until jammy and oil separates at edges, 6 to 8 minutes.
Add coriander, turmeric, Kashmiri chili, and 1/2 tsp salt; cook spices in the tomato base for 1 minute, stirring.
Add chickpeas and 1/2 cup chickpea liquid or water; bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Lightly mash a few chickpeas with the back of a spoon to thicken; simmer 3 more minutes to desired gravy consistency.
Stir in garam masala, amchur, and lemon juice; simmer 1 minute, then taste and adjust salt to taste.
Turn off heat, rest 2 minutes, then garnish with chopped cilantro and serve hot with rice or bhatura.
tip: Swap amchur with 1 tsp pomegranate powder or 2 tsp lemon juice. For make-ahead, cook through step 6; cool and refrigerate 3 days, then reheat and finish with garam masala and amchur.

title: Palak Paneer
steps: Blanch spinach: Boil 6 cups water, add spinach, cook 2 minutes until just wilted. Shock in ice water 2 minutes, drain well, then blend to a smooth puree with 1/4 cup water.
Optional paneer sear: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium; sear paneer 2–3 minutes, turning until lightly golden. Set aside on a plate.
Make masala: In the same pan, heat 2 tbsp ghee over medium. Add onion and cook 7–8 minutes until golden. Add ginger, garlic, and green chili; sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Spice and tomato: Stir in turmeric, coriander, cumin, and Kashmiri chili; toast 30 seconds. Add tomato puree and cook 4–5 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy and ghee separates.
Fold in spinach: Add spinach puree and 1/2 cup water; simmer over medium-low for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until the raw greens taste cooks off. Season with salt to taste.
Finish: Stir in cream and garam masala; simmer 1 minute. Gently fold in paneer and warm 2–3 minutes on low. Adjust consistency with a splash of hot water if too thick.
Rest and serve: Turn off heat, cover, and rest 2 minutes for flavors to meld. Serve hot with roti, naan, or basmati rice.
tip: For vegan, swap paneer with firm tofu and ghee/cream with oil/cashew cream. Blanching and shocking spinach preserves color; don’t overcook after adding cream to keep it vibrant.

title: Dal Tadka
ing: 1 cup toor dal (split pigeon peas), rinsed
steps: Combine toor dal, water, and turmeric in a pot; bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook until dal is soft and mushes easily, about 25 to 30 minutes.
Whisk the cooked dal vigorously or use a spoon to mash until creamy; stir in salt and keep warm on low heat. If too thick, add hot water 2 tbsp at a time to reach a pourable, soupy consistency.
Heat ghee with a little frying oil in a medium skillet over medium heat until shimmering, 2 minutes. Add cumin seeds and dried red chilies; let sizzle until fragrant, about 20 seconds.
Stir in onion; cook, stirring, until translucent and lightly golden, 6 to 8 minutes. Add garlic and ginger; sauté until the raw smell fades, about 45 seconds.
Add tomato, Kashmiri red chili powder, and garam masala; cook, stirring, until tomatoes break down and the fat separates from the sides, 4 to 5 minutes.
Pour the entire tempering into the pot of dal; stir well and simmer together on low for 5 minutes to meld flavors, adjusting salt as needed.
Stir in lemon juice, then take off heat. Rest 2 minutes for flavors to settle.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and an optional drizzle of hot ghee; serve hot with steamed rice or roti.
tip: Swap: use 1/2 cup toor dal + 1/2 cup moong dal for a lighter taste. Make-ahead: Cook dal base up to 3 days ahead; reheat with a splash of water and add fresh tadka just before serving.

title: Eggplant Parmesan
ing: 8 oz fresh mozzarella, thinly sliced and patted dry
steps: Lay eggplant slices on racks, sprinkle both sides with 1 tbsp kosher salt, and let purge for 30 minutes. Rinse and pat very dry with towels.

Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a saucepan over medium. Add onion and cook 5 minutes until translucent; add garlic 30 seconds. Stir in crushed tomatoes, oregano, and red pepper flakes; simmer for 20 minutes, then season to taste.
Heat frying oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Working in batches, pan-fry eggplant until golden and tender, 3 to 4 minutes per side, adding oil as needed. Drain on paper towels.
Heat oven to 375°F. Lightly oil a 9x13-inch baking dish. Spoon a thin layer of sauce in the bottom.

Layer eggplant to cover, slightly overlapping. Top with sauce, a scattering of Parmigiano-Reggiano, a few mozzarella slices, and torn basil. Repeat 2 more layers, finishing with sauce and cheeses on top.
Cover loosely with foil and bake at 375°F for 25 minutes. Uncover and bake until bubbling and lightly browned, 15 to 20 minutes more.
Rest 15 minutes before slicing to set layers. Grind black pepper to taste and garnish with extra basil if desired.
tip: To avoid sogginess, dry mozzarella well and let the baked dish rest before slicing. Sauce and fried eggplant can be made a day ahead; assemble and bake before serving.

title: Mushroom Risotto
ing: 1 tbsp olive oil, as needed, for frying
steps: Warm 6 cups vegetable stock in a saucepan over low heat and keep at a bare simmer for the duration of cooking.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil and 2 tbsp butter in a wide heavy pot over medium heat. Add mushrooms and cook, stirring, until browned and their liquid evaporates, 6 to 8 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.
Add remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the pot. Stir in onion with a pinch of salt and cook over medium heat until translucent, 4 to 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in Arborio rice and cook, stirring constantly, until edges look translucent, about 2 minutes. Pour in white wine and simmer, stirring, until almost absorbed, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add 1/2 to 3/4 cup hot stock and stir gently, maintaining a brisk simmer. When mostly absorbed, repeat additions, 1 ladle at a time, stirring often, 18 to 20 minutes total.
When rice is al dente and creamy, fold in cooked mushrooms. Add a final splash of stock to achieve a fluid, spoonable consistency; simmer 1 minute.
Off heat, vigorously beat in 1 tbsp butter and 1/2 cup grated Parmigiano-Reggiano until glossy. Season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper to taste.
Rest 1 minute, then serve immediately in warm bowls. Top with parsley and shaved Parmigiano-Reggiano.
tip: Use mixed mushrooms (cremini, shiitake, oyster) for depth. Leftovers keep 2 days; rewarm gently with a splash of stock. Substitute more stock for wine if desired.

title: Black Bean Burgers
ing: 2 cans black beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed
1/3 cup finely diced red bell pepper
steps: Spread rinsed beans on a lined sheet; bake at 350°F for 10 minutes to dry slightly, then cool 5 minutes.
Pulse oats in a food processor to coarse crumbs. Add half the dried beans and pulse to a chunky paste, 6 to 8 quick pulses.
In a bowl, combine bean paste, remaining beans, panko, onion, bell pepper, garlic, soy sauce, ketchup, cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, egg, salt, and pepper. Mix until just cohesive.
Divide mixture into 4 equal portions and form 3/4-inch-thick patties. Chill uncovered for 10 minutes to firm.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering. Add patties and cook 4 to 5 minutes per side until well browned and heated through to 165°F.
Toast buns and serve burgers hot with desired toppings and condiments.
tip: Swap egg with 1 tbsp ground flax + 3 tbsp water for vegan. Patties keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat in a skillet to re-crisp. For grilling, cook on oiled foil to prevent sticking.

title: Stuffed Bell Peppers
steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Slice tops off peppers, reserve tops, and remove seeds and membranes. Trim bases if needed so peppers stand upright in a snug baking dish.
Warm 2 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Sauté onion for 5 minutes until translucent, then add garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in rice, cinnamon, oregano, salt, and pepper; toast 1 minute. Add crushed tomatoes and 1 cup water, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 8 minutes; rice will be par-cooked.
Off heat, fold in parsley, mint, raisins, and pine nuts. Let rest 5 minutes, then gently fold in feta.
Pack filling into peppers to just below the rim, mounding slightly. Replace pepper tops and nestle peppers upright in the baking dish.
Cover dish tightly with foil and bake at 375°F for 35 minutes, then uncover and bake 10–15 minutes more until peppers are tender and rice is fully cooked.
Rest 5–10 minutes to settle juices. Serve warm or at room temperature, spooning any pan juices over the peppers.
tip: Swap pine nuts with chopped walnuts if preferred. The peppers keep refrigerated 3 days; rewarm covered at 325°F for 15 minutes or enjoy at room temp.

title: Aloo Gobi
ing: 1 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy 12-inch skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add potatoes in a single layer and brown, turning, for 6–8 minutes. Remove to a plate.
Add cauliflower to the skillet; brown edges 4–5 minutes. Remove to the plate with potatoes; keep skillet over medium heat.
Lower to medium. Add cumin seeds; toast 30 seconds until fragrant. Stir in onion with a pinch of salt; cook, stirring, until golden, 7–9 minutes.
Add ginger and garlic; cook 45–60 seconds. Stir in coriander, turmeric, and chili powder; toast 30 seconds. Add tomatoes; cook down until jammy and oil separates, 4–6 minutes.
Return potatoes and cauliflower with any juices. Add 1/4 cup water and 1 tsp salt; stir to coat. Cover and cook over medium-low, stirring once or twice, until potatoes are tender, 12–15 minutes.
Uncover and cook 2–3 minutes to evaporate excess moisture, stirring gently to keep florets intact. Sprinkle garam masala and lemon juice; fold to combine.
Taste and adjust salt. Rest off heat 3 minutes for flavors to settle. Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve hot with roti or rice.
tip: Swap: use 1 tsp paprika + a pinch cayenne if no Kashmiri chili. Make-ahead: cool, refrigerate 3 days; rewarm covered with a splash of water to keep moist.

title: Paneer Tikka Masala
ing: 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Whisk yogurt, lemon juice, ginger, garlic, 1 tsp Kashmiri chili, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and 1/2 tsp salt. Add paneer; toss gently. Marinate 20 to 30 minutes while you start the sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high. Sear marinated paneer in batches until lightly charred on 2 sides, 2 to 3 minutes total per batch. Transfer to a plate; reserve marinade.
In a wide pan, melt ghee over medium heat. Add onion and a pinch of salt; cook, stirring, until deep golden, 10 to 12 minutes. Stir in remaining 1 tsp Kashmiri chili and cook 30 seconds.
Add tomato puree and reserved marinade; simmer, stirring, until thick and glossy and fat separates, 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir in water, sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, and pepper; bring to a gentle simmer for 3 minutes to meld flavors.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in cream and crushed kasuri methi; simmer 2 minutes. Do not boil after adding cream to prevent splitting.
Add seared paneer and any juices; simmer gently, stirring, until heated through and coated, 2 to 3 minutes. Adjust salt to taste.
Rest off heat 2 minutes for flavors to settle. Garnish with cilantro and a drizzle of cream; serve hot with naan or basmati rice.
tip: For deeper char, broil marinated paneer on a rack 4 inches from heat for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once. Sauce can be made 2 days ahead; reheat gently and add cream and paneer just before serving.

title: Malai Kofta
ing: 1/2 cup cashews, soaked 20 minutes and drained
steps: Combine grated paneer, mashed potatoes, cornstarch, raisins, chopped cashews, cardamom, 1/2 tsp salt, and white pepper; mix gently to form a soft dough. Chill 10 minutes.
Divide mixture into 12 balls and roll smooth. Heat frying oil to 350°F in a deep pot. Fry koftas in batches 3–4 minutes, turning, until deep golden. Drain on a rack.
Blend soaked cashews with 1/2 cup water until silky smooth; set aside. Purée crushed tomatoes until smooth; set aside.
Heat ghee and 1 tbsp oil in a wide pan over medium. Add onion and cook 8–10 minutes until light golden. Stir in ginger-garlic paste; sauté 1 minute until aromatic.
Add cumin, coriander, turmeric, and Kashmiri chili. Cook 30 seconds. Pour in tomato purée and simmer for 10–12 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy with ghee spots.
Stir in cashew cream, 1/2 cup water, heavy cream, sugar, and 1 tsp salt. Simmer gently 4–5 minutes on low; finish with garam masala. Adjust seasoning.
Just before serving, warm gravy on low 2 minutes. Add koftas and coat gently; simmer 1 minute to heat through. Do not overcook to avoid breaking.
Garnish with cilantro. Serve immediately with naan or jeera rice.
tip: For nut-free, replace cashews with 1/2 cup heavy cream plus 2 tbsp milk powder. Fry koftas just before serving; keep gravy separate up to 2 days refrigerated and reheat gently.

title: Spanakopita
ing: 1 lb fresh spinach, washed and chopped
2 tbsp olive oil, as needed for brushing
steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Line a 9-inch square or similar baking pan with a light brush of olive oil.
Wilt spinach in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, then transfer to a colander and cool 5 minutes. Squeeze thoroughly to remove excess liquid, then chop finely.
In a bowl, mix spinach, feta, ricotta, dill, parsley, scallions, eggs, nutmeg, salt, and pepper until evenly combined.
Stack phyllo under a slightly damp towel. Lay 1 sheet in the pan, brush lightly with melted butter; repeat with 5 sheets, alternating directions and buttering each sheet.
Spread the spinach filling evenly over the layered phyllo, smoothing to the edges.
Top with 4 more phyllo sheets, buttering each. Generously butter the top layer, then score the surface into 4 to 6 portions with a sharp knife.
Bake at 375°F for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Rest 10 minutes to set before cutting along the score lines and serving warm.
tip: Sub 2 tsp dried dill if fresh unavailable. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; re-crisp at 350°F for 10 minutes. Keep phyllo covered with a damp towel to prevent drying while assembling.

title: Mujadara
ing: 1 cup brown or green lentils, rinsed
1 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/2 tsp black pepper, or to taste
steps: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a wide pot over medium; add 1.5 lbs sliced onions and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring often, until deep golden and jammy, 25–30 minutes. Lower heat if browning too fast.
Add cumin and allspice; stir 30 seconds until fragrant. Add lentils and 3 cups water. Bring to a boil, then simmer over medium-low until lentils are just tender, 15–18 minutes.
Stir in rice, 1 tsp salt, and pepper. If liquid is below the rice, add up to 1/2 cup hot water to barely cover. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low until rice is tender, 15–18 minutes.

While rice cooks, in a skillet heat 1 tbsp olive oil with 2 tbsp frying oil over medium-high. Add remaining 1/2 lb onions and fry, stirring, until dark caramel-brown and crisp at edges, 8–12 minutes. Drain on paper towel; salt lightly.
When rice is done, turn off heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork, folding in half the fried onions.
Mound mujadara on a platter. Top with remaining fried onions. Taste and adjust salt and pepper to taste. Serve warm or at room temperature with yogurt and parsley if using.
tip: Rinse rice until water runs clear to keep grains separate. Mujadara keeps 4 days refrigerated; rewarm covered with a splash of water over low heat or in a microwave.

title: Vegetable Bibimbap
ing: 10 oz firm tofu, pressed and sliced 1/2-inch
8 oz shiitake mushrooms, stemmed and sliced
steps: Cook rice: Add rinsed rice and 2 1/4 cups water to a pot, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes; rest off heat 10 minutes, covered, then fluff.
Marinate tofu: Whisk 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1/2 tbsp sesame oil, and 1/2 tsp sugar. Pat tofu dry, toss with marinade, and let sit 10 minutes.
Blanch greens: Boil a pot of salted water. Blanch spinach 30 seconds and sprouts 1 minute; rinse cold, squeeze dry. Toss each with a pinch of salt, a few drops sesame oil, and a little minced garlic.

Sauté vegetables: Heat 2 tsp oil over medium-high. Cook carrots with a pinch of salt for 2–3 minutes until crisp-tender; set aside. Repeat with zucchini 2–3 minutes. Sauté mushrooms with 1 tsp oil and 1 tsp soy sauce 3–4 minutes until tender; pepper to taste.
Pan-sear tofu: Heat 2 tsp oil over medium. Sear tofu 3–4 minutes per side until golden at edges; keep warm.
Make sauce: Stir gochujang, remaining 1 tbsp soy sauce, remaining 1/2 tbsp sesame oil, rice vinegar, and honey until smooth; thin with 1–2 tsp water if needed.
Assemble bowls: Divide hot rice among 4 bowls. Neatly arrange spinach, sprouts, carrots, zucchini, mushrooms, tofu, and cucumber on top. Sprinkle sesame seeds and scallions.
Serve: Spoon 1–2 tbsp sauce per bowl. Mix well at the table so rice, vegetables, and sauce are evenly combined; add salt or pepper to taste.
tip: Swap shiitake with oyster mushrooms or king trumpet. Keep toppings and rice separate up to 3 days; reheat rice and sautéed veg, then assemble and add fresh cucumber and sauce.

title: Falafel Bowl with Tahini
ing: 1 1/2 cups dried chickpeas, soaked overnight and drained
steps: Soak 1 1/2 cups dried chickpeas in plenty of water for 12 to 18 hours, then drain very well. Do not use canned chickpeas; pat the soaked chickpeas dry with towels.

In a processor, pulse chickpeas, onion, 4 cloves garlic, parsley, cilantro, cumin, coriander, salt, pepper, and baking soda until finely ground and mealy, 30 to 60 seconds. Do not puree; mixture should hold when pressed.
Sprinkle in flour and pulse just to combine. Chill the mixture for 20 minutes to firm. With wet hands, form 20 golf-ball-size falafel; flatten slightly to 3/4-inch thick patties.
Heat 1 1/2 inches frying oil in a deep skillet to 350°F. Fry falafel in batches until deep brown and crisp, 3 to 4 minutes per side; drain on a rack. Keep warm at 250°F while finishing.
Whisk tahini, lemon juice, grated garlic, and a pinch of salt. Slowly whisk in cold water until smooth and pourable, about 1/4 cup; adjust lemon and salt to taste.
Toss cucumbers, tomatoes, and red onion with a pinch of salt and pepper. Warm rice and shred romaine.
Assemble bowls: divide rice and romaine among 4 bowls. Add tomato-cucumber salad. Top each with 5 falafel.
Drizzle generously with tahini sauce, sprinkle sesame seeds and chopped herbs, and add black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.
tip: Soak chickpeas at least 12 hours for authentic texture. Leftover falafel reheat well in a 375°F oven for 10 minutes; keep tahini separate and thin with water if it thickens.

title: Mushroom Stroganoff
ing: 8 oz shiitake mushrooms, stems removed, sliced
12 oz wide egg noodles, cooked al dente
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide skillet over medium-high. Add half the mushrooms and sear without stirring for 3 minutes, then toss and cook 2 minutes more. Transfer; repeat with remaining mushrooms, adding oil as needed.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter and onion; cook until translucent, 5 to 6 minutes. Stir in garlic, paprika, and mustard; cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over onions; stir 1 minute. Pour in wine, scraping browned bits; simmer 2 minutes to reduce by half. Stir in vegetable stock and bring to a gentle simmer for 3 minutes to thicken.
Return mushrooms and any juices to the pan; simmer on medium-low for 4 to 5 minutes until tender and coated. Remove from heat; let stand 1 minute to cool slightly.
Whisk sour cream in a bowl to loosen. Stir into the pan off heat until smooth; warm gently on low for 1 minute without boiling. Season with salt, pepper, lemon juice, and half the dill.
Serve over hot egg noodles; garnish with remaining dill. Sauce should be velvety and cling to noodles. Serve immediately.
tip: Substitute crème fraîche for sour cream for extra stability. Make ahead: chill sauce up to 2 days; rewarm gently with a splash of stock—do not boil after adding dairy.

title: Cauliflower Tacos
ing: 1 large head cauliflower, cut into small florets
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss cauliflower with frying oil, salt, pepper, cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, and oregano until evenly coated.
Spread florets on a sheet pan in a single layer and roast at 425°F for 22 to 25 minutes, stirring once, until browned at the edges and tender.
Whisk sour cream, adobo sauce, lime zest, and lime juice in a small bowl; season crema with a pinch of salt to taste.
Warm corn tortillas directly over a burner or in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds per side until pliable.
Fill each tortilla with roasted cauliflower, then top with onion, cilantro, and queso fresco.
Drizzle with chipotle-lime crema and serve immediately while hot.
tip: Swap queso fresco with crumbled cotija or omit for vegan and use a dairy-free crema. Roast cauliflower a day ahead; rewarm at 375°F for 8 minutes before assembling.

title: Pav Bhaji
ing: 1 cup green bell pepper, finely chopped
1 cup green peas, fresh or frozen
steps: Boil potatoes and cauliflower in a pot of salted water until fork-tender, about 12–15 minutes. Add peas for the last 2 minutes, then drain well.
Heat 1 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion and sauté until translucent, about 4–5 minutes.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute. Add bell pepper and cook until softened, 4–5 minutes. Add tomatoes and cook down until jammy, 8–10 minutes.
Mash boiled potatoes, cauliflower, and peas lightly. Add to the skillet with chili powder, pav bhaji masala, turmeric, and salt. Mix and mash thoroughly.
Pour in 1/2 cup hot water to loosen. Simmer over medium-low, mashing occasionally, until thick and glossy, 8–10 minutes. Adjust salt and spice, add lemon juice and 1 tbsp butter.
For pav, slit rolls without cutting through. Heat a griddle over medium. Melt 1 tbsp butter, toast pav cut-sides until golden, 1–2 minutes.
If bhaji thickens too much, add a splash of hot water and simmer 1 minute. Finish with cilantro and a small pat of butter stirred in.
Serve bhaji hot with toasted pav, extra butter, lemon wedges, and chopped onion on the side.
tip: Sub 1/2 cup carrot for part of cauliflower if desired. Bhaji keeps 3 days refrigerated; thin with hot water and reheat until bubbling before serving.

title: Chiles Rellenos
ing: 10 oz Oaxaca cheese, cut into 8 batons
1 lb ripe Roma tomatoes, cored and quartered
1/2 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
steps: Char poblanos over an open flame or under a broiler set to High, turning until blistered and blackened on all sides, 6–8 minutes. Transfer to a covered bowl to steam for 10 minutes.
Gently peel charred skins. Slit each chile lengthwise and remove seeds and membranes, keeping stems intact. Pat dry.
Tuck a baton of Oaxaca cheese into each chile. Lightly dust chiles with 2 tbsp of the flour to help batter adhere; set aside.
Blend tomatoes, onion, garlic, vegetable broth, sugar, and 1/2 tsp salt until smooth. Simmer in a saucepan over medium heat for 12–15 minutes; stir in vinegar and keep warm on low.
Whip egg whites with a clean bowl and whisk to stiff peaks, 3–4 minutes. Beat yolks with remaining flour, 1/2 tsp salt, and pepper, then gently fold into whites to make a fluffy batter.
Heat 1/2 inch frying oil in a wide skillet to 350°F. Dip each stuffed chile in batter, letting excess drip, and fry seam side down until golden, 2–3 minutes per side. Drain on a rack.
Nestle fried chiles into the warm tomato sauce and simmer gently for 2 minutes to meld. Cheese should be melted; internal temp should reach 165°F for safety.
Serve chiles napados (sauced) on plates; garnish with cilantro. Eat immediately while exterior is crisp and interior is molten.
tip: Swap Oaxaca with Monterey Jack or queso asadero. Keep fried chiles on a rack in a 250°F oven up to 20 minutes; sauce just before serving to preserve crispness.

title: Gado-Gado
ing: 14 oz firm tofu, pressed and cubed
steps: Heat 2 tbsp frying oil in a skillet over medium and pan-fry tofu and tempeh until golden on all sides, 6 to 8 minutes; season with a pinch of salt and pepper and set aside on paper towels.

Boil potatoes in salted water until just tender, 8 to 10 minutes; lift out. In the same pot, blanch green beans 2 to 3 minutes, then cabbage 1 minute, then spinach 30 seconds; drain and cool. Keep vegetables crisp-tender.
Place eggs in a saucepan, cover with water, bring to a boil, then simmer 8 minutes; cool in cold water, peel, and halve.

Make the peanut sauce: in a saucepan combine peanut butter, coconut milk, water, palm sugar, kecap manis, tamarind, garlic, and half the chilies. Simmer over low heat, stirring, 6 to 8 minutes until smooth and pourable.
Adjust sauce thickness with a splash of water if needed; season with salt to taste. Keep warm over very low heat, stirring occasionally.
Arrange on a large platter: potatoes, green beans, cabbage, spinach, cucumber, bean sprouts, tofu, and tempeh. Top with warm peanut sauce.
Garnish with remaining chilies, roasted peanuts, and fried shallots. Serve immediately, letting diners toss at the table.
tip: Sub palm sugar with light brown sugar if needed. Blanch and prep vegetables a day ahead; keep chilled and covered. Warm sauce gently before serving; thin with hot water to loosen.

title: Rajma
ing: 1 1/2 cups dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight
steps: Drain soaked beans, rinse well, and add to a pot with 3 cups water. Bring to a boil, then simmer covered over low heat for 60 to 70 minutes until beans are very tender and easily mashed between fingers.
Heat 2 tbsp frying oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook, stirring, until deep golden, 10 to 12 minutes.
Stir in ginger and garlic; cook 1 minute until fragrant. Add tomato puree and cook, stirring, until it thickens and oil separates at the edges, 8 to 10 minutes.
Add ground coriander, cumin, turmeric, and Kashmiri chili powder; cook 1 minute to bloom spices.
Add cooked beans with their cooking liquid. Mash a few beans against the pot to thicken, then simmer gently for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until gravy is silky.
Stir in garam masala, adjust salt and pepper to taste, and simmer 2 more minutes. If too thick, add hot water a few tbsp at a time to reach a pourable, creamy consistency.
Rest off heat for 5 minutes to let flavors meld, then garnish with chopped cilantro and a drizzle of frying oil if desired.
Serve hot with steamed basmati rice; keep curry above 165°F when holding and reheat leftovers to 165°F before serving.
tip: Soak beans 8–12 hours for best texture; quick-soak by boiling 2 minutes, resting 1 hour. For creamier rajma, add 2 tbsp yogurt whisked in off heat. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated.

title: Imam Bayildi
ing: 1 lb ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
1 tsp flaky sea salt, to taste
steps: Peel eggplants in lengthwise stripes, leaving some skin on, and split lengthwise without cutting through. Soak in salted water for 20 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Warm 1/3 cup frying oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sear eggplants on all sides until lightly browned, about 8 minutes. Transfer to a braising dish, cut-sides up.
In the same skillet, add 2 tbsp olive oil. Cook onions over medium heat until very soft and pale golden, 12 to 15 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, black pepper, 1/2 tsp kosher salt, and sugar. Simmer until saucy, 8 to 10 minutes. Off heat, stir in parsley and lemon juice.
Gently pry a pocket in each eggplant and spoon in the tomato-onion mixture, mounding any extra on top.
Whisk remaining olive oil with 1/2 cup water and a pinch of salt. Pour around eggplants. Cover the dish tightly.
Bake at 350°F until eggplants are completely tender and silky, 45 to 55 minutes. Baste once or twice with pan juices.
Cool to room temperature, uncovered 20 minutes. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt to taste and serve at room temperature with crusty bread.
tip: Make ahead: Best after resting; refrigerate up to 3 days. Swap: Use canned crushed tomatoes (14 oz) when fresh are out of season; reduce added water by 2 tbsp.

title: Cacio e Pepe
ing: 1/2 cup pasta cooking water, reserved hot
1 tbsp olive oil, as needed for pan
steps: Bring 3 quarts water to a rolling boil over high heat, season with 1 tsp kosher salt.
Toast 1 1/2 tsp black pepper with 1 tbsp olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat for 1 minute, then turn heat off.
Cook 12 oz spaghetti until just shy of al dente, 1 to 2 minutes less than package time; reserve 1 cup boiling water.
Add 1/2 cup reserved hot pasta water to the skillet, simmer 30 seconds over medium to bloom the pepper and form a peppery liquid.
Transfer spaghetti to the skillet; toss over medium heat until coated and some water is absorbed, about 1 minute.
Off the heat, vigorously toss while sprinkling in 1 1/4 cups Pecorino a little at a time, adding more hot pasta water by tablespoons to form a silky emulsion, 1 to 3 minutes.
Return to low heat only if needed, tossing constantly, to keep the sauce fluid; stop before it thickens too much. Season with more pepper if desired.
Serve immediately, twirling portions; the sauce should be glossy and cling in a thin, creamy layer.
tip: Use only Pecorino Romano, very finely grated. Work off the heat to prevent clumping; adjust with splashes of hot pasta water. Reserve extra water in case the sauce tightens while serving.

title: Pasta alla Norma
ing: 1 lb ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped
steps: Toss eggplant cubes with 1 tsp kosher salt and rest in a colander for 20 minutes to draw out moisture. Pat very dry with towels before frying.
Heat 1/2 inch frying oil in a wide skillet over medium-high to 360°F. Fry eggplant in batches until deep golden, 5 to 7 minutes per batch. Drain on paper towels.
In a saucepan, warm 2 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add garlic and red pepper flakes; cook until fragrant, 30 seconds. Add tomatoes, 1/2 tsp salt, and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Boil 4 quarts water in a large pot. Salt generously (about 2 tbsp). Cook rigatoni until al dente, 9 to 11 minutes. Reserve 1 cup pasta water, then drain.
Fold fried eggplant into the tomato sauce and simmer for 2 minutes to marry flavors. Adjust seasoning with black pepper to taste.
Add pasta to the sauce, loosening with splashes of reserved pasta water until glossy and well-coated, about 1 to 2 minutes over medium heat.
Off heat, stir in half the basil. Plate, then shower with grated ricotta salata and remaining basil. Serve immediately.
tip: Sub 1 (28-oz) can whole tomatoes, crushed by hand, when fresh aren’t good. Fry eggplant ahead; hold sauce up to 2 days refrigerated and rewarm gently before combining with pasta.

title: Trofie al Pesto
ing: 2 cups fresh basil leaves, loosely packed
8 oz Yukon gold potatoes, peeled, cut in 1/2-inch cubes
6 oz green beans, trimmed, cut in 1 1/2-inch lengths
1/4 cup pasta cooking water, as needed
steps: Bring 4 quarts of water to a boil in a large pot. Add 1 tsp kosher salt.
In a mortar or food processor, combine basil, garlic, and pine nuts; pound or pulse to a coarse paste, 1 to 2 minutes.
Work in Parmigiano and Pecorino, then drizzle in 6 tbsp olive oil until creamy yet thick; season with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Add potatoes to the boiling water and cook for 5 minutes. Add green beans and cook 3 minutes more.
Add trofie to the same pot; cook until al dente per package, usually 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water. Drain pasta, potatoes, and beans together; return to warm pot off heat.
Loosen pesto with 2 to 4 tbsp hot pasta water to create a silky sauce. Add to pot and toss gently to coat; add more water as needed.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper. Serve immediately, passing extra cheese at the table.
tip: Sub Pecorino Romano if Pecorino Sardo is unavailable. Store leftovers airtight up to 1 day; refresh with a splash of hot water and oil. For maximum aroma, make pesto just before serving.

title: Penne alla Vodka
ing: 1/2 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/4 tsp black pepper, or to taste
2 tbsp fresh basil, thinly sliced, for garnish
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add 12 oz penne and cook until al dente, 9 to 10 minutes. Reserve 1/4 cup pasta water, then drain.
Meanwhile, heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add 4 oz diced pancetta and cook, stirring, until lightly crisp, 4 to 5 minutes.
Add 1 small chopped onion and cook until translucent, 3 to 4 minutes. Stir in 2 cloves minced garlic and 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes; cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Off the heat, pour in 1/2 cup vodka. Return to medium heat and simmer until reduced by half and the alcohol scent fades, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in 1 cup crushed tomatoes. Simmer gently over medium-low, stirring occasionally, for 5 to 7 minutes until slightly thickened.
Lower heat and stir in 3/4 cup heavy cream; simmer 2 minutes. Season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter to gloss the sauce.
Add drained penne and 1/4 cup reserved pasta water to the skillet. Toss over medium heat until the sauce clings, 1 to 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and fold in 1/2 cup grated Parmesan. Adjust seasoning to taste. Serve hot, garnished with 2 tbsp sliced fresh basil.
tip: Guanciale or good bacon can stand in for pancetta. Sauce base can be made 2 days ahead; rewarm gently and finish with cream, butter, and pasta water before serving.

title: Lasagne alla Bolognese
steps: Warm 1 tbsp olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add 4 oz pancetta and cook until rendered, about 5 minutes. Stir in onion, carrot, and celery; sweat until soft, 8 minutes, without browning.
Crumble in 1 lb ground beef; season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Cook, breaking up, until no pink remains, 6–8 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.

Pour in 1 cup dry white wine; simmer until nearly evaporated, 6–8 minutes. Add 1 1/2 cups crushed tomatoes and 1 cup beef stock; bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low and cook partially covered for 90 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir 1 cup whole milk into the ragù; simmer gently for 20 minutes. Taste and season with remaining salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Make béchamel: Melt 2 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in 2 tbsp flour; cook 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in 1 cup milk; simmer, whisking, until smooth and nappe, 5–7 minutes. Season lightly with salt.
Heat oven to 375°F. If using dried pasta, parboil sheets in salted water for 4 minutes, then drain on towels. If fresh, no boil needed.
Assemble in a 9x9-inch dish: spread a thin layer of ragù, then pasta, a thin veil of béchamel, ragù, and a sprinkle of Parmigiano. Repeat 4–5 layers, finishing with béchamel and Parmigiano on top.
Cover tightly with foil and bake at 375°F for 25 minutes. Uncover and bake until bubbling and lightly browned, 15–20 minutes. Rest 15 minutes before slicing and serving warm.
tip: For tradition, use mostly beef with a little pork; veal is a fine swap. Ragù improves overnight—make ahead and chill up to 2 days. Use fresh pasta if possible for the most tender layers.

title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil, 8 to 10 minutes. Add 1 tbsp salt to season the water.
Cook spaghetti until al dente, 8 to 9 minutes, stirring occasionally. Reserve 1 cup pasta water; drain.
Warm olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat, 2 minutes. Add garlic and cook gently until pale golden, 2 to 3 minutes; do not brown.
Stir in red pepper flakes and 2 tbsp reserved pasta water; let sizzle 15 seconds to bloom the flavors.
Add drained spaghetti to the skillet. Toss constantly over medium heat, adding reserved pasta water a splash at a time to create a silky emulsion, 1 to 2 minutes.
Season with kosher salt and black pepper. Toss in parsley off heat until evenly coated and glossy, 30 seconds.
Taste and adjust salt, pepper, or a touch more oil. Serve immediately, twirling pasta to capture the sauce.
tip: For extra aroma, finish with a spoon of the pasta water that touched the garlic oil. Add grated pecorino only if you like; it’s not traditional in Naples and may tighten the emulsion.

title: Dan Dan Noodles
ing: 2 tbsp Sichuan preserved mustard greens (ya cai), rinsed, minced
1 tbsp chili flakes (preferably Sichuan), or to taste
3 tbsp Chinese sesame paste (zhi ma jiang)
1 tbsp chili oil, or to taste
steps: Toast 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan over medium for 1 minute, grind finely, set aside. Mix sesame paste and peanut butter with 1/2 cup hot noodle water until smooth.
Stir in 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp black vinegar, 1 tbsp chili oil, 1 tsp sugar, and half the ground peppercorn to the sesame mixture; adjust salt to taste. This is the sauce base.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high. Add 8 oz ground pork, break up, and cook until lightly crisp and no pink remains, 5 to 6 minutes; stir in 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine.
Add 2 tbsp minced ya cai, 2 cloves minced garlic, 1 tbsp minced ginger, 1 tbsp chili flakes, and remaining peppercorn. Stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant; keep warm on low.
Boil 12 oz noodles in salted water until just tender, 2 to 3 minutes for fresh (or per package). Reserve 1/2 cup cooking water; drain well.
Divide sauce among 4 warm bowls. Top with hot noodles, toss briefly to coat, loosening with reserved water as needed until glossy.
Spoon pork-ya cai mixture over noodles. Scatter 2 tbsp sliced scallions. Serve immediately, letting diners toss so pork and sauce distribute evenly.
Taste and adjust with extra chili oil or vinegar to preference; serve hot.
tip: Ya cai is essential; if unavailable, use zha cai or pickled mustard stems. Sauce can be mixed 1 day ahead; loosen with hot noodle water before serving.

title: Yakisoba
ing: 8 oz pork belly or shoulder, thinly sliced
1 cup bean sprouts, rinsed and drained
2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
2 tbsp pickled red ginger (beni shoga), for garnish
steps: Loosen 12 oz yakisoba noodles: if vacuum-packed, microwave 30 seconds or soak in hot water 1 minute, then drain well and separate strands.
Whisk 1/2 cup yakisoba sauce with 1 tbsp Worcestershire and 1 tsp sugar; set aside. Prep vegetables and thinly slice 8 oz pork.

Heat a large wok or skillet over medium-high. Add 1 tbsp oil, then pork. Stir-fry until just cooked and lightly browned, about 3–4 minutes; season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Transfer pork to a plate.
Add 1/2 tbsp oil. Stir-fry onion and carrot 2 minutes. Add cabbage; cook until crisp-tender, 3–4 minutes.
Return pork to pan. Add noodles; toss to combine. Drizzle sauce mixture around pan edges; stir-fry until noodles are evenly coated and steaming, about 2–3 minutes.
Add bean sprouts and a splash of water (1–2 tbsp) if dry. Stir-fry 1 minute until sprouts are just wilted. Taste and adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Divide among 4 plates. Garnish with aonori, pickled red ginger, and zigzags of Kewpie mayonnaise. Serve hot.
tip: Swap pork with chicken thigh or shrimp. Keep leftovers up to 2 days refrigerated; reheat in a skillet with a splash of water to loosen noodles.

title: Japchae
ing: 10 oz beef ribeye, cut into thin strips
6 oz shiitake mushrooms, stems removed, sliced
steps: Make the seasoning: in a bowl mix 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, and 2 tbsp sesame oil until dissolved; set aside.
Marinate beef: toss 10 oz beef with 1 tsp garlic and a spoonful of the seasoning; rest for 10 minutes while prepping vegetables.
Cook eggs into a thin omelet over medium heat with a light film of oil, 2–3 minutes; cool and slice into thin ribbons; set aside.
Blanch spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds, drain, rinse cold, squeeze dry, and season with a little seasoning and 1/2 tsp sesame seeds.
Boil dangmyeon in plenty of water for 6–7 minutes until chewy; drain, rinse cold, cut once or twice with scissors; toss with 2–3 tbsp seasoning to prevent sticking.
Stir-fry in batches over medium-high: sauté onion 2–3 minutes, remove; carrot 2 minutes, remove; bell pepper 1–2 minutes, remove; shiitake with 1 tsp garlic 2–3 minutes; season lightly with salt.
Stir-fry marinated beef 2–3 minutes until just cooked through and browned; add scallions for 30 seconds; combine all cooked components in a large bowl.

Finish: add remaining seasoning and 1 tsp sesame seeds; toss noodles over medium heat in a large pan 1–2 minutes to warm and absorb; adjust salt and a pinch of pepper to taste. Serve warm or at room temp.
tip: Substitute ribeye with flank or omit for vegetarian. Make ahead: cool completely and refrigerate up to 2 days; rewarm gently with a splash of water or soy sauce.

title: Beef Chow Fun
ing: 12 oz flank steak, sliced 1/4-inch against grain
16 oz fresh wide rice noodles (hor fun), separated
10 oz bean sprouts, rinsed and drained
steps: Marinate beef: In a bowl combine soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sugar, and sesame oil. Add steak and toss until coated; rest for 15 minutes while you prep vegetables and sauce.
Make sauce: In a small bowl mix oyster sauce, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and white pepper; set aside. Gently separate rice noodles into long ribbons so they don’t tear.
Heat wok: Set a carbon-steel wok over high heat until lightly smoking, about 2 minutes. Add 2 tbsp peanut oil, swirl to coat, then spread beef in a single layer.
Sear beef: Let beef sear undisturbed for 45–60 seconds until browned, then stir-fry 30 seconds more until just cooked through; transfer to a plate to avoid overcooking.
Aromatics and onions: Return wok to high heat, add 1 tbsp peanut oil. Add garlic and onion; stir-fry 1–2 minutes until onion is just translucent with char at edges.
Noodles and char: Add remaining 1 tbsp oil, then the rice noodles. Toss gently and let them sit 45–60 seconds to pick up wok hei, then toss again; repeat once to warm through without breaking.

Combine and season: Return beef, add bean sprouts and scallions. Pour in sauce; toss with broad scoop-and-fold motions for 1–2 minutes until evenly coated and sprouts just wilt. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Finish: Stir-fry 30 seconds more to evaporate excess moisture. Serve immediately, hot, with noodles glossy and distinct strands.
tip: If noodles are cold, steam or microwave briefly until pliable before separating. Substitute neutral oil for peanut if needed; avoid over-saucing—Beef Chow Fun should be dry-fried, not gravy-like.

title: Tonkotsu Ramen
ing: 1 lb pork belly, rolled and tied
2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
steps: Blanch bones: Cover pork neck bones and trotters with cold water, bring to a rolling boil over high heat, boil 10 minutes, then drain. Rinse bones under hot water and scrub residue from surfaces.

Start broth: In a large stockpot (at least 8 qt), add cleaned bones and 6 qt fresh water. Bring to a vigorous boil over high heat, then keep at a hard boil, skimming foam. Boil uncovered for 6 hours, topping with hot water to keep bones submerged.

Aromatics: At hour 5, add ginger and garlic. Continue a hard boil for 60 minutes to extract collagen until broth turns opaque and creamy. Strain through a fine sieve, pressing to extract liquid; keep hot.

Chashu: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high. Sear rolled pork belly on all sides until browned, about 8 minutes. Combine soy sauce, mirin, and sake with 1 cup water; simmer belly covered over low for 1 hour, turning occasionally, until tender. Cool in liquid, slice thin.
Marinated eggs: Boil eggs 7 minutes, then chill in ice water 5 minutes. Peel and marinate in 1/2 cup chashu braising liquid plus 1/2 cup water for 2–4 hours, chilled.
Season broth: Skim fat from chashu liquid. Stir 1/2 to 3/4 cup into hot broth to taste; add salt and pepper to balance. Keep broth at a gentle simmer while assembling.
Noodles: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Cook fresh ramen noodles 1–2 minutes until just tender. Drain well; do not rinse.
Assemble: Divide noodles among 4 warmed bowls. Ladle 2 to 2 1/2 cups boiling-hot broth into each. Top with sliced chashu, halved eggs, menma, scallions, and a nori square. Serve immediately.
tip: Pressure cooker shortcut: 90 minutes on high after blanching yields rich broth; simmer open 20 minutes to emulsify. Leftover broth freezes up to 2 months; reheat to a rolling boil and whisk to re-emulsify.

title: Spaghetti alle Vongole
ing: 2 lb small clams, scrubbed and soaked
steps: Rinse and scrub 2 lb clams, then soak in cold salted water for 20 minutes; drain and rinse well. Discard any broken shells.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook 12 oz spaghetti until very al dente, about 1 minute shy of package time; reserve 1 cup pasta water and drain.
Warm 3 tbsp olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add 3 cloves sliced garlic and 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes; cook until fragrant, about 45 seconds, without browning.
Add 1/2 cup dry white wine; simmer for 1 minute. Add clams, cover, and cook over medium-high until they open, 4 to 6 minutes. Discard any that stay closed.
Transfer opened clams to a bowl with tongs, leaving juices in the pan. Add drained spaghetti to the skillet with 1/2 cup reserved pasta water; toss over medium heat 1 to 2 minutes.
Stir in 2 tbsp butter and most of the 1/4 cup parsley until the sauce turns glossy and lightly coats the pasta, 1 minute. Season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper to taste.
Return clams and any juices to the skillet; toss gently over low heat 30 seconds to warm through. Remove from heat.
Divide among warm bowls, sprinkle remaining parsley, and serve with 1/2 lemon in wedges for squeezing immediately.
tip: If using larger clams, steam them 1 to 2 minutes longer. For bianco style, omit tomatoes; for rosso, add 1/2 cup crushed tomatoes with the wine. Clams are best day-of; refrigerate leftovers up to 1 day.

title: Gnocchi with Brown Butter and Sage
ing: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
1/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, plus more for serving
2 tbsp frying oil, as needed for the baking sheet
steps: Prick 2 lb potatoes and bake at 400°F until very tender, 50 to 60 minutes; cool just until you can handle. Halve, scoop flesh, and rice while hot onto a lightly floured surface.

Sprinkle 1 tsp fine sea salt over the potatoes. Let steam off 5 minutes, then add 1 large egg and 1 1/2 cups flour. Gently fold and knead 30 to 60 seconds until a soft, barely tacky dough forms; do not overwork.

Divide dough into 4 pieces. On a floured surface, roll each into 3/4-inch ropes. Cut into 1-inch pillows and, if desired, roll on a fork or gnocchi board. Transfer to an oiled, floured sheet and dust lightly.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil with 2 tsp kosher salt. Lower to a gentle simmer. Cook gnocchi in batches; when they float, simmer 30 to 60 seconds more. Lift with a spider to a warm bowl.
In a wide skillet over medium heat, melt 8 tbsp butter. Add 12 sage leaves. Cook, swirling, until butter foams and turns hazelnut-brown and sage is crisp, 3 to 5 minutes; remove skillet from heat.
Add cooked gnocchi to the brown butter; return to medium heat and toss 30 to 60 seconds to coat. Season with 1/4 tsp pepper and a pinch of salt if needed.
Off heat, fold in 1/3 cup Parmigiano-Reggiano. Serve immediately with extra cheese. Reserve a splash of cooking water to loosen sauce if it tightens.
tip: Bake, don’t boil, the potatoes for drier flesh and lighter gnocchi. Freeze uncooked gnocchi on a sheet until firm, then bag; cook from frozen, adding about 1 minute after they float.

title: Orecchiette with Broccoli Rabe and Sausage
ing: 1 lb broccoli rabe, tough ends trimmed, cut in 2-inch pieces
12 oz Italian sausage, casings removed, crumbled
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli rabe and blanch for 2 minutes; lift out with tongs to a bowl of cold water, then drain and squeeze gently dry.
In the same boiling water, cook orecchiette until al dente, about 10-12 minutes; reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
While pasta cooks, heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add sausage and cook, breaking up, until browned and cooked through, 6-8 minutes (165°F). Transfer to a plate.
Add remaining 1 tbsp oil to the skillet. Add garlic and red pepper flakes; cook over medium-low until fragrant, 45-60 seconds, without browning.
Add broccoli rabe to the skillet with a pinch of salt; sauté, tossing, until tender and glossy, 2-3 minutes. Return sausage to the pan.
Add drained orecchiette to the skillet. Pour in 1/3 cup reserved pasta water; toss over medium heat until the pasta is well coated and starchy liquid clings, 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Sprinkle Pecorino, black pepper, and taste for salt; add more pasta water 1-2 tbsp at a time for a light emulsion. Toss vigorously to combine.
Rest 1 minute, then serve hot with additional Pecorino at the table.
tip: Swap broccoli rabe with broccolini for milder bitterness. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; rewarm with a splash of water and a drizzle of oil.

title: Pasta Primavera
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook spaghetti until al dente, 8–10 minutes. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat until butter foams, 1 minute. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, 30 seconds.
Add asparagus and broccoli; sauté over medium-high heat until bright and just tender, 3–4 minutes. Add zucchini; cook 2 minutes.
Stir in cherry tomatoes and peas; cook until tomatoes begin to slump, 2 minutes. Season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Add heavy cream and 1/4 cup reserved pasta water; simmer gently to thicken, 2–3 minutes.
Add drained spaghetti to the skillet; toss until coated and glossy, 1–2 minutes. Add Parmesan and lemon juice; toss, adding more pasta water as needed for a silky sauce.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Remove from heat and fold in basil. Serve immediately, passing extra Parmesan if desired.
tip: Swap vegetables seasonally (e.g., snap peas, carrots). Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; loosen with a splash of hot water when reheating.

title: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
ing: 1 1/4 lb peeled San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil over high heat. Salt the water with 1 tbsp kosher salt.
Set a wide skillet over medium heat. Add guanciale and 1 tsp frying oil if needed to start rendering. Cook, stirring, until golden and crisp, 7–9 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Add red pepper flakes to the rendered fat and bloom 30 seconds. Raise heat to medium, pour in white wine, and simmer until mostly reduced, 2–3 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Simmer gently over medium-low, stirring occasionally, until lightly thickened and glossy, 10–12 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
While the sauce simmers, cook bucatini in the boiling water until very al dente, 1–2 minutes shy of package time (about 7–8 minutes). Reserve 1 cup pasta water, then drain.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add drained bucatini to the sauce with 1/2 cup reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously until the pasta is coated and the sauce clings, 1–2 minutes.
Off the heat, sprinkle most of the Pecorino Romano and toss until creamy, adding splashes of pasta water as needed for a silky emulsion.
Serve immediately, topped with remaining guanciale bits if separated in the pan and a final shower of Pecorino Romano.
tip: Guanciale is traditional; pancetta is a distant second. Sauce can be made to step 4 up to 2 days ahead; chill and reheat gently, loosening with pasta water.

title: Pastitsio
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook 8 oz bucatini until just shy of al dente, 1–2 minutes less than package; drain. Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil and cool on a tray.

Heat a skillet over medium-high. Add 1 lb ground lamb and cook, breaking up, until browned and no longer pink, about 6–8 minutes; drain excess fat. Stir in 1 cup onion and cook 3 minutes. Add 2 cloves garlic and cook 30 seconds.

Add 1/4 cup red wine; simmer 1 minute. Stir in 1 cup crushed tomatoes, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp allspice, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp pepper. Simmer over medium-low for 12–15 minutes until thick; cool 5 minutes.
Heat oven to 375°F. For béchamel, melt 3 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in 3 tbsp flour; cook 1 minute. Gradually whisk in 2 cups milk; simmer, whisking, until thick, 5–7 minutes.
Remove béchamel from heat; season with 1/4 tsp nutmeg and a pinch of salt. Whisk in 1/3 cup grated kefalotyri until smooth. Temper and whisk in 1 beaten egg until glossy.
Lightly oil an 8-inch square baking dish. Layer pasta in the bottom. Spread meat sauce evenly over pasta. Pour béchamel over the top, smoothing to edges; tap dish to settle.
Bake at 375°F until bubbling at edges and top is lightly golden, 30–35 minutes. The center should be 165°F. Rest 15 minutes for clean slices.
Cut into squares and serve warm, sprinkled with 1 tbsp chopped parsley.
tip: Kefalotyri can be swapped with Romano or Parmesan. Cools and firms as it rests; leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated. Reheat covered at 325°F until hot.

title: Zhajiangmian
ing: 2 cups cucumber, cut into fine matchsticks
1 cup scallions, cut into thin matchsticks
steps: Blanch 1 cup mung bean sprouts in boiling water for 30 seconds, drain, and set aside. Cut 2 cups cucumber and 1 cup scallions into fine matchsticks.
Heat 2 tbsp frying oil over medium heat. Add 8 oz ground pork and cook, breaking up, until no longer pink and lightly browned, about 4 to 5 minutes.
Stir in 1 1/2 tbsp minced ginger and 2 cloves minced garlic; cook until fragrant, 30 seconds.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Add 1/2 cup sweet bean sauce, 2 tbsp fermented soybean paste, 1 tbsp light soy sauce, and 1 tsp sugar. Fry the sauces with the pork, stirring, for 2 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup water to loosen. Simmer gently, stirring often, until glossy, thick, and oil separates, about 8 to 10 minutes. Adjust consistency with a splash of water if too thick.
Boil 12 oz fresh wheat noodles in salted water until just tender, 2 to 3 minutes for fresh (or per package for dried). Drain well.
Divide noodles among 4 bowls. Top each with a generous spoon of pork sauce, cucumber, scallion, and sprouts. Sprinkle 1/4 tsp white pepper to taste.
Toss at the table so the sauce coats the noodles evenly; add a little hot noodle water if needed to help it cling.
tip: Tianmianjiang is key; if unavailable, use hoisin thinned with a bit of soy, but flavor will differ. Sauce keeps 3 days refrigerated; rewarm with a splash of water before serving.

title: Miso Soup
ing: 6 oz silken tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
2 tbsp dried wakame, soaked and drained
steps: Make dashi: Add kombu to 4 cups cold water in a saucepan and heat gently until small bubbles form, 8–10 minutes; remove kombu just before boiling.
Add katsuobushi, bring to a bare simmer for 30 seconds, turn off heat, and steep 5 minutes; strain through a fine sieve to yield clear dashi.
Return hot dashi to the pot. Add soaked, drained wakame and tofu; warm over low heat until steaming, 2–3 minutes. Do not boil.
In a bowl, whisk 3 tbsp white miso and 3 tbsp red miso with a ladleful of hot dashi until smooth, then stir back into the pot off heat.
Taste and adjust saltiness by adding a little more hot dashi or miso as needed. Keep below a simmer to preserve aroma.
Ladle into warm bowls and garnish with sliced scallions; serve immediately while hot.
tip: For lighter soup, use all white miso; for deeper savor, use all red. Dashi can be made ahead 3 days (refrigerated). Stir miso off heat to keep it fragrant and prevent separation.

title: Red Lentil Soup
ing: 1 cup red lentils, rinsed until water runs clear
1 tsp Aleppo pepper or mild chili flakes
2 tbsp parsley, finely chopped, for garnish
steps: Warm 2 tbsp olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a pot over medium heat until butter foams, about 1 minute.
Add onion and carrot; cook, stirring, until softened and lightly sweet, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste, paprika, and cumin; cook to bloom spices, 1 minute.
Add rinsed red lentils and 4 cups stock; bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer for 18 to 22 minutes until lentils are very soft.
Season with 1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Off heat, blend with an immersion blender until silky, or mash for a rustic texture.
Return to low heat to adjust consistency with hot water or stock as needed; simmer 2 minutes. Stir in 1 tbsp lemon juice.
In a small pan, warm 1 tbsp olive oil over low heat; stir in Aleppo pepper until fragrant, 30 seconds. Do not burn.
Ladle soup into bowls, drizzle chili oil, garnish with parsley, and serve with lemon wedges.
tip: For vegan, replace butter with olive oil and use vegetable stock. Soup thickens as it sits; thin with hot water when reheating. Traditional sides: warm pita or Turkish bread.

title: Roasted Butternut Squash Soup
ing: 2 lb butternut squash, peeled, seeded, cubed
1/2 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/4 tsp black pepper, or to taste
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss squash with olive oil, 1/4 tsp salt, and a pinch of pepper. Spread on a sheet pan and roast until deeply tender and caramelized, 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once.
Meanwhile, warm a pot over medium heat. Add butter, then onion. Cook, stirring, until soft and translucent, 6 to 8 minutes. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Transfer roasted squash to the pot. Stir in broth, remaining salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend the soup smooth using an immersion blender in the pot, or carefully in batches in a countertop blender. Return to pot if needed.
Stir in heavy cream and gently warm over low heat for 2 minutes; do not boil. Taste and adjust salt and pepper.
Ladle into warm bowls and serve hot. Optional: garnish with a swirl of cream and freshly ground pepper.
tip: Swap vegetable broth for chicken to keep it vegetarian. Soup keeps 4 days refrigerated; reheat gently. For extra depth, add 1 peeled, chopped apple with the onion.

title: Potato Leek Soup
ing: 3 large leeks, white and light green parts only, sliced
1 lb russet potatoes, peeled and diced 1/2-inch
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 tbsp fresh chives, finely sliced, for garnish
steps: Melt 2 tbsp butter with 1 tbsp olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add sliced leeks and 1/2 tsp salt; cook, stirring, until soft but not browned, 10 to 12 minutes.
Add 1 lb diced potatoes, 4 cups stock, and 1 cup water. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce to low, cover partially, and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until potatoes are very tender.
Skim any foam. Using a potato masher, mash in the pot for a rustic texture, or blend with an immersion blender until silky; do not overblend to avoid gumminess.
Stir in 1/2 cup heavy cream. Warm gently over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes; do not boil. Season with remaining salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Add 1 tsp lemon juice if desired to brighten.
Ladle into warm bowls and garnish with finely sliced chives. Serve immediately with crusty bread.
tip: Swap chicken stock with vegetable stock for vegetarian. Soup keeps 3 days refrigerated; rewarm gently without boiling. For vichyssoise, chill thoroughly and serve cold with extra chives.

title: New England Clam Chowder
ing: 1 1/4 lb russet potatoes, peeled and 1/2-inch diced
1 tbsp fresh chives, chopped, for garnish
steps: Rinse and scrub 4 lb clams under cold water. In a large pot over high heat, add 1 cup water, bring to a boil, add clams, cover, and steam until they open, 6–8 minutes. Transfer clams to a bowl; strain and reserve 3 cups clam liquor.
When cool enough, remove clam meat from shells, discarding any that stayed closed. Chop clam meat into bite-size pieces; set aside. Rinse pot.
Set the pot over medium heat. Add bacon and cook until crisp, 6–8 minutes. Spoon off all but 2 tbsp fat; add 1 tbsp butter if needed to reach 2 tbsp fat total.
Add onion and celery; cook over medium heat until translucent, 5–6 minutes. Stir in thyme, then sprinkle in flour; cook, stirring, 2 minutes to form a pale roux.
Whisk in reserved clam liquor gradually, scraping the bottom. Add potatoes and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer, then cook uncovered until potatoes are tender, 12–15 minutes.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in whole milk and heavy cream; warm gently until steaming, 3–4 minutes—do not boil. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Add chopped clams and simmer very gently until just heated through, 2–3 minutes—do not overcook. Remove bay leaf; adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle into warm bowls. Sprinkle with parsley and chives. Serve hot with oyster crackers.
tip: Sub 2 cups bottled clam juice if short on liquor. Chowder keeps 2 days refrigerated; cool quickly and reheat gently without boiling to preserve texture.

title: Harira
ing: 1 lb bone-in lamb shank, cut into chunks
1/2 cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
1/2 cup all-purpose flour, whisked with 1 1/2 cups water (slurry)
steps: Warm 2 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add lamb and brown on all sides for 6–8 minutes.
Stir in onion, garlic, and celery; cook until softened, 4–5 minutes. Add cilantro, parsley, turmeric, ginger, cinnamon, pepper, and salt; stir 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomatoes, tomato paste, chickpeas, lentils, and 6 cups water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a lively simmer; cover and cook for 40 minutes until lamb is tender and lentils are nearly soft.
Skim foam as needed. Remove lamb bones if present, returning meat to the pot; shred large pieces.
Stir in vermicelli and simmer for 8 minutes until pasta is just tender.
Whisk flour with 1 1/2 cups water to make a smooth slurry. Gradually pour into the gently simmering soup, stirring constantly. Simmer 4–6 minutes more until lightly thickened to a velvety texture.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper. The soup should be bright, gently spiced, and lightly tangy; thin with hot water or simmer longer to reach preferred consistency.
Ladle hot into bowls and garnish with extra cilantro or lemon wedges, as desired.
tip: For a Ramadan touch, serve with dates and lemon. Substitute 1/2 lb diced beef for lamb if preferred; cook time may vary. Harira thickens as it rests—loosen with hot water when reheating.

title: Mulligatawny
ing: 1 medium tart apple, peeled and diced
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium; season chicken with salt and pepper, sear 3–4 minutes per side until browned. Remove and pour off excess fat, leaving 1 tbsp in pot.
Add onion to pot and cook over medium 5 minutes until translucent. Stir in garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute. Add curry powder, turmeric, and cayenne; toast 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in lentils, carrot, and apple. Return chicken to pot and add chicken stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer for 35 minutes, partly covered.
Remove chicken and cool 5 minutes. Simmer soup 5 minutes more until lentils are tender. Skim fat if needed.
Shred chicken, discarding skin and bones. Return meat to pot. Stir in coconut milk and simmer 5 minutes; adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in lemon juice. Ladle into warm bowls and garnish with cilantro. Serve hot.
tip: For a rice-thickened version, add 2 tbsp uncooked basmati with the lentils. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; thin with stock when reheating.

title: Wonton Soup
ing: 2 tbsp scallions, thinly sliced, for garnish
steps: Combine pork, shrimp, scallions, ginger, 2 tbsp light soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, 1 tsp sesame oil, sugar, white pepper, and half the beaten egg; stir vigorously until sticky, 2 minutes.

Lay out wrappers; place 2 tsp filling in center. Brush edges with remaining beaten egg, fold into a triangle, press to seal, then bring the two bottom corners together and pinch to form classic wontons.
Bring 6 cups chicken stock and 2 cups water to a gentle boil over medium-high heat; season with 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp light soy sauce. Reduce to a lively simmer.
In a separate pot, bring 3 quarts water to a boil. Add wontons in batches, stir to prevent sticking, and cook until they float plus 2 minutes, about 4 to 5 minutes total.
While wontons cook, warm 2 tsp sesame oil with 1 tbsp frying oil in a small pan over low heat for 1 minute to bloom aroma; drizzle into the soup base.
Transfer cooked wontons to serving bowls with a slotted spoon. Ladle hot broth over, ensuring 6 to 8 wontons per bowl.
Taste and adjust seasoning; garnish with sliced scallions and serve piping hot immediately.
tip: Swap pork with all-shrimp if preferred; add a pinch of white pepper to broth for extra warmth. Freeze uncooked wontons on a tray, then bag; boil from frozen 6 to 7 minutes.

title: Avgolemono
ing: 1 tbsp fresh dill, chopped, for garnish
1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Bring 6 cups chicken broth to a gentle boil over medium heat, then add 1/2 cup orzo and 1 tbsp olive oil. Reduce to a lively simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, 8 to 9 minutes.
While orzo cooks, crack 3 large eggs into a bowl. Whisk vigorously until frothy, 45 to 60 seconds, then whisk in 1/3 cup lemon juice and 1 tsp lemon zest until fully combined.
Lower soup to the barest simmer. Ladle 1 cup hot broth into a measuring cup. Very slowly drizzle the hot broth into the egg-lemon mixture, whisking constantly, until warm and slightly thickened.
Repeat with a second ladle (about 1 more cup) of hot broth, whisking constantly to temper without scrambling the eggs.

Turn off the heat. Slowly pour the tempered egg-lemon mixture back into the pot, stirring gently but continuously. Keep the soup below a simmer and cook over very low heat until slightly velvety, 3 to 5 minutes.
Season with 1/2 tsp kosher salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper. If the soup is too thick, whisk in a splash of hot water or broth; if too thin, warm gently 1 to 2 minutes more without boiling.
Ladle into warm bowls and garnish with 1 tbsp chopped dill and 1 tbsp chopped parsley. Serve immediately while silky and fragrant.
tip: For classic body, substitute 3 tbsp medium-grain rice for orzo and simmer 15 to 18 minutes. Leftovers keep 2 days; rewarm gently below a simmer to avoid curdling, adding hot water if needed.

title: Caldo Verde
ing: 1 lb russet potatoes, peeled and sliced 1/4 inch
8 oz collard greens, very thinly shredded
1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley, for garnish, as needed
steps: Warm 2 tbsp olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Add chouriço and fry until edges render and brown, 3 to 4 minutes. Lift chouriço out and reserve; leave drippings in pot.
Add onion to the pot and cook until translucent, 5 to 6 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant, without browning.
Add potatoes and stock. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a gentle simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are very tender.
