Mash most potatoes against the pot sides or use an immersion blender for 5 to 10 seconds to achieve a mostly smooth, lightly rustic texture.
Return the chouriço to the pot. Stir in collard greens, salt, and pepper. Simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes until greens are tender but bright.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper. Ladle into warm bowls, drizzle each with a little olive oil, and garnish with parsley. Serve hot.
tip: For tradition, use Galician cabbage or true Portuguese couve; very thinly shred greens for the signature silkiness. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; thin with a splash of stock when reheating.

title: Corn Chowder
ing: 2 tbsp fresh chives, thinly sliced, for garnish
steps: Place a heavy pot over medium heat and cook bacon until crisp, 6 to 8 minutes; spoon off all but 1 tbsp fat, adding 1 tbsp frying oil if needed.
Add onion and celery; cook, stirring, until softened, 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in potatoes, corn, milk, chicken broth, bay leaf, thyme, 1/2 tsp salt, and pepper. Bring just to a bare simmer over medium, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
In a small pan, melt butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook, stirring, 1 to 2 minutes to form a blond roux.
Whisk roux into the chowder. Simmer gently, stirring, until slightly thickened, 5 to 7 minutes. Do not boil to avoid curdling milk.
Remove bay leaf. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. If thicker texture is desired, lightly mash a few potatoes against the pot side and stir back in.
Ladle into warm bowls and garnish with chives and reserved crisp bacon if desired. Serve hot.
tip: Sub 3 cups thawed frozen corn when fresh isn’t available. Chowder keeps 3 days refrigerated; cool quickly and reheat gently over low heat, adding a splash of milk if needed.

title: Pasta e Fagioli
ing: 1 (15 oz) can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Warm 2 tbsp olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add pancetta and cook, stirring, until rendered and lightly golden, about 6 minutes.
Add onion, celery, and carrot with a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring, until very soft and sweet but not browned, 8 to 10 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Clear a spot, add tomato paste, and cook until brick red, 1 minute. Stir in rosemary and bay leaf, then add crushed tomatoes; simmer for 3 minutes to concentrate.
Pour in chicken broth and 1 cup water. Add Parmigiano rind. Bring to a simmer, then cook gently for 15 minutes to meld flavors.
Mash half of the cannellini beans with a fork. Stir all beans (mashed and whole) into the pot; simmer 5 minutes. Season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper.
Stir in ditalini and cook at a gentle boil, stirring often, until al dente, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove rosemary, bay leaf, and cheese rind.
Adjust thickness with hot water for a brothy bowl or simmer 2 to 3 minutes longer for thicker. Taste and adjust salt and pepper.
Ladle into warm bowls. Finish each with a drizzle of olive oil, chopped parsley, and grated Parmigiano. Serve hot.
tip: Swap pancetta with 2 tbsp olive oil for vegetarian; use vegetable broth. Soup thickens as it rests—loosen with hot water when reheating.

title: Solyanka
ing: 12 oz mixed cured meats (ham, smoked sausage, salami), cut into matchsticks
1/4 cup fresh dill, chopped, for garnish
steps: Brown beef in 1 tbsp oil over medium-high for 6–8 minutes until well browned; reduce heat and add onion. Cook 5 minutes until translucent.
Stir in tomato paste; cook 1 minute. Add cured meats; sauté 3 minutes to render and lightly brown.
Add beef broth, bay leaf, and pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes until beef is tender (beef should reach 145°F minimum).
Add diced pickles, pickle brine, capers, olives, and half the dill. Simmer for 10 minutes to meld flavors.
Taste and balance: add a pinch of sugar if overly sharp, or a splash more brine for brightness. Adjust salt to taste (cured meats are salty).
Remove bay leaf. Ladle into warm bowls. Float 2 lemon slices per bowl on top.
Serve hot with a spoonful of sour cream and remaining dill sprinkled over each portion.
tip: Use any trio of smoked/cured meats you have. Soup keeps 3 days chilled; reheat gently without boiling. For fish solyanka, swap meats for 1 lb firm fish and use fish stock.

title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
ing: 1 lb ripe tomatoes, cut into chunky wedges
1 medium cucumber, peeled in stripes, halved lengthwise and sliced 1/2-inch thick
1 green bell pepper, cored and sliced into rings
6 oz Greek feta cheese, cut into a thick slab
1 tsp dried oregano, plus more to taste
steps: Combine tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and green bell pepper in a wide salad bowl; keep pieces chunky for rustic texture.
Add Kalamata olives and capers, then gently toss once to distribute without bruising the tomatoes.
Whisk olive oil, red wine vinegar, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper in a small bowl until emulsified, about 20 seconds.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss gently to coat evenly; let stand for 5 minutes to meld flavors.
Place the feta slab on top of the dressed salad, drizzle with a little extra olive oil if desired, and sprinkle a pinch more oregano.
Serve immediately at cool room temperature for best flavor; do not chill after dressing.
tip: For authenticity, keep feta in one slab rather than crumbles. If tomatoes are very juicy, skip salt in dressing and season at the table. Leftovers keep 1 day chilled; bring to room temp before serving.

title: Caprese Salad
steps: Pat tomato and mozzarella slices dry with paper towels to reduce excess moisture.
On a platter, alternate tomato and mozzarella slices with whole basil leaves, slightly overlapping, forming a neat ring or rows.
Drizzle 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil evenly over the salad.
Sprinkle 1/2 tsp kosher salt and 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper evenly over the slices.
Optional: Drizzle 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar lightly over the tomatoes only to avoid masking the cheese.
Serve immediately at cool room temperature (68–72°F) for best flavor; do not chill once assembled.
tip: Use peak-season heirloom tomatoes for best flavor; swap balsamic with a few drops of aged balsamic or omit for strict traditionalists. Store leftovers up to 1 day, covered and chilled; bring to room temp before serving.

title: Cobb Salad
steps: Cook bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp, 8 to 10 minutes; drain on paper towels and crumble.
Place eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water, bring to a boil, then cover, remove from heat, and stand 10 minutes. Cool under cold water, peel, and chop.
Whisk red wine vinegar, olive oil, Dijon, Worcestershire, sugar, salt, and pepper in a bowl until emulsified.
Combine romaine and iceberg in a large platter or bowl. Toss lightly with 3 tbsp dressing to coat greens.
Arrange neat rows of chicken, tomatoes, blue cheese, avocado, scallions, bacon, and chopped eggs over the greens.
Drizzle remaining dressing over the salad just before serving, or pass at the table for guests to add to taste.
Serve immediately so the lettuces stay crisp.
tip: Use leftover roast chicken or turkey. For make-ahead, prep components up to 1 day; keep lettuce and avocado uncut until serving and hold bacon and dressing separate to preserve crunch and emulsion.

title: Salade Niçoise
ing: 10 oz oil-packed tuna, drained and flaked
steps: Place 12 oz potatoes in a pot, cover with cold salted water, bring to a boil, then simmer until just tender, 12–15 minutes. Drain and cool 5 minutes, then halve.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch 8 oz green beans until crisp-tender, 2–3 minutes. Transfer to ice water to chill, then drain and pat dry.
Place 4 large eggs in a saucepan, cover with water, bring to a gentle boil, then simmer 7 minutes for jammy centers. Cool in ice water 5 minutes, peel, and halve.
Whisk 1/4 cup olive oil, 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tsp Dijon, 1 tsp chopped capers, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/8 tsp pepper until emulsified.
In a large bowl, gently toss potatoes and green beans with 2 tbsp dressing to coat while warm.
Arrange lettuce on a platter. Neatly distribute dressed potatoes, green beans, 10 oz tuna, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, 1/2 cup olives, and 6 anchovies.
Drizzle remaining dressing over the salad. Nestle halved eggs on top and spoon a little dressing over them.
Serve at once at cool room temperature; do not chill, to preserve aromas and texture.
tip: Use high-quality oil-packed tuna and small Niçoise olives for authenticity. Components can be cooked up to 1 day ahead; keep chilled separately and bring to cool room temp before assembling.

title: Waldorf Salad
ing: 1/2 cup walnuts, toasted and coarsely chopped
steps: Whisk mayonnaise, sour cream, lemon juice, salt, and pepper in a large bowl until smooth, about 30 seconds.
Add apples, celery, grapes, walnuts, and raisins; toss gently to coat evenly, 1 to 2 minutes.
Cover and chill to meld flavors for 10 minutes in the refrigerator.
Line a platter or four plates with the lettuce.
Spoon the salad over the lettuce and sprinkle with parsley just before serving.
tip: Toast walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant. For a lighter dressing, use all yogurt in place of sour cream and some of the mayonnaise.

title: Fattoush
ing: 2 pitas, split and cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tsp sumac, plus more for garnish
steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Toss pita pieces with 3 tbsp olive oil and 1/4 tsp salt, spread on a sheet pan, and bake until crisp and golden, 8–12 minutes. Cool completely.
In a small bowl, whisk lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, 2 tbsp olive oil, red wine vinegar, 1 tsp sumac, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp pepper until emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine romaine, cucumbers, tomatoes, radishes, scallions, mint, and parsley.
Add half the dressing to the vegetables and toss gently to coat. Let sit 5 minutes to slightly wilt the greens.
Just before serving, add the cooled toasted pita and remaining dressing. Toss until the pita is glossy and the salad is evenly coated.
Taste and adjust seasoning with a pinch more salt or sumac as desired. Serve immediately so the pita stays crisp.
tip: For extra crunch, pan-fry pita in 2 tbsp oil until deep golden. If pomegranate molasses is very tangy, balance with 1/2 tsp honey. Add purslane when in season for a classic touch.

title: Panzanella
ing: 12 oz day-old rustic bread, cut into 1-inch chunks
1 1/2 lb ripe tomatoes, cut into bite-size wedges
steps: Warm 2 tbsp frying oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add bread and toast, stirring, until edges are golden and dry, 6 to 8 minutes; cool completely.
In a small bowl, whisk olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt, and black pepper until emulsified.
Place tomatoes in a large bowl and toss with 1 tbsp of the dressing; let stand 10 minutes to release juices.
Add cucumber, red onion, capers, and toasted bread to the tomatoes. Pour over remaining dressing and the tomato juices; toss thoroughly until bread is evenly moistened.
Add torn basil and gently toss again. Let the salad stand at room temperature for 15 to 20 minutes, tossing once, until bread is plush but not soggy. Adjust seasoning and serve.
tip: Use truly ripe summer tomatoes and sturdy country bread. If bread is very hard, lightly sprinkle with water before toasting. Salad holds 4 hours at room temp; refresh with a splash of vinegar before serving.

title: Som Tam (Green Papaya Salad)
ing: 2 tbsp dried shrimp, rinsed and patted dry
1 lime, cut in wedges, for serving
1 cup cabbage, cut into wedges, for serving
steps: Pound 2 cloves garlic and 2 Thai chilies in a mortar until a coarse paste forms, about 30 seconds.
Add 2 tbsp palm sugar and pound to dissolve, then add 2 tbsp dried shrimp and lightly bruise to release aroma, 15 seconds.
Add 1/2 cup green beans and bruise just until creased, 10 to 15 seconds, keeping pieces mostly whole.
Add 1 cup halved cherry tomatoes and bruise gently to release juices, 10 seconds. Stir in 3 tbsp fish sauce and 3 tbsp lime juice until the sugar fully dissolves.
Add 2 cups shredded green papaya. Use the pestle to lightly pound while tossing with a spoon until evenly coated and slightly wilted, 1 to 2 minutes.
Taste and adjust the balance: add fish sauce for salt, lime for sour, or palm sugar for sweetness. Toss in 1/4 cup roasted peanuts.
Serve immediately with cabbage wedges and lime on the side. Drizzle a few drops of frying oil as needed to gloss, if desired.
tip: Unripe papaya should be firm and pale green; soak shreds in ice water 5 minutes, then drain well for extra crunch. For vegetarian, replace fish sauce with soy sauce and dried shrimp with extra peanuts.

title: Sunomono (Japanese Cucumber Salad)
ing: 2 oz wakame seaweed, dried, soaked and drained
1 tsp toasted sesame seeds, for garnish, as needed
steps: Slice cucumbers into 1/8-inch rounds. Toss with 1 tsp kosher salt and let stand 10 minutes to draw out moisture.
Rinse cucumbers under cold water to remove excess salt, then squeeze gently by handfuls to expel liquid. Pat dry.
Soak dried wakame in cold water for 5 minutes until rehydrated, then drain well and squeeze out excess water. Chop large pieces.
In a bowl, whisk rice vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and grated ginger until sugar dissolves, about 1 minute.
Add cucumbers, wakame, pickled ginger, and scallions to the bowl; toss to coat evenly. Chill for 5–10 minutes for flavors to marry.
Divide among 4 small bowls and sprinkle with white and black sesame seeds. Garnish with extra toasted sesame seeds as needed and serve cold.
tip: For a sweeter style, increase sugar to 1½ tbsp. If using Persian cucumbers, use 4 and peel optional. Salad keeps covered and chilled up to 24 hours; re-toss before serving.

title: Larb
ing: 1 cup chopped fresh herbs, mix of mint and cilantro
2 tbsp finely chopped lemongrass, tender inner stalk only
1 to 3 tbsp toasted chili flakes, to taste
steps: Toast rice in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, until deep golden and nutty, 10 to 12 minutes. Cool, then grind to a coarse powder with a mortar and pestle or spice grinder.

In a skillet, add pork and 2 tbsp warm water. Cook over medium heat, stirring and breaking up, until just cooked through and no pink remains, 5 to 7 minutes; temperature should reach 160°F. Cool 5 minutes.
In a large bowl, whisk lime juice, fish sauce, salt, white pepper, and half of the toasted rice powder until dissolved.
Add warm cooked pork to the bowl along with shallots, scallions, lemongrass, and chili flakes. Toss gently to coat and let stand 3 minutes to absorb flavors.
Fold in chopped mint and cilantro. Sprinkle in more toasted rice powder to taste for body and fragrance, tossing to distribute evenly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more fish sauce, lime juice, or chili flakes. The balance should be bright, savory, and lightly spicy.
Serve larb at room temperature with lettuce leaves and cucumber. Sprinkle a final pinch of rice powder on top and eat with sticky rice if desired.
tip: For chicken larb, use ground chicken and cook to 165°F. Make rice powder ahead; store airtight 1 month. Sticky rice is traditional on the side; add extra chili flakes for Lao heat.

title: Tabbouleh
ing: 1/4 cup fine bulgur, rinsed and drained
1 cup fresh mint leaves, finely chopped
1 cup romaine leaves, torn, for serving
steps: Place 1/4 cup fine bulgur in a small bowl, rinse under cold water, drain well, then let stand to soften in its residual moisture for 10 minutes.
Wash and dry parsley and mint thoroughly; finely chop by hand with a sharp knife to avoid bruising.
In a large bowl, combine chopped parsley, mint, tomatoes, and scallions; fluff with fingers to keep herbs airy.
Squeeze any excess moisture from the bulgur; add to the bowl and toss to distribute evenly.
In a small bowl, whisk 1/3 cup lemon juice, 1/3 cup olive oil, 1 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp pepper until emulsified.
Pour dressing over the salad; toss gently but thoroughly to coat every leaf.
Let tabbouleh rest for 10 minutes at room temperature to meld flavors; taste and adjust lemon or salt if needed.
Serve mounded with torn romaine leaves on the side; enjoy immediately for brightest flavor.
tip: Use the finest bulgur (#1); it softens without boiling. For make-ahead, chop herbs dry and keep components separate up to 6 hours; dress and add tomatoes just before serving.

title: Kachumber
steps: Combine 2 cups finely diced cucumber, 1 cup finely diced tomatoes, and 1/2 cup finely diced red onion in a mixing bowl.
Add 1/4 cup chopped cilantro, 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp roasted cumin, 1/8 tsp red chili powder, and a pinch of black pepper.
Toss gently until the vegetables are evenly coated; taste and adjust salt, lemon, and chili to preference.
Rest for 5 minutes at room temperature to meld flavors, then toss once more and serve immediately.
tip: For extra aroma, dry-roast whole cumin and grind fresh. Swap lemon with 2 tsp lime juice. Best eaten fresh; if prepping ahead, dice veg and chill separately, then dress just before serving.

title: Shirazi Salad
ing: 1/2 cup fresh herbs, finely chopped, mix of mint and parsley
steps: Combine cucumbers, tomatoes, and red onion in a large bowl; dice to pea-size for authentic texture.
Add chopped fresh herbs and sprinkle in dried mint; toss gently to distribute aromatics evenly.
Whisk lime juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper in a small bowl until emulsified, about 15 seconds.
Pour dressing over salad and fold gently until vegetables are lightly coated, about 30 seconds.
Taste and adjust salt, pepper, and lime to balance brightness and seasoning.
Chill for 10 minutes to meld flavors, then serve immediately while crisp.
tip: For best texture, deseed very juicy tomatoes. Salad is best within 2–4 hours; if prepping ahead, keep dressing separate and combine up to 15 minutes before serving.

title: Guacamole
ing: 1 small Roma tomato, cored and diced
steps: Place onion and jalapeño in a bowl with salt and lime juice, stir, and let stand for 5 minutes to mellow and season.
Add diced avocados and gently mash with a fork until mostly creamy with small chunks, about 1–2 minutes.
Fold in cilantro and black pepper, then fold in diced tomato just until combined.
Taste and adjust salt or lime. If serving later, press plastic wrap directly onto the surface.
Serve at room temperature with tortilla chips or as a topping.
tip: For milder heat, use half a jalapeño or remove all seeds. Refrigerate up to 1 day with plastic wrap pressed on the surface to reduce browning; re-season with a pinch of salt and lime before serving.

title: Vietnamese Fresh Spring Rolls
ing: 1 cup fresh herbs, mixed mint and cilantro
steps: Bring a medium pot of water to a boil over high heat. Add shrimp and 1/2 tsp salt, simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until opaque and 145°F, then drain, cool, peel, and slice each shrimp in half lengthwise.
In the same pot, boil fresh water. Add rice vermicelli and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until tender; drain, rinse under cold water, and drain well. Toss with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of pepper.
Prep fillings: julienne cucumber and carrot, tear lettuce into roll-sized pieces, pick mint and cilantro leaves, and slice scallions. Set up a damp towel-lined board for rolling.
Make dipping sauce: whisk hoisin, peanut butter, water, and rice vinegar in a small bowl until smooth; adjust thickness with a splash of water if needed.
Fill a wide bowl with warm water (about 110°F). Dip one rice paper wrapper for 5 to 7 seconds until pliable, then lay on the damp towel; do not over-soak.
Layer fillings in the lower third: a small tuft of noodles (about 1/4 cup), a few cucumber and carrot strips, a piece of lettuce, herbs, and scallions; sprinkle with peanuts.
Fold the sides over, lift the bottom edge to encase the filling, roll one turn, place 2 shrimp halves pink side down along the top edge, then continue to roll tightly to seal.
Repeat with remaining wrappers and fillings, keeping finished rolls covered with a barely damp towel to prevent drying. Serve immediately with hoisin-peanut sauce.
tip: For a classic nước chấm dip, mix fish sauce, lime, sugar, water, garlic, and chili. Rolls keep 4 hours chilled and covered; refresh the surface with a damp towel if slightly dry.

title: Pork and Chive Potstickers
steps: Toss 1 cup napa cabbage with 1/2 tsp kosher salt and rest 10 minutes; squeeze out excess liquid firmly.

In a bowl, mix 1 lb ground pork, squeezed cabbage, 2 cups chopped chives, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 2 cloves minced garlic, 1 tsp sugar, and 1/2 tsp white pepper.
Stir in 1/4 cup cold water a tablespoon at a time until the filling is sticky and cohesive, about 2 minutes of vigorous stirring.
Fill wrappers: place 1 tbsp filling in center, dab edges with water, fold into a half-moon, pleat and press to seal; repeat to make about 48 potstickers.
Heat a 10–12 inch nonstick or cast-iron skillet over medium-high; add 1 tbsp frying oil. Arrange 12–15 potstickers flat-side down and fry until bottoms are golden, 2–3 minutes.
Carefully pour in 1/3 cup water, cover immediately, and steam on medium for 5–6 minutes until most water evaporates and pork reaches 160°F.
Uncover and cook 1–2 minutes to re-crisp bottoms; transfer to a tray. Repeat with remaining dumplings, adding oil and water as needed.
Stir 1/4 cup rice vinegar, 1/4 cup soy sauce, and 1 tsp chili oil to make the dipping sauce; serve hot potstickers with sauce.
tip: Substitute garlic chives with scallions if needed. Freeze uncooked, well-spaced on a tray, then bag; cook from frozen, adding 2–3 minutes to steaming time.

title: Stuffed Mushrooms
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Line a sheet pan with parchment. Gently twist stems from mushrooms; reserve stems. Arrange caps, hollow side up, on the pan; brush lightly with 1 tbsp olive oil.
Finely chop reserved stems. Warm 2 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp frying oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add chopped stems and a pinch of salt; cook until moisture evaporates, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in garlic and crushed red pepper; cook 30 seconds. Add white wine; simmer until nearly dry, about 2 minutes. Transfer mixture to a bowl to cool 5 minutes.
Add breadcrumbs, Parmigiano-Reggiano, parsley, remaining 2 tbsp butter (melted), black pepper, and a pinch of salt to the bowl; mix until evenly moistened and clumping slightly.
Taste filling; adjust salt and pepper to taste. Pack filling firmly into mushroom caps, mounding slightly. Drizzle with remaining 1 tbsp olive oil.
Pour chicken broth onto the pan around the mushrooms to create gentle steam. Bake at 400°F until caps are tender and tops are golden, 18 to 22 minutes.
For a deeper crust, broil on high for 1 to 2 minutes, watching closely. Let rest 5 minutes so juices settle before serving warm.
tip: Swap chicken broth with vegetable broth for vegetarian. Filling can be made 1 day ahead; refrigerate and stuff just before baking.

title: Spinach Artichoke Dip
ing: 10 oz frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
14 oz canned artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Lightly grease an 8-inch baking dish with 1 tbsp olive oil.
In a bowl, beat 8 oz cream cheese until smooth. Mix in 1/2 cup sour cream and 1/2 cup mayonnaise until creamy.
Stir in 1 cup mozzarella, 1/2 cup Parmesan, 2 cloves minced garlic, 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp pepper.
Fold in 10 oz well-drained spinach and 14 oz chopped artichoke hearts until evenly combined.
Spread mixture in the prepared dish and smooth the top. Bake at 375°F for 20 to 25 minutes until hot and bubbling at the edges.
Broil on high for 1 to 2 minutes until the top is lightly golden; watch closely to avoid burning. Rest 5 minutes before serving.
tip: Swap 1/2 cup mozzarella with Monterey Jack for extra melt. Make ahead: assemble, cover, and refrigerate up to 24 hours; bake 5 to 10 minutes longer from cold.

title: Mozzarella Sticks
ing: 16 oz low-moisture whole-milk mozzarella, cut into 18 sticks
1 1/2 cups marinara sauce, warmed for serving
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Cut mozzarella into 3x1/2x1/2-inch sticks. Pat very dry with paper towels to minimize splatter and help coating adhere.
Set up dredging: bowl 1—flour, salt, pepper. Bowl 2—eggs whisked with milk. Bowl 3—breadcrumbs, Parmesan, garlic powder, oregano, paprika, cayenne; mix well.
Coat sticks: dredge in flour, shake excess; dip in egg; roll in breadcrumb mix. Repeat egg and breadcrumb coating once more for a thick seal.
Arrange breaded sticks on a parchment-lined sheet and freeze until very firm, 20–30 minutes; this prevents cheese blowouts when frying.
Heat frying oil to 350°F in a heavy pot (oil at least 2 inches deep). Maintain 325–350°F throughout frying; adjust heat as needed.
Fry in batches without crowding until deeply golden, 1 1/2–2 minutes, turning once. Internal cheese will be melted; exterior should be crisp.
Transfer to a rack set over a sheet pan; immediately season lightly with salt to taste. Let rest 1 minute so crust sets.
Serve hot with warmed marinara sauce and a sprinkle of chopped parsley for garnish.
tip: Double-coat and freeze thoroughly to prevent leaks. Freeze uncooked breaded sticks up to 1 month; fry from frozen, adding 30–60 seconds and ensuring color is deep golden.

title: Jalapeño Poppers
steps: Heat oven to 400°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with a wire rack for even crisping.
Stir cream cheese, cheddar, bacon, salt, pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder until smooth, about 1 minute.
Fill each jalapeño half with 1 to 1.5 tbsp cheese mixture, mounding slightly but keeping flush with edges.
Set up dredging: place flour in one bowl, beaten eggs in a second, and breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge each stuffed jalapeño: coat in flour, dip in egg, then press into breadcrumbs to fully cover the filling and cut edges.
Arrange poppers cut-side up on the rack, mist lightly with oil or brush with 1 tbsp frying oil.
Bake at 400°F until peppers are tender and crumbs are golden, 18 to 22 minutes; rest 5 minutes before serving.
Optional extra-crisp: shallow-fry baked poppers in 350°F oil for 45 to 60 seconds per side, then drain on a rack.
tip: Swap cheddar for pepper jack for extra heat. Make ahead: bread and chill up to 24 hours; bake from cold, adding 2 to 3 minutes. Serve with ranch or salsa for dipping.

title: Arancini
steps: Bring 4 cups chicken broth to a boil, add 2 cups rice and 1/2 tsp salt, reduce to low, cover, and cook until tender and broth is absorbed, about 18 minutes; spread on a tray to steam off for 10 minutes.
While warm, fold in 2 tbsp butter and 1/2 cup grated Parmigiano; cool to room temperature, then mix in 2 beaten eggs. Chill the rice mixture covered for 30 minutes to firm.
Make the ragù: brown 8 oz ground beef with 2 oz pancetta over medium-high for 5 minutes; add 1/2 cup onion and cook 3 minutes. Deglaze with 1/2 cup wine and reduce 2 minutes.
Stir in 3/4 cup passata, 1/2 tsp pepper, and a pinch of salt; simmer on low for 12 minutes until thick. Fold in 1/2 cup blanched peas and cool completely, 15 minutes.
Set breading station: 1 1/2 cups flour in one bowl, 1 cup water whisked with a pinch of salt in another, and 2 cups breadcrumbs in a third.
With damp hands, scoop about 1/3 cup rice, flatten in palm, add 1 tbsp ragù and 1 cube mozzarella; enclose with more rice to form a ball or cone about 2 1/4 inches wide. Repeat to make 12.
Dredge each arancino in flour, dip in salted water, then coat in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to seal. Rest formed arancini 10 minutes to set the crust.
Heat frying oil to 350°F in a deep pot; fry arancini in batches, turning, until deep golden, 4 to 5 minutes. Drain on a rack and season lightly with kosher salt.
Serve hot; the center cheese should be melted and the rice tender. Hold in a 200°F oven up to 20 minutes before serving.
tip: Swap beef with finely chopped leftover ragù alla bolognese if on hand. Cooled, fried arancini keep 2 days refrigerated; re-crisp at 350°F for 12 minutes.

title: Onion Bhaji
steps: Combine gram flour, rice flour, salt, turmeric, cumin, coriander, chili powder, black pepper, and baking powder in a large bowl.
Add ginger, garlic, cilantro, and lemon juice, then drizzle in 3/4 cup cold water to form a thick batter; it should cling to onions. Rest the batter for 10 minutes.
Toss in the sliced onions and squeeze with your hands to lightly bruise and release moisture; the mixture should hold in loose clumps. If dry, add up to 1/4 cup more water.
Heat frying oil in a deep pot to 350°F over medium heat. Line a tray with paper towels and set a wire rack on top.
Using moistened fingers, drop golf-ball-size loose clumps (about 2 tbsp each) into the oil without packing tight; fry 6 to 8 minutes at 325–350°F, turning until deep golden and crisp.
Maintain oil temperature between 325–350°F. Fry in batches to avoid crowding, returning oil to 350°F between batches.
Drain bhajis on the rack. Season lightly with a pinch of salt while hot and rest 2 minutes to set the crust.
Serve hot with mint chutney and tamarind sauce.
tip: For extra crispness, add 1 tbsp hot oil to the batter before onions. Keep warm on a 250°F rack up to 20 minutes. Substitute scallions for part of the onions for a lighter flavor.

title: Elote (Mexican Street Corn)
ing: 6 ears corn, husks on for grilling, silks removed
steps: Preheat grill to medium-high (425°F). Pull husks back from each ear, remove silks, then fold husks back. Lightly brush corn with frying oil.
Grill corn over direct heat, turning every 2 to 3 minutes, until kernels are tender and charred in spots, 10 to 12 minutes. Keep warm.
In a bowl, whisk mayonnaise, Mexican crema, lime juice, chili powder, cayenne, salt, and black pepper until smooth.
Peel husks back to form a handle or remove completely. Brush hot corn generously with the crema mixture to coat all sides.
Roll or sprinkle corn with crumbled cotija, pressing so it adheres. Sprinkle a pinch more chili powder if desired.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve immediately with lime wedges for squeezing.
tip: Swap Mexican crema with 1/3 cup sour cream plus 1 tbsp milk. Grill corn up to 1 hour ahead; warm over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, then sauce and cheese just before serving.

title: Bruschetta al Pomodoro
ing: 1 lb ripe tomatoes, cored and finely diced
1/2 cup fresh basil leaves, thinly sliced
1 loaf rustic Italian bread (about 12 oz), sliced 1/2-inch thick
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for brushing
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for finishing
steps: Combine tomatoes, 1/4 cup olive oil, red wine vinegar, grated garlic, 1/2 tsp salt, and pepper in a bowl; fold in basil. Let macerate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Preheat broiler to high or heat a grill to medium-high (about 450–500°F). Arrange bread slices on a sheet pan if broiling.
Brush both sides of bread with 2 tbsp olive oil. Broil or grill, turning once, until crisp at edges and well toasted with light char, 2–4 minutes total.
While hot, lightly rub one side of each slice with the cut side of the halved garlic clove.
Taste tomatoes and adjust seasoning with a pinch more salt or vinegar if needed. Spoon a generous mound onto each slice, letting juices soak in.
Finish with a light sprinkle of the finishing salt and drizzle 1 tbsp olive oil over the bruschette. Serve immediately.
tip: Use the ripest in-season tomatoes; if very juicy, drain briefly before mixing. Toast bread just before serving; topping can be made 1 hour ahead and kept at room temp.

title: Crab Rangoon
steps: In a bowl, mix cream cheese, crab, scallions, soy sauce, Worcestershire, sugar, garlic powder, salt, and white pepper until smooth and cohesive, about 1 minute.
Lay 6 wonton wrappers on a board. Brush edges lightly with beaten egg. Place 1 tbsp filling in the center of each.
Fold into a four-corner star: bring opposite corners together, press out air, then pinch all edges firmly to seal. Repeat with remaining wrappers and filling.
Set a wire rack over a sheet pan. Heat frying oil in a heavy pot to 350°F over medium heat; maintain 340–360°F throughout frying.
Fry 6 rangoons at a time until deeply golden and blistered, 2 to 3 minutes, turning once. Transfer to rack to drain; let stand 2 minutes to finish crisping.
Whisk sweet chili sauce with rice vinegar in a small bowl. Taste and adjust with a pinch of salt if needed.
Serve rangoons hot with dipping sauce. If any leak while frying, remove, cool slightly, and reseal seams on the next batch by pressing together more firmly.
tip: Seal well: dry edges, then egg-wash and pinch hard to prevent leaks. Make-ahead: Form and freeze on a tray; fry from frozen at 350°F for 3–4 minutes.

title: Takoyaki
ing: 1/3 cup beni shoga (red pickled ginger), finely chopped
steps: Whisk flour, dashi, eggs, soy sauce, and salt until very smooth; rest the batter for 15 minutes to hydrate.
Preheat a takoyaki pan over medium heat for 3 minutes. Lightly brush each well with frying oil until glistening.
Fill each well almost to the top with batter. Drop octopus pieces into centers, then sprinkle with tenkasu, scallions, and beni shoga.
As edges set (about 1 to 2 minutes), use skewers to scrape overflow toward each well and begin turning 90° to tuck batter underneath.
Continue rotating balls every 30 to 45 seconds for even shaping and browning; cook until deeply golden and crisp outside, about 6 to 8 minutes total.
Transfer takoyaki to a tray. Brush with takoyaki sauce while hot, then drizzle with Japanese mayonnaise in thin lines.
Shower with katsuobushi and aonori to finish. Serve immediately while the centers are custardy.
tip: Boil raw octopus in lightly salted water for 40–50 minutes until tender, then chill before chopping. Keep the pan well-oiled; excess batter helps form round balls—trim edges with the skewer as you turn.

title: Tzatziki
steps: Set a fine-mesh sieve over a bowl, add the grated cucumber, sprinkle with 1/4 tsp of the salt, and let drain for 10 minutes, then squeeze firmly to remove as much liquid as possible.
In a mixing bowl, whisk the Greek yogurt until smooth, 30 seconds, then whisk in olive oil, lemon juice, and vinegar until glossy and combined.
Stir in garlic, dill, optional mint, remaining 1/4 tsp salt, and black pepper until evenly distributed.
Fold in the well-squeezed cucumber until fully incorporated and the mixture is thick and scoopable.
Cover and chill for at least 60 minutes to meld flavors; keep refrigerated at 40°F or below until serving.
Stir, taste, and adjust salt or lemon to preference, then drizzle with a little olive oil before serving.
tip: Use thick, well-strained yogurt; watery yogurt thins the dip. Tzatziki keeps refrigerated for 3 days; stir before serving. For lactose-free, use strained lactose-free Greek-style yogurt.

title: Pão de Queijo
ing: 5 oz queijo Minas padrão, finely grated
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Line two sheet pans with parchment paper.
Bring 1 cup whole milk, 1/2 cup frying oil, and 1 tsp kosher salt to a full simmer over medium heat, 3 to 4 minutes.
Place 2 cups tapioca flour in a bowl. Pour the hot liquid over it and mix with a spoon until evenly moistened. Cool 5 minutes.
Beat in 2 large eggs one at a time until smooth and glossy. Fold in 5 oz queijo Minas and 3 oz Parmesan until evenly distributed.
Lightly oil hands; pinch off golf‑ball pieces (about 1 oz each) and roll smooth. Arrange 2 inches apart on pans.
Bake at 400°F until puffed, set, and lightly golden on spots, 18 to 22 minutes. Centers should be elastic, not wet. Serve hot.
tip: Queijo Minas is traditional; if unavailable, use 6 oz total of Parmesan plus mild provolone. Shape and freeze raw balls on a tray, then bag; bake from frozen at 400°F for 22–26 minutes.

title: Queso Fundido
ing: 12 oz Mexican chorizo, casings removed, crumbled
2 tbsp canned diced green chiles, drained
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Place a 10-inch oven-safe skillet or small cast-iron on the middle rack to preheat for 5 minutes.
Add oil to the hot skillet, then the chorizo. Cook over medium heat on the stovetop, stirring, until browned and cooked through, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in onion and cook until softened, 3 to 4 minutes. Add garlic and green chiles; cook until fragrant, 30 to 45 seconds. Remove from heat.
Toss Oaxaca and Monterey Jack together. Spread half over the chorizo mixture, then layer the remaining cheese evenly on top.
Bake at 425°F until the cheese is fully melted and bubbling with lightly browned spots, 8 to 10 minutes. Rotate once for even browning.
Carefully remove; season with pepper to taste. Rest 2 minutes so the cheese sets slightly. Garnish with cilantro.
Serve immediately, family-style, with warm tortillas and lime wedges. Scoop the molten cheese-chorizo into tortillas and eat hot.
tip: Substitute part-skim low-moisture mozzarella for Oaxaca if needed. Keep warm at the table over a small candle warmer; reheat gently in a 350°F oven for 5 minutes if it firms up.

title: Crème Brûlée
ing: as needed boiling water, for water bath
steps: Heat oven to 325°F. Set 8 (6-oz) ramekins in a deep roasting pan. Put a kettle of water on to boil for the water bath.

Warm cream and half-and-half with 6 tbsp sugar and salt in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring, until steaming with small bubbles at edges, 5–7 minutes. Do not boil. Remove from heat; stir in vanilla.
In a bowl, whisk yolks with remaining 4 tbsp sugar just until blended and slightly lightened, 30–45 seconds. Do not whip in excess air.
Slowly whisk warm dairy into yolks in a thin stream to temper. Strain custard through a fine sieve into a pitcher to remove bubbles and any chalazae.
Divide custard among ramekins. Skim surface bubbles with a spoon for an even top.
Pour boiling water into the pan to come halfway up ramekins. Bake at 325°F until edges are set and centers quiver slightly when jiggled, 30–35 minutes.
Transfer ramekins to a rack to cool 1 hour, then cover and chill until fully set, at least 3 hours or up to 3 days.

Just before serving, blot any condensation. Sprinkle 1 tsp sugar evenly over each custard. Torch with a kitchen torch until deep amber and glassy, 30–60 seconds, or broil 5–8 inches from heat 3–5 minutes, rotating for even caramelization. Let stand 5 minutes to harden.
tip: Use all cream (4 cups) for a richer custard. For even tops, chill overnight. If broiling instead of torching, keep custards cold and rotate the pan for uniform color.

title: Panna Cotta
ing: 1 tsp vegetable oil, as needed for greasing
8 oz fresh berries, for garnish, as needed
steps: Lightly grease eight 6-oz ramekins with a thin film of vegetable oil, then wipe out excess so only a whisper remains.
Sprinkle powdered gelatin over cold water in a small bowl; let stand without stirring for 5 minutes to bloom.
In a saucepan, combine heavy cream, whole milk, sugar, vanilla, and salt. Warm over medium heat, stirring, until sugar dissolves and steam forms, 5 to 7 minutes. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Add bloomed gelatin and whisk gently until fully dissolved, about 1 minute. Strain through a fine sieve into a pitcher to ensure perfect smoothness.
Divide the mixture evenly among ramekins. Cool on the counter 20 minutes, then cover each and refrigerate until set, at least 4 hours or up to 24 hours.
To unmold, run a thin knife around edges, dip ramekin bottoms in warm water for 5 to 10 seconds, then invert onto plates and lift off. If needed, repeat the warm-water dip.
Serve chilled, plain or topped with fresh berries. Keep refrigerated and serve within 48 hours for best texture.
tip: For softer set, use 2 tsp gelatin; for firmer, 3 tsp. Flavor variations: infuse cream with lemon zest or split vanilla bean, then strain. Keeps refrigerated, covered, up to 2 days.

title: Tres Leches Cake
ing: 1 tsp neutral frying oil, as needed, for pan
1/4 cup fresh berries, for garnish, as needed
1 tbsp chopped mint, for garnish, as needed
steps: Heat oven to 350°F. Lightly oil a 9x13-inch baking pan, line bottom with parchment, and oil the parchment.

Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. In a mixer, beat egg whites on medium-high to soft peaks, 2 to 3 minutes. Gradually stream in 1/2 cup sugar; beat to glossy medium-stiff peaks, 1 to 2 minutes.
In another bowl, beat egg yolks with remaining 1/2 cup sugar until pale and thick, 2 to 3 minutes. Beat in 1/3 cup whole milk and 1 tsp vanilla until smooth.
Fold yolk mixture into whites in three additions. Sift dry ingredients over batter and gently fold just until no dry streaks remain; do not overmix.
Spread batter in pan and bake at 350°F until golden and a toothpick comes out clean, 22 to 26 minutes. Cool in pan 10 minutes, then pierce top all over with a fork.
Whisk evaporated milk, sweetened condensed milk, and 3/4 cup heavy cream. Slowly ladle over warm cake until absorbed. Cool to room temp, then cover and chill at least 4 hours or overnight.
Whip 1 1/2 cups heavy cream with powdered sugar and 1 tsp vanilla to medium peaks, 2 to 3 minutes. Unmold or leave in pan; spread whipped cream evenly over cake.
Garnish with berries and mint as desired. Slice into 8 portions and serve cold; keep leftovers refrigerated.
tip: For a hint of cinnamon, dust the whipped cream lightly before serving. The cake improves after an overnight chill; store covered in the fridge up to 3 days.

title: Mango Sticky Rice
ing: 2 cups glutinous rice, rinsed until water runs clear
4 large ripe mangoes, peeled and sliced
1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, for garnish
steps: Soak the rinsed glutinous rice in plenty of cool water for 4 to 6 hours (or overnight). Drain well in a fine strainer before cooking.

Line a steamer basket with a lightly oiled piece of cheesecloth or a clean thin kitchen towel. Spread the drained rice evenly, cover, and steam over vigorously simmering water for 25 to 30 minutes until tender and sticky.
While rice steams, warm 1 1/4 cups coconut milk with 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 tsp salt over medium heat, stirring until dissolved; do not boil. Keep warm off heat.
When rice is cooked, transfer to a warm bowl. Immediately pour the warm sweetened coconut milk over the rice, fold gently, cover, and rest for 20 minutes to absorb.

Make the coconut sauce: whisk 1/4 cup coconut milk with 1 tbsp rice flour and 2 tbsp water in a small pot. Cook over medium, whisking, until glossy and thick, 2 to 3 minutes. Season with 1/4 tsp salt to taste.
Slice the mangoes just before serving. For each portion, mound warm sticky rice, spoon on coconut sauce, and fan mango slices alongside.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and serve at once. If needed, briefly rewarm rice covered over gentle steam for 2 to 3 minutes before plating.
tip: Soak rice overnight for best texture. Substitute toasted mung beans for sesame seeds for crunch. Keep rice warm, covered; assemble with mango just before serving to prevent weeping.

title: Fudgy Brownies
ing: 10 tbsp unsalted butter, melted and warm
steps: Heat oven to 350°F. Line an 8x8-inch metal pan with parchment, leaving overhang; lightly grease the parchment.
Combine warm melted butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar in a bowl; whisk until glossy, 1 minute.
Whisk in eggs and vanilla until mixture is thick and ribbony, about 1 minute; do not overbeat past this point.
Fold in flour, cocoa, and salt just until no dry streaks remain. Fold in chopped chocolate and walnuts (if using).
Scrape batter into the pan and smooth the top; tap pan firmly on the counter 2 to 3 times to release air.
Bake at 350°F until the top is shiny with set edges and the center tests with moist crumbs, 22 to 26 minutes.
Cool in pan on a rack for 30 minutes, then lift out with parchment and cool 15 minutes more.
Slice into 8 squares with a warm knife, wiping between cuts, and serve.
tip: For extra fudgy centers, pull at the first moist-crumb test. Store airtight at room temp up to 3 days; warm 10 seconds to revive. Swap walnuts with 1/2 cup chocolate chips for maximal gooeyness.

title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
ing: 1 tbsp frying oil, as needed for greasing
steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Lightly oil two baking sheets or line with parchment.
In a large bowl, cream butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar on medium speed until light and fluffy, 2 to 3 minutes.
Beat in eggs one at a time until fully incorporated, then mix in vanilla, 30 seconds.
Whisk flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt in a separate bowl. Add to wet ingredients and mix on low just until no dry streaks remain.
Fold in chocolate chips and walnuts (if using) until evenly distributed; do not overmix.
Scoop 2 tbsp mounds (about 1 1/2 inches) spaced 2 inches apart onto prepared sheets.
Bake until edges are golden and centers just set, 9 to 11 minutes. Rotate pans halfway through for even baking.
Cool on sheets 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely, 15 minutes.
tip: Swap nuts with an extra 1/2 cup chips if nut-free. Dough can be chilled up to 48 hours for deeper flavor; bake from chilled adding 1 to 2 minutes.

title: Gulab Jamun
ing: 2 tbsp whole milk, warm, plus more as needed
steps: Make syrup: combine 2 cups sugar and 2 cups water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then simmer for 8 minutes until slightly viscous. Stir in 1 tsp cardamom, 1 tsp rose water, and 1 tsp lemon juice; keep warm on low.

Prepare dough: in a bowl mix 12 oz grated khoya, 1/4 cup flour, 1/4 tsp baking soda, and a pinch of salt. Rub in 2 tbsp ghee. Add 2 tbsp warm milk, knead gently 2 minutes to a soft, crack-free dough; rest 10 minutes.
Portion: divide into 20 equal pieces. Roll each into a smooth ball with no surface cracks; if cracks appear, moisten palms lightly with milk and reroll.
Heat oil: pour frying oil 2 inches deep in a heavy pot. Warm to 325°F over medium-low; maintain 300–325°F for gentle frying.
Fry first batch: add 6–8 balls, stirring constantly with a slotted spoon to keep them turning. Fry 6–8 minutes until uniformly deep golden brown; adjust heat to avoid rapid browning.
Soak: lift balls, drain 10 seconds, then add to warm (not boiling) syrup at 150–160°F. Soak 1 hour, turning occasionally so syrup penetrates evenly.
Repeat frying and soaking with remaining balls. Keep syrup warm but not hot to prevent shrinking or splitting.
Serve: garnish with 1 tbsp sliced pistachios. Serve warm or at room temperature with extra syrup spooned over.
tip: Khoya substitute: use 1 cup ricotta cooked down to dry plus 1 cup milk powder, then proceed. Store jamuns in syrup, chilled up to 5 days; warm gently before serving.

title: Pavlova
ing: 12 oz mixed fresh berries, cleaned and dried
steps: Heat oven to 250°F and line a baking sheet with parchment; lightly brush parchment with a thin film of oil to prevent sticking.
In a clean bowl, beat egg whites with a pinch of salt on medium speed until soft peaks, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Gradually add granulated sugar, 1 tbsp at a time, beating on high until very stiff, glossy peaks form and sugar is dissolved, 6 to 8 minutes; rub a bit between fingers to check for grit.
Beat in cornstarch, vinegar, and 1 tsp vanilla just to combine, 10 to 15 seconds.
Spoon meringue onto parchment in a 9-inch round, building a slight rim; smooth sides and top. Bake at 250°F for 75 minutes, then turn oven off and cool inside oven, door closed, 1 hour.
Transfer shell to a platter. Whip cream, powdered sugar, and 1 tsp vanilla to soft peaks, 1 to 2 minutes.
Top cooled pavlova with whipped cream and arrange berries over the top just before serving.
Slice gently with a serrated knife and serve immediately.
tip: For a crisper shell, dry an extra 30 minutes in the turned-off oven. Swap berries for passionfruit pulp. Assemble just before serving; store the undecorated shell airtight up to 2 days.

title: Tiramisu
ing: 2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder, for dusting
steps: Whisk 6 large egg yolks with 3/4 cup sugar in a heatproof bowl set over barely simmering water, stirring constantly until thickened and 165°F, about 6 to 8 minutes; cool 10 minutes.
Fold 1 lb chilled mascarpone into the cooled yolk mixture in 2 additions until smooth; do not overmix. Refrigerate while you whip the cream.
Beat 1 1/2 cups cold heavy cream with 1/4 tsp salt to medium-stiff peaks, 2 to 3 minutes. Gently fold whipped cream into the mascarpone mixture until just combined.
Stir 1 1/2 cups cooled espresso with 3 tbsp dark rum and 2 tbsp coffee liqueur in a shallow dish. Briefly dip each ladyfinger, 1 to 2 seconds per side; do not soak.
Arrange a snug single layer of dipped ladyfingers (about half) in a 9x13-inch dish. Spread half the mascarpone cream evenly over the layer.
Repeat with remaining dipped ladyfingers and top with the remaining mascarpone cream, smoothing the surface.
Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, until set and sliceable.
Just before serving, dust the top evenly with 2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder and slice into 8 portions.
tip: Swap Marsala for rum if preferred. Tiramisu keeps refrigerated, covered, up to 2 days; dust with cocoa at serving to prevent spotting.

title: Baklava
ing: 1 lb phyllo dough, thawed overnight in fridge
12 tbsp unsalted butter, melted and clarified
2 cups unsalted shelled pistachios, finely chopped
1/2 cup pistachios, finely ground, for garnish
steps: Prepare syrup: combine 1 cup sugar, 3/4 cup water, 1/2 cup honey, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and lemon peel; bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes. Discard peel and cool syrup to room temperature.
Heat oven to 350°F. Brush a 9x13-inch pan with melted clarified butter. Keep phyllo covered with a slightly damp towel to prevent drying.
Mix 2 cups chopped pistachios with 1/4 cup sugar and 1/2 tsp cinnamon. Set aside. Reserve remaining butter for layering.
Layer base: place 8 sheets phyllo in pan, one at a time, brushing each lightly with butter. Trim edges to fit as needed.
Scatter 1/3 of nut mixture evenly. Add 4 buttered phyllo sheets. Repeat nuts and 4 sheets two more times (total 3 nut layers). Top with 8 buttered sheets for the lid.
Using a sharp knife, cut baklava into 16 diamonds or squares, ensuring cuts go through all layers.
Bake at 350°F for 40 to 45 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Rotate pan halfway for even browning.

Immediately after removing from oven, slowly pour cooled syrup evenly over hot baklava. Let absorb and cool at room temperature for 3 to 4 hours before serving. Garnish with 1/2 cup finely ground pistachios.
tip: Clarify butter by skimming milk solids for crisper layers. Store covered at room temp up to 3 days; re-crisp 10 minutes at 300°F if needed.

title: Basque Burnt Cheesecake
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Grease a 9-inch springform pan with butter, then line with 2 overlapping sheets of parchment, letting them rise 2 inches above the rim.
In a large bowl, beat cream cheese and sugar on medium until smooth and creamy, about 2 minutes, scraping the bowl.
Beat in eggs one at a time on low, fully incorporating before adding the next, about 30 seconds each.
Mix in heavy cream, vanilla, and salt on low until silky and lump-free. Sift flour over batter and mix on low just until combined, 10 to 15 seconds.
Pour batter into the lined pan and tap firmly on the counter 2 to 3 times to release large air bubbles.
Bake at 425°F for 50 to 60 minutes until deeply browned on top, the center jiggles like loose custard, and edges are set; tent lightly if overly dark at 45 minutes.
Cool in pan on a rack until just warm, about 1 hour; the cake will deflate and set. Remove the ring and parchment once cool enough to handle.
Chill uncovered until cold, at least 4 hours or overnight; slice with a hot, wiped knife and serve slightly cool or at room temperature.
tip: For a looser center, bake 48–52 min; for firmer slices, bake 58–62 min. Keeps 3 days refrigerated; bring to room temp 20 minutes before serving.

title: Kheer
ing: 3/4 cup basmati rice, rinsed until water runs clear
1 pinch saffron threads, soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk
steps: Warm 1 tbsp ghee in a heavy 4–5 qt pot over medium heat, 2 minutes. Add 3/4 cup rinsed basmati and toast, stirring, until lightly aromatic, about 2 minutes.
Pour in 8 cups whole milk and 1/8 tsp salt. Bring just to a gentle boil over medium, stirring often to prevent scorching, 10–12 minutes.
Reduce to low and simmer uncovered, stirring and scraping the bottom and sides frequently, until rice is very tender and milk has reduced by about one-third, 30–35 minutes.
Stir in 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup sweetened condensed milk. Simmer on low, stirring, until slightly thickened and creamy, 10–12 minutes.
Add 1/4 tsp ground cardamom and saffron with its milk. Cook, stirring, 2 minutes, then turn off heat.
In a small pan over medium heat, dry-toast 1/2 cup cashews and 1/4 cup almonds until pale golden, 3–4 minutes. Stir nuts and 1/3 cup raisins into kheer.
Taste and adjust sweetness if needed. Kheer will thicken as it cools; for serving warm, rest 5 minutes. For chilled, cool to room temp, then refrigerate 4 hours.
Serve warm or chilled, garnished with a few extra toasted nuts if desired.
tip: Rinse rice well for a cleaner, silkier finish. Kheer thickens on chilling; loosen with a splash of warm milk before serving. Swap basmati with short-grain rice for a plusher texture.

title: Banana Bread
ing: frying oil, as needed, for greasing
steps: Heat oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan with a little oil, then coat with 1 tbsp softened butter; line the long side with a parchment sling.
In a large bowl, whisk melted butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar until glossy, 1 minute. Whisk in eggs one at a time until smooth. Whisk in milk and vanilla.
In a separate bowl, whisk flour, baking soda, and salt. Stir in walnuts.
Fold dry ingredients into the wet mixture with a spatula until a few streaks remain. Fold in mashed bananas just until combined; do not overmix.
Scrape batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top. Bake at 350°F until deep golden and a tester comes out with a few moist crumbs, 55 to 65 minutes.
Cool in pan on a rack for 15 minutes. Lift out using the parchment and cool completely, about 1 hour, before slicing.
tip: Swap walnuts with 1/2 cup chocolate chips. Store wrapped at room temp 3 days or freeze slices up to 2 months; thaw at room temp and warm in a 300°F oven for 8 minutes.

title: Mochi Ice Cream
ing: 1 tbsp frying oil, as needed for greasing
steps: Line a baking sheet with parchment. Scoop 8 balls of ice cream (about 2 tbsp each), place on sheet, and freeze until firm for 45 minutes.
In a microwave-safe bowl, whisk mochiko, sugar, salt, and water until smooth with no lumps.
Cover the bowl loosely and microwave on high for 1 minute, stir; repeat 1 minute, stir; then 30 seconds more until thick, glossy, and sticky (total about 2.5 minutes).
Dust a large sheet of parchment generously with potato starch. Scrape hot mochi onto it, dust top with more starch, and roll to a 1/8-inch sheet. Cool at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Chill rolled mochi on a tray in the refrigerator for 10 minutes to set slightly, then punch out 8 rounds using a 3.5-inch cutter.
Lightly oil a cupcake pan or small ramekins. Place one mochi round in a cup, dust off excess starch, add an ice cream ball, and pinch edges to seal.
Invert seam-side-down into the cup and freeze until firm for 20 minutes. Repeat with remaining pieces, working with 1 ice cream ball at a time to prevent melting.
Before serving, rest at room temperature for 2 to 3 minutes so the mochi softens slightly.
tip: Swap potato starch with cornstarch for dusting if needed. Store wrapped mochi ice cream in the freezer up to 2 weeks; soften a few minutes before eating.

title: Huevos Rancheros
ing: 8 oz ripe tomatoes, cored and chopped
1 tbsp vegetable oil, for frying tortillas
1 tbsp vegetable oil, for frying eggs
1 lime, cut into wedges, for serving
steps: Make ranchera sauce: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add onion, jalapeño, and garlic; cook 3 minutes. Stir in tomatoes, tomatillos, cumin, salt, and pepper; simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until lightly thickened.
Adjust sauce: Taste and add a squeeze of lime if desired. Keep warm over low heat, stirring occasionally, for up to 10 minutes.
Warm beans: In a small skillet over low heat, warm refried beans, stirring, 3 to 5 minutes until spreadable. Cover to keep warm.
Fry tortillas: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat. Fry tortillas in batches 30 to 45 seconds per side until lightly crisp yet pliable; drain on paper towels and keep warm.

Fry eggs: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Crack in eggs and cook 3 to 4 minutes for sunny-side up, spooning hot oil over whites until set and yolks runny. Cook longer for firmer yolks if preferred.
Assemble: Spread 2 tbsp warm beans onto each tortilla. Spoon 2 to 3 tbsp ranchera sauce over beans.
Plate: Set two topped tortillas on each plate. Nestle one egg on each tortilla, then ladle more warm sauce over eggs to taste.
Garnish and serve: Sprinkle with cilantro and serve immediately with lime wedges. Add salt and pepper to taste at the table.
tip: Swap: Use roasted canned tomatoes if fresh are out of season. To make ahead, simmer sauce up to 3 days in advance; rewarm with a splash of water.

title: Buttermilk Pancakes
ing: 3 tbsp unsalted butter, melted and cooled
1 tbsp frying oil or butter, as needed
1 cup berries or sliced fruit, for serving
steps: Whisk 2 cups flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, and 1/2 tsp salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk 2 cups cold buttermilk, 2 eggs, 3 tbsp melted butter, and 1 tsp vanilla until smooth.
Pour wet into dry; gently stir just until a few streaks of flour remain. Do not overmix; batter should be lumpy. Let rest 5 minutes.
Heat a large nonstick skillet or griddle over medium to medium-low until a drop of water skitters, about 375°F. Lightly grease with oil or butter.
Scoop 1/4 cup batter per pancake onto the griddle, spacing apart. Cook until edges set and bubbles break and stay open, 2 to 3 minutes.
Flip carefully and cook until golden and centers spring back, 1 to 2 minutes more. Keep finished pancakes warm at 200°F while repeating.
Regrease the pan as needed and adjust heat to maintain even browning without scorching.
Serve hot with maple syrup and fruit.
tip: For extra tang, replace 1/4 cup buttermilk with sour cream. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; rewarm on a 300°F sheet pan for 8 minutes or in a toaster.

title: French Toast
ing: 8 slices day-old brioche or challah, 1-inch thick
steps: Whisk eggs, whole milk, heavy cream, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt in a shallow dish until smooth, about 30 seconds.
Preheat a large skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes. Add 1 tsp oil and 1/2 tbsp butter; heat until butter foams but does not brown, 30–45 seconds.
Lay 2 slices bread in custard; soak 20–30 seconds per side until evenly moistened but not soggy. Let excess drip back into dish.
Place soaked slices in skillet. Cook until deep golden on first side, 2–3 minutes; flip and cook until second side is golden and centers feel set, 2–3 minutes.
Adjust heat as needed to prevent scorching. Add more oil and butter for each batch. Repeat soaking and cooking with remaining slices.
Hold finished toast on a wire rack set over a sheet pan in a 200°F oven while you cook remaining batches, up to 15 minutes.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve immediately with warmed maple syrup.
tip: Stale bread soaks best; slice fresh bread and air-dry 1–2 hours if needed. For richer custard, replace 1/4 cup milk with cream; for lighter, use all milk.

title: Belgian Waffles
ing: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled
frying oil, as needed for the iron
powdered sugar, to taste, for serving
steps: Preheat a Belgian waffle iron to medium-high until fully hot. Lightly brush grids with a thin film of frying oil.
In a bowl, whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt until evenly combined.
In a second bowl, whisk egg yolks, milk, melted butter, and vanilla until smooth.
In a clean bowl, beat egg whites to soft peaks, 2 to 3 minutes. Do not overbeat.
Whisk wet ingredients into dry just until streaks of flour disappear. Gently fold in whipped whites in two additions until batter is airy.
Lightly oil the waffle iron again. Ladle batter to cover grids without overflowing. Close and cook until deeply golden and crisp, 4 to 5 minutes per waffle.
Transfer waffles to a wire rack (not a plate) to keep crisp. Repeat with remaining batter, oiling grids as needed.
Serve hot dusted with powdered sugar. Optional accompaniments: fresh berries or lightly sweetened whipped cream.
tip: For extra crispness, hold cooked waffles on a rack in a 225°F oven up to 20 minutes. Batter can rest 10 minutes before cooking to relax gluten; avoid overmixing to keep waffles tender.

title: Breakfast Burrito
steps: Warm tortillas: Wrap 4 tortillas in foil and heat at 300°F for 10 minutes until pliable; keep wrapped.
Brown sausage: Heat 1 tsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook sausage, breaking up, until browned and 165°F, 5–6 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.
Cook potatoes and veg: In the same skillet add 2 tsp oil, potatoes, onion, and poblano. Season lightly with salt. Cook, stirring, until potatoes are tender and golden, 8–10 minutes.
Beat eggs: Whisk eggs, milk, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp pepper until fully combined and slightly frothy, 20–30 seconds.
Scramble eggs: Push veg to one side, add 1 tsp oil if dry, pour in eggs. Cook over medium, gently folding, until just set and glossy, 2–3 minutes. Return sausage and stir to combine.
Assemble: Lay out warm tortillas. Divide sausage-egg-potato mix among them, top each with 1/4 cup cheddar, 2 tbsp salsa, and cilantro.
Roll: Fold sides over, then roll tightly from the bottom to enclose. For a toasted finish, sear seam-side down in a dry skillet over medium for 1–2 minutes each side.
Serve: Halve burritos and serve with sour cream and pico de gallo. Eat hot.
tip: Swap sausage with chorizo for extra kick. Burritos keep 3 days wrapped and chilled; reheat in a 350°F oven for 12–15 minutes or skillet-steam with a splash of water.

title: Avocado Toast with Poached Egg
steps: Bring a wide saucepan of water (about 2 quarts) to a bare simmer at 190–195°F; stir in 2 tsp white vinegar.
Split and pit avocados, scoop into a bowl, add 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/8 tsp pepper; mash gently until mostly smooth with a few small chunks.
Toast 4 slices sourdough until deep golden; brush each with 1 tbsp olive oil divided and lightly butter while hot.
Crack each egg into a small cup. Swirl the simmering water, slide in eggs one by one, and poach for 3–4 minutes until whites are set and yolks still soft.
Use a slotted spoon to lift eggs; drain on paper towel and trim ragged whites if desired.
Spread avocado evenly over toast. Crumble 1/4 cup feta over the four toasts and sprinkle 1 tbsp chives and 1/4 tsp chili flakes.
Top each toast with a poached egg. Season with a pinch more salt and pepper to taste and serve immediately.
tip: Swap feta for goat cheese or shaved Parmesan. For make-ahead, mix avocado with extra lemon and press plastic wrap directly on the surface; refrigerate up to 4 hours.

title: Overnight Oats
ing: 2 tbsp chopped fresh mint, for garnish
steps: Combine 2 cups oats, 1 1/2 cups milk, 1 cup yogurt, 1/2 cup apple juice, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and 1/4 tsp salt in a large bowl; stir until evenly moistened.
Fold in 1/2 cup chopped almonds and 1/2 cup raisins until distributed; the mixture should be thick but spoonable. Adjust with 2–4 tbsp milk if very stiff.
Cover the bowl tightly and refrigerate overnight for at least 8 hours to allow the oats to fully hydrate and flavors to meld.
Before serving, core and coarsely grate 2 apples with peel; fold the grated apples into the oats until well combined.
Taste and adjust sweetness with a little more honey if desired; if too thick, loosen with a splash of milk until creamy.
Spoon into bowls and top each serving with fresh berries and chopped mint just before serving.
tip: Swap milk/yogurt with almond milk or skyr to taste. Keeps refrigerated up to 3 days; stir in fresh apple right before serving for best texture.

title: Homemade Granola
steps: Heat oven to 325°F and line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment.
In a large bowl, combine oats, almonds, pepitas, coconut, salt, and cinnamon; toss to mix evenly.
Warm honey, brown sugar, and oil in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring until sugar dissolves, 2 to 3 minutes. Off heat, stir in vanilla.
Pour syrup over dry mix and stir until every flake is lightly coated and no dry pockets remain.
Spread mixture in an even, compact layer on the pan, pressing gently with a spatula for clumps.
Bake at 325°F for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once at 12 minutes, until golden brown and fragrant.
Cool on the pan completely, 25 to 30 minutes, then sprinkle on raisins and cranberries and toss to distribute.
Break into clusters and store airtight at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.
tip: Swap honey with maple syrup for vegan. For extra clusters, don’t stir during baking—just rotate the pan, then cool undisturbed before breaking.

title: Spinach and Feta Frittata
steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Place a rack in the center position so the pan can finish under even heat.
Whisk eggs, milk, salt, and pepper in a bowl until smoothly combined, about 30 seconds; set aside.
Warm olive oil in a 10-inch oven-safe skillet over medium heat until shimmering, 1 minute.
Add onion and cook, stirring, until translucent and tender, 5 to 6 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook until fragrant, 30 seconds.
Add spinach in batches, tossing until just wilted and excess moisture cooks off, 2 to 3 minutes total.
Spread spinach evenly in the skillet. Pour in egg mixture, then scatter feta and parsley evenly over the top.
Cook undisturbed on the stovetop until edges are set and the center is softly jiggly, 3 to 4 minutes.
Transfer skillet to the oven and bake at 375°F until the center is just set and eggs reach 160°F, 8 to 10 minutes. Rest 5 minutes, then slice and serve.
tip: Sub 1/4 cup chopped dill or scallions for parsley. Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days; rewarm at 300°F for 8 to 10 minutes.

title: Quiche Lorraine
ing: 4 oz slab bacon or lardons, cut into 1/4-inch batons
1 tbsp unsalted butter, softened, for the tin
steps: Rub 8-inch tart tin with 1 tbsp softened butter. In a bowl, cut 8 tbsp cold butter into 1 1/4 cups flour until sandy. Sprinkle in 3 tbsp ice water; mix just until dough clumps. Flatten, wrap, chill 30 minutes.
Lightly flour surface. Roll dough to a 12-inch round, 1/8-inch thick. Fit into tin, easing corners; trim flush. Prick base with a fork. Chill shell 20 minutes.
Heat oven to 375°F. Line shell with parchment and pie weights. Bake 15 minutes. Remove weights; bake until just set and lightly golden, 8–10 minutes. Cool 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook 4 oz bacon in a skillet over medium heat until lightly crisp, 6–8 minutes. Drain on paper towels; blot excess fat so custard stays clear.
Whisk 3 eggs, 3/4 cup milk, 3/4 cup cream, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/8 tsp pepper, and 1/8 tsp nutmeg until smooth; avoid foam. Scatter bacon evenly over warm shell.
Reduce oven to 350°F. Pour custard over bacon to just below rim. Place tin on a baking sheet for easy handling.
Bake at 350°F until the center is just set with a slight wobble, 22–28 minutes; internal custard temperature should reach about 175°F. Do not overbrown.
Cool on a rack 10–15 minutes to finish setting. Unmold if desired, slice into 4 wedges, and serve warm or at room temperature.
tip: For a Lorraine purist, omit cheese; if desired, add 2 oz finely grated Gruyère. Keeps refrigerated, wrapped, up to 2 days; rewarm at 300°F for 10–12 minutes.

title: Dutch Baby Pancake
steps: Set oven to 425°F and place a 10-inch ovenproof skillet or cast-iron pan inside to preheat for 10 minutes.
In a blender, combine eggs, milk, flour, granulated sugar, vanilla, and salt; blend until smooth for 20 to 30 seconds, then rest the batter for 5 minutes to relax the flour.
Carefully remove the hot skillet, add butter, and swirl until fully melted and foaming, about 20 seconds.
Pour the batter into the center of the skillet and immediately return it to the oven.
Bake at 425°F until the pancake is deeply golden, puffed, and the edges are crisp, 16 to 18 minutes.
Remove skillet and let stand 1 minute to set. The pancake will deflate slightly as it cools—this is expected.
Dust generously with powdered sugar, cut into wedges, and serve warm with berries and lemon for squeezing.
tip: For extra crisp edges, preheat the skillet for a full 10 minutes. Batter can be blended and chilled up to 1 hour; reblend briefly before baking.

title: Menemen
ing: 2 large green Turkish peppers (or 2 Anaheim peppers), thinly sliced
4 large ripe tomatoes, peeled and finely chopped
steps: Heat 3 tbsp olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a wide skillet over medium heat until the butter foams, about 1 minute.
Add 1 large chopped onion and 2 sliced green peppers; cook, stirring, until softened and lightly sweet, 6–8 minutes.
Stir in 4 chopped tomatoes, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp black pepper; cook, stirring, until the tomatoes break down and thicken to a saucy consistency, 8–10 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Taste and adjust seasoning; the mixture should be well seasoned and gently simmering.
Pour in 6 lightly beaten eggs evenly over the tomato-pepper base. Let set undisturbed 30–45 seconds, then gently stir from the edges toward the center.
Continue gently folding until curds are just set but still creamy and slightly runny, 2–3 minutes. Do not overcook; remove from heat while still soft.
Scatter 1/4 cup crumbled feta, 2 tbsp chopped parsley, and a pinch of Aleppo pepper over the top.
Serve immediately from the pan with warm bread; eat while the eggs remain soft and creamy.
tip: For a richer version, use 2 tbsp butter and skip feta. Peel tomatoes easily by scoring and blanching 30 seconds. Leftovers are best avoided; if needed, refrigerate up to 1 day and rewarm gently.

title: Masala Omelette
ing: 2 tbsp green bell pepper, finely chopped
3/4 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
steps: Crack 8 large eggs into a bowl. Add turmeric, ground coriander, red chili powder, salt, and black pepper. Whisk vigorously until fully combined and slightly frothy, about 45 seconds.
Stir in onion, tomato, cilantro, cilantro stems, green bell pepper, and green chile. Mix to evenly disperse vegetables without deflating the eggs.
Heat a 10-inch nonstick or well-seasoned skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Add 1 tsp oil and 1/2 tsp butter, swirl to coat until butter foams, about 20 seconds.
Pour in 1/4 of the egg mixture. Shake the pan to level, then use a spatula to draw in the edges so uncooked egg flows to the rim. Cook until the bottom is just set, 1 to 1 1/2 minutes.
Fold the omelette in half, then cook 30 to 45 seconds more until the center is just set but still moist (160°F for food safety). Slide to a warm plate.
Repeat cooking with remaining egg mixture, adding 1 tsp oil and 1/2 tsp butter per omelette and adjusting heat to prevent browning too fast.
Serve immediately, optionally with buttered toast or pav, and a wedge of lime for squeezing.
tip: Swap green bell pepper with finely chopped capsicum or omit. Mix can be made 1 hour ahead and chilled; re-whisk before cooking. Leftovers keep 1 day, chilled; rewarm gently in a covered skillet.

title: Tamagoyaki
ing: 1 tbsp neutral oil, as needed, for conditioning pan
1 tbsp finely grated daikon, as needed, for garnish
1 tsp soy sauce, as needed, for garnish
steps: In a bowl, whisk 6 large eggs just until blended; avoid foaming. Whisk in 3 tbsp dashi, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp mirin, 1 tsp soy sauce, and 1/4 tsp salt until smooth.
Strain the egg mixture through a fine sieve into a pouring cup to remove chalazae and bubbles; rest for 5 minutes to let foam subside.
Heat a tamagoyaki pan (or 8-inch nonstick skillet) over medium-low. Lightly oil with a folded paper towel; the film should shimmer, not smoke.

Pour a thin layer of egg (about 2 to 3 tbsp) to just cover the surface. Tilt to spread. When the top is mostly set but still glossy, 45 to 60 seconds, roll from far edge toward you with chopsticks or a spatula.

Push the roll back to the far side. Re-oil the pan lightly. Pour another thin layer, lifting the roll to let egg flow underneath. Cook until just set, 30 to 45 seconds, then roll toward you, encasing the first layer.
Repeat layering, setting, and rolling 5 to 7 more times until all egg is used and a neat log forms. Adjust heat to keep browning minimal; total cooking about 8 to 12 minutes.
Lightly press the finished roll with a mat or paper towel to shape. Rest 3 minutes, then transfer to a board and let stand 2 minutes to set.
Slice into 8 to 10 pieces with a damp knife. Serve warm or at room temperature with grated daikon and a few drops of soy sauce to taste.
tip: Swap dashi with water plus 1/8 tsp dashi powder if needed. Cool completely, wrap, and refrigerate up to 2 days; slice just before serving to keep edges neat.

title: Cinnamon Rolls
ing: 3 tbsp unsalted butter, softened, for filling
1 large egg, beaten, for egg wash
steps: Bloom yeast by combining 1/2 cup warm milk (110°F) with 2 tbsp sugar and 1 1/8 tsp yeast; let stand until foamy, 5–8 minutes.
Make dough: In a bowl, combine flour and salt. Add bloomed yeast mixture, 1 egg, and 2 tbsp softened butter. Mix, then knead until smooth and elastic, 6–8 minutes.
First rise: Shape into a ball, place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm spot until doubled, about 45–60 minutes.
Make filling: In a small bowl mix 3 tbsp softened butter, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 1/2 tsp cinnamon, and 1/4 tsp cardamom into a spreadable paste.
Shape: Punch down dough and roll into a 12x10-inch rectangle. Spread filling evenly, leaving a 1/2-inch border on one long side. Roll up tightly toward the border, seam-side down.
Cut and arrange: Trim ends, then cut 8 even pieces. Place in a parchment-lined 8-inch round pan or spaced on a sheet. Cover and proof until puffy, 25–35 minutes. Preheat oven to 400°F.
Brush with beaten egg. Sprinkle pearl sugar. Bake at 400°F until deep golden and centers read 190°F, about 14–17 minutes. Tent with foil if browning too fast.
Cool 10 minutes before serving warm. Optionally brush with a little melted butter after baking for sheen.
tip: Substitute coarse sugar if pearl sugar is unavailable. Rolls keep 2 days at room temp in an airtight container; rewarm 5 minutes at 300°F.

title: Blueberry Muffins
ing: 1/4 cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled
1 tbsp all-purpose flour, for tossing berries
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Line a standard 12-cup muffin tin with 8 liners and lightly oil the empty wells as needed.
Whisk 1 1/2 cups flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl until uniform, about 30 seconds.
In a second bowl, whisk milk, melted butter, egg, and vanilla until smooth, about 20 seconds.
Toss blueberries with 1 tbsp flour to lightly coat, then gently fold into the wet mixture.
Make a well in the dry ingredients, add the wet mixture, and fold just until no dry pockets remain; batter should be thick with a few small lumps. Do not overmix.
Divide batter evenly among 8 liners, filling about 3/4 full. Sprinkle tops with coarse sugar.
Bake at 400°F until domed and golden and a tester comes out clean, 16 to 18 minutes. Rotate the pan once halfway through.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer muffins to a rack to cool at least 10 minutes before serving.
tip: Tossing berries with flour helps prevent sinking. Store airtight at room temp up to 2 days; rewarm 5 minutes at 300°F. Frozen blueberries work; fold in from frozen and add 1 to 2 minutes bake time.

title: Açaí Bowl
steps: Run açaí purée packets under warm water for 10 to 15 seconds to loosen, then break into chunks.
Add frozen açaí, frozen berries, 1 banana (sliced), apple juice, and honey to a blender. Blend on high until very thick and smooth, 45 to 60 seconds, stopping to stir as needed.
Adjust thickness: add 1 to 2 tbsp more apple juice if the blender stalls, or a handful of ice if too thin. Mixture should mound on a spoon.
Divide the açaí base into 4 chilled bowls. Smooth the tops with a spoon.
Top each bowl with 1/4 cup granola, remaining banana slices, strawberries, coconut, peanuts, and a sprinkle of chia seeds.
Serve immediately while icy and thick.
tip: For authentic flavor, use unsweetened Brazilian açaí purée; swap apple juice with orange juice or guaraná syrup for a Rio-style touch. Freeze bowls 10 minutes before assembling to keep the base thick.

title: Breakfast Hash with Fried Eggs
ing: 1.5 lb russet potatoes, peeled and 1/2-inch diced
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Place diced potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch, add 1 tsp salt, bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 to 6 minutes until just tender; drain well and steam-dry 2 minutes.
Heat a large 12-inch heavy skillet over medium. Add bacon and cook, stirring, until crisp and fat renders, 6 to 8 minutes; transfer bacon to a paper towel–lined plate. Leave 2 tbsp fat in skillet.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add potatoes in an even layer; cook undisturbed 4 minutes, then toss and cook 6 to 8 minutes more until golden and crisp at edges.

Add onion and bell pepper with 1 tbsp oil if pan is dry; cook, stirring, until onion is translucent and peppers are tender, 4 to 5 minutes. Season with 1/2 tsp kosher salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Fold in bacon.
Press hash into an even layer and cook 2 minutes to build crust. Taste and adjust seasoning. Reduce heat to medium-low and keep warm while frying eggs.

In a separate nonstick skillet, heat 1 tbsp oil over medium. Crack in eggs and cook sunny-side up until whites are set and yolks still runny, 3 to 4 minutes; or flip for over-easy, 30 to 60 seconds more.
Divide hash among 4 plates. Top each with a fried egg. Garnish with parsley and additional pepper to taste. Serve immediately.
tip: Swap bacon for diced corned beef to make a classic corned beef hash. Leftover hash reheats well in a skillet over medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes to re-crisp.

title: Kaya Toast
steps: Make kaya: In a heatproof bowl, whisk eggs, sugar, salt, coconut milk, and pandan extract until smooth with no streaks.
Set bowl over a gentle simmering bain-marie (water barely bubbling). Stir constantly with a spatula, scraping sides, until thick and glossy, 15–20 minutes.
When lines hold on the spatula, remove from heat and stir 1 minute to cool slightly. Press through a fine sieve into a clean bowl; cover surface and chill 10 minutes.
Spread 1/2 tbsp butter on each bread slice. Toast on a dry skillet over medium heat until deep golden on both sides, about 2–3 minutes per side.
While warm, spread 1–1.5 tbsp kaya on four slices; top with remaining slices to form sandwiches.
Trim crusts for tradition, then press lightly and slice each sandwich into thirds or halves. Serve warm.
Optional soft-set eggs (classic pairing): Simmer water, remove from heat, add 2 eggs, cover 7 minutes, then crack into bowls and season to taste.
tip: Kaya keeps 1 week refrigerated; warm gently to loosen. No pandan extract? Use 2 pandan leaves tied in a knot and steep in the coconut milk over low heat 5 minutes; cool, remove leaves, then proceed.

title: Idli with Sambar
ing: 1 cup mixed vegetables, diced (carrot, drumstick, pumpkin)
steps: Rinse 1 cup urad dal and 1/2 tsp fenugreek; rinse 2 cups idli rice separately. Soak both in plenty of water for 6 hours. Drain. Grind urad to a fluffy batter with cold water as needed, then grind rice to slightly coarse batter.
Combine batters with 1 tsp salt to thick pourable consistency. Ferment covered in a warm spot until doubled and bubbly, 8–12 hours at about 80–90°F.
