Grease idli plates with 1 tsp oil. Stir batter gently. Pour to 3/4 full. Steam in idli steamer with boiling water for 10–12 minutes; rest 2 minutes, then unmold. Keep warm.
Rinse 1 cup toor dal until water runs clear. Pressure cook with 3 cups water and 1/2 tsp turmeric for 8 minutes at high pressure; natural release 10 minutes. Mash dal smooth.
Simmer 1 cup mixed vegetables in 1 cup water until tender, 8–10 minutes. Add mashed dal, 1 tsp tamarind paste, 1 tsp jaggery, 1 tsp salt, and 2 tbsp sambar powder. Simmer for 6–8 minutes to meld.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee with 1 tbsp oil in a small pan over medium. Add 1 tsp mustard, 1 tsp cumin, 2 dried chilies, 10 curry leaves, and 1/4 tsp asafoetida; bloom 30–45 seconds until aromatic.

Add 1 cup sliced onion; sauté until translucent, 4–5 minutes. Add 1 cup chopped tomatoes; cook until soft and pulpy, 4–5 minutes. Pour tempering into sambar and simmer 2 minutes. Adjust salt to taste.
Serve hot idlis with ladles of sambar. Garnish with 2 tbsp chopped cilantro and coconut chutney powder if using. Idlis are best warm and fluffy; re-steam 2–3 minutes to refresh.
tip: For crisp vadas-in-sambar, add fried medu vadas just before serving. Batter ferments best in a warm oven with light on; in cold weather, add a pinch of sugar to encourage activity.

title: Garlic Mashed Potatoes
ing: 2 lb russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks
4 tbsp unsalted butter, cut into pieces
1 tbsp fresh chives, finely sliced, for garnish (optional)
1/4 tsp kosher salt, for boiling water
steps: Place potatoes in a large pot, cover by 1 inch with cold water, and add 1/4 tsp salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a gentle boil and cook until fork-tender, 12 to 15 minutes.

While potatoes cook, warm oil in a small saucepan over medium-low. Add minced garlic and cook gently until fragrant and pale golden, 2 to 3 minutes; do not brown. Stir in butter to melt, then add warm milk and cream. Keep warm on low heat.
Drain potatoes well and return to the hot pot over low heat. Shake and cook 30 to 60 seconds to evaporate excess moisture.
Mash potatoes with a potato masher or ricer until mostly smooth.
Pour in the warm garlic-butter mixture. Add 1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Fold with a spatula just until creamy and cohesive; avoid overmixing.
Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper to taste. If too thick, stir in a splash more warm milk, 1 to 2 tbsp at a time.
Transfer to a warmed serving bowl. Garnish with chives if using and serve hot.
tip: Swap russets with Yukon Golds for a slightly more buttery texture. To make ahead, refrigerate up to 2 days and rewarm gently with extra warm milk to loosen.

title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts
ing: 1 1/2 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
steps: Heat oven to 425°F and place a rimmed sheet pan on the center rack to preheat for 5 minutes.
In a bowl, toss Brussels sprouts with olive oil, salt, and pepper until evenly coated.
Carefully spread Brussels sprouts cut-side down on the hot sheet pan in a single layer.
Roast at 425°F for 18 to 22 minutes until deeply browned on cut sides and tender when pierced.
Transfer to a bowl, toss with lemon juice, and adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Sprinkle with Parmesan before serving, if using, and serve hot.
tip: Swap lemon with 1 tsp red wine vinegar for a sharper finish. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; re-crisp on a hot sheet pan at 450°F for 5 minutes.

title: Mexican Red Rice
ing: 1 cup long-grain white rice, rinsed and drained
4 oz ripe tomatoes, cored and chopped
1/2 cup frozen peas and carrots, thawed
1 lime, cut into wedges, optional garnish
steps: Blend tomatoes, onion, and garlic with 1/2 cup of the broth until smooth, about 30 seconds. Set aside.
Warm oil in a 10-inch skillet with lid over medium heat. Add rice and fry, stirring, until evenly golden, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook, stirring, until thickened and slightly darkened, 3 to 4 minutes.
Whisk remaining 1 1/2 cups broth with tomato paste, salt, and cumin; pour into skillet. Bring to a gentle boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15 minutes. Do not lift the lid.
Without uncovering, turn off heat and let steam 10 minutes. Then lift lid, scatter in peas and carrots, and fluff gently with a fork.
Cover again and rest 2 minutes to warm the vegetables through. Adjust salt to taste and discard any scorched grains from edges if present.
Serve hot, garnished with cilantro and lime wedges, if desired.
tip: Rinse rice until water runs clear for distinct grains. For vegetarian, use vegetable broth. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat covered with a splash of broth or water.

title: Jeera Rice
ing: 1 1/2 cups basmati rice, rinsed until water runs clear and soaked 20 minutes
4 whole green cardamom pods, lightly crushed
1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
steps: Drain the soaked rice well in a sieve for 5 minutes to remove excess water.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee with 1 tbsp oil in a medium heavy pot over medium heat for 1 minute until shimmering.
Add 2 tsp cumin seeds, bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon; fry, stirring, until cumin crackles and turns a shade darker, about 45–60 seconds.
Stir in drained rice and gently sauté to coat each grain, 2 minutes, until rice turns glossy and lightly nutty.
Pour in 1 3/4 cups hot water and add salt; bring to a brisk boil over medium-high heat, 1–2 minutes.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and cook undisturbed for 12 minutes at a gentle simmer.
Turn off heat and let rice rest covered for 10 minutes to finish steaming; do not lift the lid.
Fluff gently with a fork, discard whole spices if desired, and garnish with chopped cilantro before serving hot.
tip: Rinse and soak basmati for separate, long grains. For richer aroma, replace water with a light stock or add a few cumin seeds while steaming to refresh before serving.

title: Garlic Naan
ing: 2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
steps: Bloom yeast by stirring 2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast and 1 tsp sugar into 3/4 cup warm water (110°F). Let stand until foamy, 8–10 minutes.

In a bowl, mix 2 1/4 cups flour and 1 tsp salt. Add bloomed yeast, 1/2 cup yogurt, and 1 tbsp oil. Knead until smooth and slightly tacky, 8–10 minutes. Lightly oil bowl, cover, and rise until doubled, 60 minutes.
Stir 3 tbsp melted butter with 4 cloves minced garlic and 1 tbsp ghee (optional). Reserve 2 tsp of this mix for finishing; keep the rest for brushing during cooking.
Punch down dough and divide into 8 equal pieces. Roll each into a ball, rest covered 10 minutes, then roll one ball at a time into a teardrop about 8 inches, 1/8 inch thick.

Tawa/skillet method: Heat a heavy skillet on medium-high until very hot, 3–4 minutes. Lightly brush one side with garlic butter, lay buttered side down. Cook until bubbles form and underside is deep golden with char spots, 1–2 minutes.
Brush the top with garlic butter, flip, and cook 30–60 seconds more until cooked through. Press edges with a spatula for even puffing. Repeat with remaining dough, adjusting heat to avoid scorching.

Oven/broiler method: Set a sheet pan in the oven and preheat to 500°F with broiler on high for 15 minutes. Place rolled dough on hot pan, broil 1–2 minutes per side until blistered, brushing with garlic butter after first flip.
Immediately brush hot naan with reserved garlic butter, sprinkle with 2 tbsp chopped cilantro and black pepper to taste. Serve warm.
tip: For richer dough, replace 2 tbsp water with milk. Keep cooked naan wrapped in a towel; rewarm 5 minutes at 350°F or on a hot skillet. Add 1/4 tsp nigella seeds to dough for traditional aroma.

title: Skillet Cornbread
ing: 3 tbsp unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly
steps: Set oven to 450°F. Place a 10-inch cast-iron skillet on middle rack to preheat for 10 minutes.
In a bowl whisk cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt until evenly combined.
In another bowl whisk buttermilk and egg, then whisk in 3 tbsp melted butter until smooth.
Make a well in the dry ingredients and stir in the wet just until combined; do not overmix.
Carefully remove hot skillet, add 2 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp oil; swirl until the fats are shimmering and the skillet is well-coated.
Scrape batter into the hot skillet, smoothing the top; you should hear a sizzle around the edges.
Bake at 450°F until golden with crisp edges and a tester comes out clean, 15–18 minutes.
Cool in skillet 5 minutes, then slice into wedges and serve warm.
tip: For a purist, omit sugar. Substitute 1 cup whole-milk yogurt thinned with 2 tbsp milk for buttermilk. Leftovers keep 1 day at room temp, wrapped; rewarm in a 350°F oven for 8 minutes.

title: Classic Coleslaw
steps: In a large bowl, combine 4 cups green cabbage, 1 cup red cabbage, and 1 cup grated carrots.
In a separate bowl, whisk 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 2 tbsp apple cider vinegar, 1 tbsp Dijon, 1 tbsp sugar, 1/4 tsp celery seed, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp pepper until smooth.
Pour the dressing over the cabbage mixture and toss with tongs until every strand is lightly coated.
Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours) to allow flavors to meld and the cabbage to soften slightly.
Toss again before serving, taste, and adjust salt and pepper to taste.
tip: For a lighter slaw, swap half the mayonnaise with plain yogurt. Coleslaw keeps refrigerated, covered, for up to 2 days; toss and refresh with a splash of vinegar if needed.

title: Creamed Spinach
steps: Rinse spinach well. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil, add spinach, and blanch for 45 to 60 seconds until just wilted. Drain and immediately rinse under cold water to stop cooking.
Squeeze out as much water as possible. Chop the spinach into small pieces and set aside on a plate lined with paper towels.
Heat 1 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp frying oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until translucent. Stir in garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Sprinkle in flour and cook, stirring, for 1 minute to form a blond roux. Whisk in milk gradually, then add cream. Simmer gently for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until thick and smooth.
Stir in chopped spinach and remaining 1 tbsp butter. Cook over medium-low, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes until heated through and well coated.
Season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 1 minute, taste and adjust seasoning, then serve hot.
tip: Sub frozen spinach: use 1 lb, thawed and very well squeezed dry. Make-ahead: cool, cover, and refrigerate up to 2 days; rewarm gently with a splash of milk if too thick.

title: Hasselback Potatoes
ing: 1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Heat oven to 425°F with a rack in the center.
Set each potato between two chopsticks; slice crosswise every 1/8 inch, stopping 1/4 inch from the base so the slices stay attached.
Stir melted butter, olive oil, garlic, salt, and pepper. Brush generously over and between potato slices, reserving half for basting.
Set potatoes cut-side up on a foil-lined sheet. Bake at 425°F for 30 minutes until slices begin to fan.
Baste with more butter-oil mixture, gently easing it between slices. Bake 20 minutes more.
Baste again; bake 10–15 minutes until edges are deeply crisp and centers are tender when pierced (205°F internal for doneness).
Transfer to a warm platter. Spoon any pan butter over the tops and rest 3 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and serve immediately.
tip: Swap russets with Yukon Golds for a creamier interior. To make ahead, slice and rinse, then dry well; brush with fat just before roasting to keep edges crisp.

title: Rosemary Focaccia
ing: 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for pan
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for topping
1 tsp olive oil, as needed, for greasing
steps: Whisk 2 1/4 cups bread flour, 1 tsp instant yeast, and 1 tsp fine sea salt in a bowl. In a cup, mix 3/4 cup warm water with 1 tsp honey and 2 tbsp olive oil.
Stir wet into dry until a shaggy dough forms, then knead on a lightly oiled surface for 7-8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Dough should be soft and slightly tacky.
Lightly oil a bowl with 1 tsp olive oil. Place dough inside, cover, and let rise in a warm spot until doubled, about 60-75 minutes at 75°F-80°F.
Oil an 8x8-inch pan with 1 tbsp olive oil. Gently deflate dough, stretch to fit the pan, cover, and rest 15 minutes. Heat oven to 425°F with a rack in the center.
With oiled fingertips, dimple the dough deeply. Drizzle 2 tbsp olive oil over the surface, sprinkle 1 tbsp chopped rosemary and 1/2 tsp flaky sea salt evenly.
Bake at 425°F for 18-22 minutes until golden and an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 200-205°F.
Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack and cool 15 minutes before slicing and serving warm.
tip: Swap: add 1 tbsp pitted olives with rosemary. To store, wrap airtight at room temp up to 2 days; rewarm at 350°F for 8 minutes to refresh crust.

title: Refried Beans
ing: 1 lb dried pinto beans, picked over and rinsed
2 tbsp queso fresco, crumbled, for garnish
steps: Combine pinto beans, water, onion, and garlic in a pot; bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered until tender, 60 to 75 minutes.
Stir in salt during the last 10 minutes of simmering; remove and discard onion. Reserve 1 1/2 cups cooking liquid and drain the rest.
Heat lard in a wide skillet over medium heat until shimmering, 2 minutes. Add cumin and pepper; cook 30 seconds to bloom spices.
Add cooked beans and 1 cup reserved liquid; mash with a potato masher to a coarse puree. Simmer, stirring, until thick but still creamy, 8 to 12 minutes.
Adjust consistency with remaining bean broth 1 to 2 tbsp at a time; season with additional salt if needed. For extra richness, swirl in a little frying oil, as needed.
Serve hot, topped with queso fresco and cilantro. Hold warm over low heat, stirring occasionally, for up to 20 minutes.
tip: Swap lard with 3 tbsp neutral oil for vegetarian. Beans keep 5 days refrigerated or 2 months frozen; thin with a splash of water when reheating.

title: Potatoes Dauphinoise
steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Rub a 2-quart gratin dish with the cut sides of the garlic clove, then butter the dish evenly.
In a saucepan, combine heavy cream, whole milk, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Add the garlic halves and warm over medium heat until steaming, 3 to 4 minutes; do not boil. Discard garlic.
Slice potatoes 1/8-inch thick using a mandoline or knife. Add slices to the warm cream mixture and simmer gently over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring to separate, until just flexible.
Layer potatoes and cream into the prepared dish, smoothing into an even thickness with minimal gaps. Pour over remaining cream to just cover the top layer.
Sprinkle Gruyère evenly over the surface. Cover the dish loosely with foil, avoiding contact with the cheese.
Bake covered at 375°F for 35 minutes, then uncover and continue baking until the top is deeply golden and potatoes are tender when pierced, 20 to 25 minutes.
Rest the gratin for 10 minutes to set, then serve in squares, spooning some of the infused cream over each portion.
tip: For a stricter traditional take, omit the Gruyère. Can be assembled up to 4 hours ahead; keep chilled and add 5–10 minutes to the covered bake time.

title: Kimchi
ing: 6 oz Korean radish, cut into thin matchsticks
2 tbsp sweet rice flour (glutinous rice flour)
steps: Dissolve 1/4 cup kosher salt in 2 cups water. Loosen cabbage layers, then pour brine between leaves. Place in a nonreactive bowl, weigh down, and soak 2 hours, turning every 30 minutes.
Rinse cabbage under cold water 3 times to remove excess salt. Drain cut-side down in a colander for 30 minutes until leaves are pliable but crisp.
Make porridge: whisk 2 tbsp sweet rice flour with 1/2 cup water in a small pot. Cook over medium, stirring, until thick and translucent, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp sugar; cool 10 minutes.
In a bowl, combine cooled porridge, 6 cloves garlic, 1 tbsp ginger, 3 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp salted shrimp, and 1/3 cup gochugaru to form a paste. Fold in radish matchsticks and scallions.
Wearing gloves, spread paste between every cabbage leaf, distributing radish and scallion evenly. Press cabbage quarters into a tight bundle to expel air.
Pack bundles into a clean 1-quart jar or container, pressing down so brine rises to cover. Leave 1 inch headspace; wipe rims and seal loosely to vent.
Ferment at cool room temperature (65–72°F) until pleasantly tangy, 24 to 48 hours. Press daily to keep submerged and taste for acidity you like.
Refrigerate sealed to slow fermentation. Rest at least 2 days before serving for best flavor; keeps refrigerated 3 to 4 weeks. Serve chilled, cut into bite-size pieces.
tip: For vegetarian, replace fish sauce and salted shrimp with 3 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp kelp powder. If brine doesn’t rise to cover, add 1/4 cup cooled boiled salted water (1/2 tsp salt).

title: Tostones
ing: 1 lime, cut into wedges, for garnish
steps: Peel plantains: cut tips off, score lengthwise through peel, pry off skin. Slice into 1-inch thick rounds.
Stir water, vinegar, salt, garlic powder, and black pepper in a bowl to make a quick seasoning dip; set nearby.
Heat 1/2 inch frying oil in a heavy skillet over medium to 350°F. Fry plantain rounds in batches 3–4 minutes per side until pale yellow and just tender; drain on paper towels.
Working while warm, press each round to 1/4-inch thick using a tostonera or between two plates lined with parchment.
Briefly dip each flattened piece in the seasoning water; pat off excess moisture so they don’t splatter.
Reheat oil to 350°F. Fry the flattened plantains again 1–2 minutes per side until crisp and golden; drain and lightly salt while hot.
Serve immediately with lime wedges; enjoy while hot and crisp.
tip: For dipping, serve with mojo or garlic mayo. Keep warm on a rack in a 250°F oven up to 20 minutes; they soften as they sit, so fry close to serving.

title: Green Beans Almondine
ing: 1/4 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/8 tsp black pepper, or to taste
steps: Bring 2 quarts water with 2 tsp kosher salt to a boil over high heat. Add green beans and blanch for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp-tender and bright green.
Drain beans and immediately plunge into an ice bath for 2 minutes to stop cooking. Drain well and pat dry to prevent sputtering later.
Set a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 tbsp frying oil and 3 tbsp butter. When butter foams, add sliced almonds and cook, stirring, until lightly golden, 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in minced shallot and cook 30 to 60 seconds until fragrant; do not brown the shallot.
Add dried green beans to the skillet. Toss to coat and warm through over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes.
Season with 1/4 tsp kosher salt and 1/8 tsp black pepper. Add lemon juice and lemon zest, tossing 15 to 20 seconds to gloss the beans.
Taste and adjust seasoning to taste. Serve immediately, spooning almonds and pan butter over the top.
tip: Swap shallot with 1 tsp minced garlic for a bolder note. Blanched beans can be refrigerated up to 24 hours; pat dry before reheating to keep the almonds crisp.

title: Sweet Potato Fries
ing: 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley, for garnish, as needed
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Place two rimmed sheet pans inside to preheat for 10 minutes.
Cut sweet potatoes into 1/4-inch-thick sticks, 3 to 4 inches long, keeping sizes even for uniform cooking.
Toss fries with cornstarch until lightly coated; shake off excess. Drizzle with oil, then season with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, and garlic powder; toss to coat.
Carefully remove hot pans, line with parchment, and spread fries in a single, spaced layer; do not crowd.
Bake at 425°F for 15 minutes on the upper and lower racks. Rotate pans and flip fries; bake 10 to 12 minutes more until edges are deeply browned and crisp.
Turn off oven, crack door, and let fries rest on pans for 3 minutes to set their crust.
Transfer to a bowl, taste and adjust salt, and sprinkle with parsley. Serve hot.
tip: For extra crispness, soak cut fries in cold water 30 minutes, then dry very well before tossing with cornstarch. Leftovers re-crisp best in a 425°F oven for 5 to 7 minutes.

title: Pepperoni Pizza
steps: In a bowl, stir 2 1/4 tsp yeast and 1 tsp sugar into 1 1/4 cups warm water (110°F). Let stand until foamy, 5–8 minutes.
Combine 3 cups flour and 1 1/2 tsp salt. Add yeast mixture and 1 tbsp olive oil; mix, then knead until smooth and elastic, 6–8 minutes. Cover and let rise until doubled, 45–60 minutes.
Place a rack in the lower third and preheat oven to 500°F (or as high as it goes). If using a stone, preheat it 30 minutes.
Punch down dough and shape into a tight ball. On a lightly floured surface, roll or stretch to a 12-inch round for a thicker crust or 13-inch for thinner.
Transfer dough to a lightly oiled 12–13 inch pizza pan or floured peel. Brush rim with 1 tbsp olive oil. Spread 1 cup pizza sauce thinly, leaving a 1-inch border.
Top evenly with 8 oz shredded mozzarella and 5 oz pepperoni. Sprinkle 2 tbsp Parmesan, 1 tsp oregano, 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes, and 1/2 tsp black pepper.
Bake at 500°F on the lower rack (or on the stone) until the crust is deeply golden and cheese bubbles with browned spots, 10–14 minutes.
Rest 2 minutes, garnish with 1 tbsp chopped basil, slice into 8 pieces, and serve hot.
tip: Sub 50% bread flour for extra chew. Parbake the crust 4 minutes for crisper bottoms, or refrigerate dough up to 24 hours for better flavor; bring to room temp before shaping.

title: Calzone
ing: 1 cup canned San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
steps: Heat oven to 475°F with a preheated sheet or stone inside; allow 30 minutes for the stone to fully heat.
Stir tomatoes with olive oil, oregano, garlic, red pepper flakes, and 1/4 tsp salt; set aside. In a bowl mix mozzarella, ricotta, Pecorino, and black pepper until evenly combined.
Divide dough into 4 equal pieces. On a lightly floured surface, roll each into an 8-inch round, about 1/8 inch thick.
Spread 2 tbsp tomato mixture on half of each round, leaving a 3/4-inch border. Top with one quarter of the cheese mix and prosciutto, keeping edges clean.
Fold dough over filling to form a half-moon. Press edges to seal, then crimp firmly. Poke a small steam vent on top with a knife tip.
Brush tops lightly with frying oil. Transfer calzoni to the hot stone or sheet and bake at 475°F for 14–16 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.
If bottoms brown too fast, move to a higher rack and continue 2–3 minutes more. Let rest 5 minutes to allow cheese to set before serving.
Serve hot with remaining tomato sauce on the side for dipping.
tip: Sub prosciutto cotto with salame or sautéed mushrooms for a meatless option. Drain ricotta in a sieve 30 minutes to avoid soggy filling; leftovers reheat well at 375°F for 8–10 minutes.

title: Okonomiyaki
ing: 4 oz pork belly slices, cut into 2-inch pieces
2 tbsp beni shoga (red pickled ginger), chopped
steps: Whisk flour with dashi until smooth, then mix in grated nagaimo and soy sauce. Rest the batter for 10 minutes to hydrate.
In a large bowl combine cabbage, beni shoga, tenkasu, and eggs. Pour in the rested batter and gently fold until cabbage is evenly coated.
Heat a 10-inch nonstick or well-seasoned skillet over medium with 1 tsp oil. Spoon in one-quarter of the batter, shaping a 7–8 inch round about 3/4 inch thick.
Arrange one-quarter of the pork belly on top in a single layer. Cook uncovered until edges set and bottom is golden, about 4–5 minutes.
Slide a spatula under the pancake, add 1 tsp oil, flip carefully so pork faces down, and cook until pork is browned and the center is set, 5–6 minutes.
Cover the pan for the last 2 minutes to steam through; internal center should be hot and set with no raw egg visible. Transfer to a plate pork-side up.
Brush top with okonomiyaki sauce, drizzle with mayonnaise, and sprinkle with aonori and katsuobushi. Repeat with remaining batter to make 4 pancakes.
Garnish with scallions and serve immediately while hot and fluffy.
tip: Nagaimo yields the classic fluffy texture; if unavailable, add 2–3 tbsp water to loosen and mix gently. Cooked pancakes keep 2 days refrigerated; reheat in a lightly oiled skillet to crisp.

title: Egg Fried Rice
ing: 3 cups cooked jasmine rice, chilled overnight
1 cup frozen peas and carrots, thawed and drained
steps: Break up 3 cups chilled rice with fingers to separate grains. Beat 4 eggs with a pinch of salt until homogenous.
Heat a wok over high heat until lightly smoking, 2 minutes. Add 1 tbsp frying oil and swirl. Pour in eggs; scramble in large curds just set, 30–45 seconds. Transfer to a plate.
Add 2 tbsp frying oil to the hot wok. Add peas and carrots; stir-fry over high heat until heated through and lightly blistered, 1–2 minutes.
Add rice. Stir-fry vigorously, pressing and tossing to separate grains, until steamy and a few grains lightly toasted, 3–4 minutes.
Drizzle in 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine around the wok’s edge to deglaze; toss. Add 2 tbsp soy sauce in a thin stream, stirring so it coats rice without pooling, 30 seconds.
Return eggs to wok, breaking into bite-size pieces. Add 1/2 cup scallions, 1 tsp sesame oil, and 1/2 tsp white pepper; toss to combine, 30–60 seconds.
Taste and season with 1/2 tsp kosher salt, to taste. Stir-fry 15 seconds more to integrate flavors, then remove from heat and serve immediately.
tip: Best with day-old, dry rice; spread fresh-cooked rice on a tray and chill 2 hours if needed. Add diced ham or shrimp (pre-cooked) for variation; swap Shaoxing with dry sherry if unavailable.

title: Tortilla Española
ing: 1 lb waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
steps: Warm 1 cup olive oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-low until shimmering, 2 minutes.
Add potatoes and onion, season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/8 tsp pepper, and gently poach, stirring occasionally, until tender but not browned, 18 to 22 minutes.
Drain potatoes and onion through a sieve set over a bowl to reserve the oil. Cool 5 minutes; wipe out the skillet.
Beat 6 large eggs in a large bowl until homogenous, 15 seconds. Fold in the warm potatoes and onion; let stand 5 minutes to hydrate.
Heat 1 tbsp reserved oil in the skillet over medium. Pour in the mixture, level the surface, and cook until the edges set and the center is lightly thickened, 4 to 5 minutes.
Loosen edges with a spatula. Invert onto a flat plate, then slide back into the skillet to cook the second side until just set in the center, 3 to 4 minutes.
Slide tortilla onto a clean plate, brush top with 1 tbsp olive oil, and rest 5 to 10 minutes for flavors to settle. Slice into wedges.
Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with parsley if desired.
tip: Use a waxy potato like Yukon Gold for shape. Reserve leftover oil for another use; it’s infused with flavor. Keeps, wrapped, at room temp 6 hours or refrigerated 2 days; bring to room temp before serving.

title: Croque Monsieur
ing: 1 tbsp unsalted butter, softened, for bread
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Warm milk in a small saucepan over low heat until steaming, 3 to 4 minutes; keep warm.
Make béchamel: melt 2 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in warm milk; simmer, whisking, until thick, 3 to 4 minutes.
Season béchamel with Dijon, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Off heat, stir in 1 oz grated Gruyère until smooth; reserve.
Lightly butter one side of each bread slice with softened butter. Place 4 slices, buttered side down, on a sheet pan.
Spread about 1 1/2 tbsp béchamel on each base slice. Top evenly with ham, then 3 oz grated Gruyère total. Cover with remaining bread, buttered side up.
Warm a large skillet with a thin film of oil over medium heat. Sear sandwiches until golden, 2 to 3 minutes per side; return to sheet pan.
Top each sandwich with 2 to 3 tbsp béchamel, then sprinkle remaining Gruyère over the tops.
Bake at 425°F until cheese is melted and bubbling and centers are heated through, 8 to 10 minutes. Rest 2 minutes, then serve hot.
tip: Use Comté instead of Gruyère if preferred. Bread can be toasted lightly before assembling for extra crispness; assembled sandwiches hold chilled, covered, up to 8 hours before baking.

title: Ultimate Grilled Cheese
ing: 2 tbsp salted butter, for skillet, as needed
steps: Spread 1/2 tbsp softened butter on one side of each bread slice. Spread 1 tsp mayonnaise on the opposite side of each slice.
Toss shredded cheddar and Gruyère with black pepper to taste. Lay out 4 bread slices, mayo side down.
Top each with 1 oz American cheese and 1/2 cup mixed shredded cheese. Cap with remaining bread, mayo side up.
Heat 1/2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat until melted and foamy, about 1 minute.
Add 2 sandwiches; cook until deep golden and cheese begins to melt, 3–4 minutes. Press gently with a spatula.
Flip; add a little more butter if dry. Cook until the second side is deep golden and cheese is fully melted, 3–4 minutes.
Transfer to a wire rack 2 minutes to rest. Repeat with remaining sandwiches, adjusting heat to prevent scorching.
Slice sandwiches diagonally and serve hot while the cheese is stretchy and glossy.
tip: Use thick-cut sourdough or brioche for variation. Keep finished sandwiches warm on a sheet pan in a 200°F oven up to 15 minutes without losing crispness.

title: Flammkuchen
ing: 8 oz slab bacon, cut into 1/4-inch lardons
1 tbsp chives, finely sliced, for garnish
steps: Heat oven with a baking steel or upside-down sheet to 500°F for 30 minutes; if using a pizza stone, heat it for the same time.
Whisk flour and salt in a bowl. Add lukewarm water and olive oil; mix, then knead 3 to 4 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest 10 minutes.
Stir fromage blanc, crème fraîche, nutmeg, and black pepper until smooth and spreadable.
In a skillet over medium heat, warm 1 tbsp frying oil. Cook bacon lardons 4 to 5 minutes just to render lightly; do not crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Toss sliced onions with a pinch of salt; let stand 5 minutes, then blot excess moisture so they won’t weep on the dough.
Divide dough into 2 balls. On a lightly floured sheet of parchment, roll each to a very thin rectangle or oval about 12x8 inches.
Spread half the cream mixture thinly over one rolled base, leaving a 1/2-inch border. Scatter half the onions and half the lardons evenly.
Slide parchment with topped dough onto the hot steel/stone and bake at 500°F for 8 to 10 minutes until blistered and browned at edges.
Repeat with second tart. Cut into squares, garnish with chives, and serve immediately while crisp.
tip: For closest texture, roll the dough paper-thin. Substitute quark for fromage blanc if needed. Parbaked bases keep 1 day, wrapped; top and bake just before serving.

title: Pierogi
ing: 1 lb russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
steps: Make dough: In a bowl whisk 1/2 cup warm water, 1/3 cup sour cream, and 1 large egg. In another bowl mix 2 cups flour with 1/2 tsp salt. Stir wet into dry, knead 5–7 minutes until smooth. Rest, covered, 30 minutes.
Make filling: Boil 1 lb potatoes in salted water until tender, 12–15 minutes; drain well and steam off moisture 2 minutes. Mash until smooth and cool 10 minutes.
While potatoes cook, melt 2 tbsp butter in a skillet over medium and sauté 1 cup diced onion until golden, 8–10 minutes. Reserve 2 tbsp for topping; add the rest to potatoes.
Finish filling: Stir in 8 oz farmer cheese, 1 tsp kosher salt, and 1/2 tsp pepper. Mix until cohesive; adjust seasoning. Chill 10 minutes for easier shaping.
Roll dough: On a lightly floured surface, roll half the dough to 1/16–1/8 inch. Cut 3-inch rounds. Keep covered to prevent drying.
Fill and seal: Place 1 tbsp filling in each round. Fold to a half-moon, press out air, and seal edges firmly. Crimp well to prevent leaks. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.

Boil: Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Add pierogi in batches, stir, and cook until they float plus 1–2 minutes, about 3–4 minutes total. Transfer to a tray lightly brushed with oil.

Pan-fry and serve: Heat 3 tbsp frying oil in a skillet over medium. Fry boiled pierogi in batches until lightly crisp and golden, 2–3 minutes per side. Toss with 2 tbsp butter and reserved onions. Garnish with chives.
tip: Farmer cheese can be swapped with dry curd cottage cheese or well-drained ricotta. Boiled (unfried) pierogi freeze well: freeze on a sheet, then bag up to 2 months; pan-fry from frozen.

title: Khachapuri
steps: In a bowl, whisk warm water, yeast, and sugar; rest for 5 minutes until foamy. Add flour, salt, and olive oil; mix, then knead 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and rise in a warm spot for 60 minutes until doubled.
Combine sulguni, imeruli, and mozzarella in a bowl. Keep chilled. Line 2 sheet pans with parchment and lightly oil. Heat oven to 475°F with a rack in the lower third.
Punch down dough and divide into 4 equal pieces. Rest 10 minutes. On a lightly floured surface, roll each into an oval about 9x6 inches, 1/4-inch thick.

Sprinkle one-quarter of the cheese mixture down the center of each oval, leaving a 1-inch border. Roll the long edges inward toward the center to encase some cheese, then pinch tips to form a tight boat.
Transfer boats to prepared pans. Bake at 475°F for 8–10 minutes until dough is just set and lightly golden and cheese is melting.
Remove pans. Using a spoon, press a shallow well in the center cheese of each boat. Crack 1 egg into each well and dot each with 1 tbsp cold butter.
Return to oven and bake at 475°F for 3–5 minutes until whites are just set and yolks still runny; bake 1–2 minutes longer if firmer yolks are desired.
Serve immediately. To eat, tear off crust and swirl it into the hot cheese, butter, and egg until creamy; season with salt and pepper to taste.
tip: Cheese swap: combine mozzarella with feta and a mild provolone if sulguni/imeruli are unavailable. Reheat at 350°F for 8–10 minutes; add a fresh egg only when serving, not for reheating.

title: Lahmacun
ing: 1/2 medium onion, finely grated, excess juice squeezed
1/2 green bell pepper, very finely chopped
1 cup flat-leaf parsley, loosely packed, for garnish
steps: In a bowl whisk 2 cups flour, 1 tsp instant yeast, and 3/4 tsp salt. Add 3/4 cup warm water and 1 tbsp olive oil; mix, then knead 5–7 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest until slightly puffy, 30–40 minutes.

Meanwhile combine 10 oz ground lamb, grated tomato, grated onion (well-squeezed), bell pepper, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 2 tbsp chopped parsley, Aleppo pepper, cumin, paprika, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Mix until a cohesive paste forms.
Set oven to 500°F with a baking steel or inverted sheet on middle rack; preheat 20 minutes. Lightly flour a surface and divide dough into 4 balls; keep covered to prevent drying.
Working with one ball, roll extremely thin to a 9–10 inch round/oval. Lift to parchment. Spread a thin, even layer (about 1/4 cup) of lamb mixture to the edge. Repeat with remaining dough.
Slide 1–2 lahmacun on the hot steel. Bake at 500°F until edges blister and topping is cooked through, 6–8 minutes. Rotate once for even browning. Internal topping should reach 160°F for lamb.
Stack baked lahmacun under a clean towel to keep pliable while you finish baking the rest.
To serve, squeeze lemon over each, top with a handful of parsley, and roll or fold to eat while hot.
Optional: For stovetop, heat a heavy skillet over medium-high 3 minutes; cook rolled dough 1 minute, flip, spread topping thinly, cover, and cook until set and spotty, 4–5 minutes.
tip: Sub lamb with 10 oz ground beef if preferred. Refrigerate topping up to 24 hours; drain any liquid before spreading. For extra heat, add more Aleppo pepper.

title: Pupusas
ing: 6 oz queso quesillo or low-moisture mozzarella, shredded
1/2 cup cooked refried red beans, cooled
1/2 cup finely chopped chicharrón (Salvadoran-style pork rind paste) or 1/2 cup sautéed minced pork
1 tsp neutral frying oil, as needed
steps: Make curtido: Toss cabbage, carrot, and onion with 1/2 tsp kosher salt. Let wilt 10 minutes, then add 1/2 cup white vinegar, 1/4 cup warm water, and 1/2 tsp oregano. Chill at least 30 minutes.

Make salsa roja: Simmer 1 cup tomato sauce with 1 clove minced garlic, 1/4 tsp black pepper, and a pinch of salt over low heat for 10 minutes; thin with 2–3 tbsp water to a pourable consistency. Keep warm.
Mix dough: In a bowl combine 2 cups masa harina and 1/2 tsp fine sea salt. Add 1 3/4 cups warm water gradually, mixing until soft, pliable, and not sticky. Rest dough covered for 10 minutes.
Prepare fillings: In separate small bowls place shredded cheese, refried beans, and chicharrón or sautéed minced pork. Cool fillings to room temp so they don’t break the dough.
Portion: Lightly oil hands as needed. Divide dough into 8 equal balls (about 3 oz each). Keep covered with a damp towel to prevent drying.

Form pupusas: Flatten a ball into a 4-inch disk. Cup it and create a well; add about 1 tbsp cheese plus 1 tbsp beans or pork (or cheese alone). Pinch edges to seal, then gently pat into a 5–5 1/2 inch disk.

Cook: Heat a nonstick or cast-iron griddle over medium to medium-high until a drop of water skitters. Lightly oil surface. Cook pupusas 3–4 minutes per side until golden spots appear and cheese begins to ooze.
Serve: Rest 1 minute. Serve hot with curtido and warm salsa roja spooned over or alongside.
tip: Swap: Use all-cheese for vegetarian pupusas. Make-ahead: Curtido improves after a day in the fridge; keep liquid to just cover and chill up to 1 week.

title: Arepas con Queso
ing: 6 oz queso de mano or fresh mozzarella, sliced
steps: In a bowl whisk warm water with salt, then sprinkle in precooked cornmeal while stirring. Add 1 tbsp softened butter and mix until smooth. Let hydrate for 5 minutes.
Knead the dough 30–60 seconds until pliable and crack-free. If dry, add 1–2 tsp water; if sticky, dust with a little cornmeal.
Divide into 8 equal portions. Roll each into a ball, then pat into disks 3 1/2 inches wide and 1/2 inch thick with smooth edges.
Heat a large cast-iron or nonstick skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes. Lightly film with frying oil. Cook arepas 6–7 minutes per side until golden with a dry crust.
Transfer to a 375°F oven and bake 8–10 minutes until they sound hollow when tapped and are cooked through.
Split each arepa halfway around the edge to make a pocket. Add sliced queso de mano and a spoon of grated queso blanco to each.
Return stuffed arepas to the skillet over medium-low heat, cover, and warm 2–3 minutes until cheese is melted.
Brush cut faces with 1 tbsp butter, season with a pinch of black pepper, and serve hot.
tip: Swap queso de mano with Oaxaca or low-moisture mozzarella plus queso fresco. Keep cooked arepas (unstuffed) in an airtight bag up to 2 days; reheat in a 350°F oven 6–8 minutes to refresh.

title: Stuffed Cabbage Rolls
steps: Core the cabbage and submerge in a large pot of boiling water over medium-high heat; simmer 8–10 minutes, peeling off leaves as they soften. Drain leaves and trim thick ribs flat with a paring knife.
In a bowl, combine beef, pork, cooked rice, onion, garlic, dill, parsley, paprika, salt, pepper, and egg. Mix gently until evenly combined without overworking.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook tomato paste 1 minute, add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, and sugar; simmer for 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Lay a cabbage leaf rib-side down. Place 1/4 cup filling near the stem end, fold sides in, and roll tightly. Repeat to make about 12 rolls.
Spread 1/2 cup sauce on the bottom of a heavy pot or Dutch oven. Nestle rolls seam-side down in a snug single layer; top with remaining sauce, adding extra torn leaves if any.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then cover and cook at a bare simmer for 60–70 minutes until cabbage is tender and an instant-read thermometer in the center of a roll reads 160°F.
Let rest 10 minutes. Spoon sauce over rolls and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with a little chopped dill or parsley if desired.
tip: Make ahead: Assemble up to 24 hours in advance and refrigerate; cook an extra 10 minutes. Swap: Use all beef and add 1 tsp dried marjoram for a Polish-style touch.

title: Burrito Bowl
ing: 15 oz black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Combine 2 cups water and 1 tsp salt in a saucepan; add 1 cup rinsed rice. Bring to a boil, reduce to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Rest off heat, covered, 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
In a bowl, toss 1 lb sliced skirt steak with 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chili powder, and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high. Add 1 tbsp frying oil. Sear steak in a single layer until browned and just cooked through, 4–6 minutes total; remove to a plate and tent to keep warm.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add 1/2 cup diced onion and cook 2 minutes. Stir in 2 cloves minced garlic; cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add 15 oz rinsed black beans and 1 cup corn to the skillet with 2 tbsp water; simmer for 3–4 minutes until heated through. Stir in 1 tbsp lime juice; adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Prepare toppings: 1 cup pico de gallo, 1 cup shredded Monterey Jack, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1/2 cup guacamole, and 1/4 cup chopped cilantro.
Assemble bowls: divide rice among 4 bowls, top with beans and corn, then steak and any juices. Add pico de gallo, cheese, sour cream, guacamole, and cilantro.
Serve immediately while warm; offer extra lime wedges if desired.
tip: Swap steak with 1 lb chicken thighs cooked to 165°F or 12 oz portobellos for vegetarian. Rice and beans can be made 2 days ahead; reheat with a splash of water.
